title: Arbitrary-Distance Quantum Error Correction with Gauss's Law for $\mathbb Z_2$ Lattice Gauge Theory
summary: It has previously been shown by Rajput, Roggero, and Wiebe that $\mathbb Z_2$ Gauss's law constraints can be used to build efficient quantum error-correcting codes (QECCs) that are robust against arbitrary single-qubit errors. In this work, we generalize the construction to be robust against arbitrary $t$-qubit errors, where $t$ is any positive integer. This includes a derivation of the optimal Gauss's law code within the considered family by minimizing the number of physical qubits required for a given code distance. Finally, we compare our codes against other efficient QECCs on metrics such as the number of physical qubits, the locality of the encoded Hamiltonian, and the logical error rate in the code capacity setting. Compared to using a domain-agnostic code for every lattice degree of freedom, we find that the Gauss's law code primarily excels at reducing the locality of the encoded Hamiltonian. Moreover, the physical qubit overhead is also reduced for $t \le 3$ (distance $d \le 7$).

AI.tldr: This paper generalizes Z₂ Gauss's law–based quantum error-correcting codes to correct arbitrary t-qubit errors, derives the optimal code minimizing physical qubits for a given distance, and shows advantages in Hamiltonian locality and—when t ≤ 3—physical qubit overhead over domain-agnostic codes.
AI.motivation: To extend robustness of Z₂ Gauss's law–based QECCs beyond single-qubit errors to arbitrary t-qubit errors while optimizing resource efficiency and preserving favorable properties like local encoded Hamiltonians.
AI.method: Generalizes prior Z₂ Gauss's law constraint-based QECC construction to support arbitrary t-qubit error correction; derives optimal code parameters by minimizing physical qubit count for target code distance; benchmarks against other efficient QECCs using metrics including physical qubit count, encoded Hamiltonian locality, and logical error rate in code capacity setting.
AI.result: Achieves t-qubit error correction capability; identifies optimal Gauss's law code within the family; demonstrates superior Hamiltonian locality versus domain-agnostic codes; achieves lower physical qubit overhead for t ≤ 3 (i.e., distance d ≤ 7).
AI.conclusion: Z₂ Gauss's law–based codes provide a structured, physically motivated path to scalable, locality-preserving QECCs with competitive or superior resource efficiency for moderate error-correction requirements.

title: Parton distribution functions from lattice QCD
comment: Invited chapter to the Encyclopedia of Nuclear Physics (Elsevier), 21 pages
summary:
Parton distribution functions (PDFs) provide one of the most direct ways to describe the partonic structure of hadrons in QCD. They encode nonperturbative information about quarks, antiquarks, and gluons as functions of the partonic momentum fraction $x$, and they connect this microscopic structure to experimentally measurable high-energy scattering processes through QCD factorization. This makes PDFs interesting to pursue with lattice QCD, which provides a first-principles formulation of the strong interaction. The challenge is that PDFs are defined through light-cone correlations, while lattice QCD is formulated in Euclidean spacetime.
  This chapter introduces the theoretical foundations and current status of lattice-QCD calculations of PDFs, with emphasis on modern approaches based on spatially nonlocal matrix elements. We first review the light-cone definitions of quark and gluon PDFs, their Mellin moments, and the connection to QCD factorization. We then explain how large-momentum effective theory, short-distance factorization, and the short-distance operator product expansion make it possible to relate Euclidean lattice observables to light-cone partonic structure. Particular attention is given to the elements that have improved over the last five years: renormalization of Wilson-line operators, perturbative matching, finite-momentum and finite-distance effects, reconstruction of the $x$ dependence, and systematic uncertainties.
  We summarize selected lattice results for proton quark PDFs, pion and kaon PDFs, gluon PDFs, and twist-3 distributions, highlighting both recent progress and remaining challenges. As will be demonstrated, lattice QCD is moving from proof-of-principle calculations toward systematically improvable determinations that can complement experimental data and global QCD analyses in mapping the partonic structure of hadrons.

AI.tldr: This chapter reviews theoretical foundations and recent advances in lattice-QCD calculations of parton distribution functions (PDFs), focusing on spatially nonlocal matrix elements and modern frameworks—such as large-momentum effective theory and short-distance factorization—that bridge Euclidean lattice observables with light-cone PDFs. It highlights progress in renormalization, matching, finite-momentum effects, x-dependence reconstruction, and systematic uncertainties, and summarizes state-of-the-art lattice results for quark, gluon, and twist-3 PDFs in protons, pions, and kaons.
AI.motivation: To overcome the fundamental challenge that PDFs are defined via light-cone correlations while lattice QCD operates in Euclidean spacetime, thereby enabling first-principles, ab initio computation of hadronic partonic structure.
AI.method: Uses spatially nonlocal matrix elements on the lattice, combined with large-momentum effective theory (LaMET), short-distance factorization, and short-distance operator product expansion (OPE) to relate Euclidean lattice observables to light-cone PDFs; includes improved renormalization of Wilson-line operators, perturbative matching, treatment of finite-momentum and finite-distance effects, and reconstruction techniques for x-dependent distributions.
AI.result: Demonstrates transition from proof-of-principle lattice PDF calculations to systematically improvable determinations; presents updated results for proton quark PDFs, pion/kaon PDFs, gluon PDFs, and twist-3 distributions, with quantified systematic uncertainties and improved control over key theoretical errors.
AI.conclusion: Lattice QCD is now a viable, complementary tool to experiment for mapping hadronic partonic structure, with recent methodological advances enabling quantitative, high-fidelity PDF extractions that can inform and constrain global QCD analyses.

title: Dynamics of nucleation in thermal phase transitions
summary: We study dynamical effects during nucleation in thermal first-order phase transitions in field theory. Focusing on the classical regime of the decay of a metastable state, we present the general formula for the thermal decay rate including the dynamical prefactor and give a recipe for its systematic evaluation. We describe the physical mechanism which reduces the actual thermal decay rate with respect to the statistical rate obtained in equilibrium theory. We also discuss the thermality conditions ensuring the existence of a steady-state thermal rate, in which case our formula is exact up to exponentially small corrections. We show that it reproduces the known results for the nucleation rate in stochastic mechanics and field theory, and allows us to unify and go beyond them. We illustrate this in real-time numerical simulations of simple field theory models. We observe significant non-perturbative contributions which can dominate the dynamical prefactor in weakly-coupled field theories at moderate exponential suppression of the decay rate. We explore the connection of these non-perturbative effects to oscillons. Notably, our numerical method requires exponentially less computing time than direct simulations of decays and is thus applicable to systems with arbitrarily strong exponential suppression. Finally, we discuss small or poorly thermalized systems when the thermality conditions are violated and the steady-state rate does not exist.

AI.tldr: This paper derives a general formula for the thermal decay rate in first-order phase transitions, including dynamical prefactors, clarifies the physical origin of rate suppression relative to equilibrium predictions, establishes thermality conditions for validity, unifies prior stochastic and field-theoretic results, validates numerically, reveals non-perturbative oscillon-related contributions dominating the prefactor in weakly-coupled theories, and extends analysis to non-thermal regimes.
AI.motivation: To resolve limitations of equilibrium-based nucleation theory by incorporating real-time dynamical effects—especially the dynamical prefactor—in thermal first-order phase transitions, and to understand how non-equilibrium dynamics modify decay rates beyond exponential suppression.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of the full thermal decay rate including dynamical prefactor in the classical regime; systematic evaluation recipe based on real-time field dynamics; numerical real-time simulations of simple scalar field theories; analysis of thermality conditions and breakdown thereof; connection to oscillon formation and non-perturbative resonance phenomena.
AI.result: A general exact (up to exponentially small corrections) formula for the thermal nucleation rate under steady-state thermality; demonstration that dynamical effects suppress the rate relative to statistical equilibrium estimates; identification of significant non-perturbative contributions to the prefactor—linked to long-lived oscillons—that dominate in weakly-coupled theories at moderate exponential suppression; development of an efficient numerical method exponentially faster than direct decay simulations.
AI.conclusion: Dynamical prefactors are essential and generically non-perturbative in thermal field-theoretic nucleation; oscillons play a key role in enhancing prefactors; the derived formalism unifies stochastic and field-theoretic approaches, enables accurate prediction of nucleation rates even under strong exponential suppression, and provides a framework for analyzing non-thermal or transient systems.

title: Misconceptions About the Physics of the QCD Trace Anomaly from Renormalization in a Reducible Basis
summary: The QCD trace anomaly is a well-established textbook result in quantum field theory with several prominent features: (1) it arises from the quantum breaking of scale symmetry at ultraviolet (UV) scales, yet is independent of the particular UV regulator used, whether lattice or dimensional regularization; (2) although it is nominally proportional to (${\cal O}(α_s)$), it is free of renormalization-scheme ambiguity; and (3) it is free of UV divergences and is therefore scale independent. Unfortunately, these important features have been undermined in the recently introduced reducible-basis renormalization, leading to misunderstandings of anomaly-related nucleon physics, including the origins of nucleon mass and internal forces.

AI.tldr: This paper critiques the reducible-basis renormalization scheme for violating fundamental properties of the QCD trace anomaly—namely its regulator independence, renormalization-scheme independence, and UV finiteness—and warns that such violations lead to misinterpretations in nucleon mass and force analyses.
AI.motivation: To clarify and defend the well-established, robust properties of the QCD trace anomaly against conceptual and technical errors introduced by the reducible-basis renormalization scheme, which incorrectly compromises its regulator independence, scheme independence, and scale invariance.
AI.method: Conceptual and theoretical analysis comparing standard renormalization frameworks (lattice, dimensional regularization) with the reducible-basis approach, focusing on how each treats the trace anomaly’s UV origin, scheme dependence, and divergence structure.
AI.result: Demonstrates that reducible-basis renormalization breaks key physical and mathematical features of the QCD trace anomaly—specifically introducing regulator dependence, renormalization-scheme ambiguity, and spurious scale dependence—thereby invalidating its use in interpreting nucleon structure.
AI.conclusion: The reducible-basis renormalization scheme is inconsistent with the fundamental quantum-field-theoretic understanding of the QCD trace anomaly; its application to nucleon physics leads to physically misleading conclusions about mass generation and internal forces.

title: Renormalizations in holomorphic field theories on Kähler manifolds
summary: The divergence of Feynman graph integrals is one of the central issues in the study of perturbative quantum field theories. A rigorous formulation of these integrals usually requires renormalization. In this paper, we prove that the Feynman graph integrals arising from holomorphic field theories on closed real-analytic Kähler manifolds are convergent with respect to heat-kernel renormalization, Cauchy principal value renormalization, and zeta-function renormalization. Moreover, these three renormalization procedures produce the same value. Our proof is based on the theory of wonderful compactifications in algebraic geometry, which provides a geometric understanding of these integrals. As a consequence, we establish a gauge anomaly formula for these graph integrals.

AI.tldr: This paper proves convergence and equivalence of three renormalization schemes—heat-kernel, Cauchy principal value, and zeta-function—for Feynman integrals in holomorphic field theories on closed real-analytic Kähler manifolds, using wonderful compactifications; it also derives a gauge anomaly formula.
AI.motivation: To resolve the divergence problem of Feynman graph integrals in perturbative quantum field theory by establishing rigorous convergence and consistency across standard renormalization methods in a geometric setting.
AI.method: Applies the theory of wonderful compactifications from algebraic geometry to provide a geometric framework for analyzing Feynman integrals; leverages properties of holomorphic field theories on closed real-analytic Kähler manifolds to prove convergence and equivalence under heat-kernel, Cauchy principal value, and zeta-function renormalization.
AI.result: Feynman graph integrals in the specified setting are convergent under all three renormalization schemes, and the resulting values coincide; a gauge anomaly formula is derived as a corollary.
AI.conclusion: The geometric structure encoded by wonderful compactifications ensures robustness and consistency of renormalization in holomorphic field theories on Kähler manifolds, unifying disparate renormalization approaches and enabling anomaly characterization.

title: Self-Forces as Nonlocal Probes of Gravastar Interiors
summary: Compact objects with the same exterior metric are locally indistinguishable to test particles, yet observables built from retarded fields can retain information about the spacetime outside the particle's immediate neighbourhood. The self-force acting on a particle in curved spacetime provides a unique probe of both the local geometry and the global structure of the background spacetime. We calculate the static, conservative self-force on minimally coupled scalar and electric charges in the simplest thin-shell gravastar: a de Sitter core matched to a Schwarzschild exterior. Weak-field expansions in the compactness $M/R$ are obtained analytically and summed in closed form. For a scalar charge outside the gravastar the self-force is nonzero---in contrast to the exactly vanishing result for a Schwarzschild black hole of the same mass---and behaves as $\tfrac{2}{5}q^2 M R^2/r_0^5$ at large distances, while for an electric charge the universal Smith--Will force $e^2M/r_0^3$ is corrected by a structure-dependent term $\tfrac{4}{5}e^2 M R^2/r_0^5$. Inside the gravastar the scalar self-force is directed toward the center at leading order in $M/R$, vanishes linearly at the center, and produces harmonic oscillations of the charge about the center; the electromagnetic self-force inside the gravastar behaves similarly. The results demonstrate explicitly that the self-force depends not only on the local curvature surrounding the particle but also on the global structure of spacetime: although the exterior geometry of a gravastar is identical to that of a Schwarzschild black hole, the interior boundary conditions modify the regular field and therefore produce distinct self-forces.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the static, conservative self-force on scalar and electric charges in a thin-shell gravastar (de Sitter core + Schwarzschild exterior), showing that the self-force—unlike in Schwarzschild black holes—is nonzero outside and structure-dependent, revealing sensitivity to global spacetime geometry beyond local curvature.
AI.motivation: To probe how the gravitational self-force encodes information about global spacetime structure—not just local curvature—by comparing self-forces in gravastars (which share the Schwarzschild exterior metric) versus Schwarzschild black holes.
AI.method: Analytic weak-field expansion in compactness $M/R$, matched asymptotics across the thin shell, mode-sum regularization of retarded fields, and closed-form summation of series for static self-force components for minimally coupled scalar and electromagnetic charges inside and outside the gravastar.
AI.result: Scalar charge outside experiences a $\sim q^2 M R^2 / r_0^5$ self-force (nonzero, unlike vanishing Schwarzschild case); electric charge exhibits Smith–Will term $e^2 M / r_0^3$ plus correction $\frac{4}{5} e^2 M R^2 / r_0^5$; inside, both forces are central, vanish linearly at origin, and induce harmonic oscillations.
AI.conclusion: The self-force is sensitive to global boundary conditions and interior structure—even when exterior geometry is identical—demonstrating its role as a unique probe of spacetime topology and matter content beyond local curvature.

title: Search for a top-philic Z' boson decaying into a $\mathrm{t\bar{t}}$ pair in a final state with jets and an electron or muon in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13.6 TeV
comment: Submitted to the Journal of High Energy Physics. All figures and tables can be found at http://cms-results.web.cern.ch/cms-results/public-results/publications/B2G-24-009 (CMS Public Pages)
summary: A search for a top-philic Z' boson in a final state with jets and an electron or muon is presented. The search is based on a sample of proton-proton collision data collected at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV by the CMS experiment at the CERN LHC during 2016$-$2018, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 138 fb$^{-1}$. The top-philic Z' boson is produced in association with a top-antitop quark pair ($\mathrm{t\bar{t}}$) and decays into a $\mathrm{t\bar{t}}$ pair, as it couples exclusively to top quarks. The analysis aims to identify a heavy Z' boson that produces Lorentz-boosted top quarks, whose hadronic decay products are merged into large-radius jets. A machine-learning algorithm is employed to identify such jets. The distribution of the invariant mass of the two top quark candidates with the highest transverse momentum is used as the discriminant variable in a Z' boson mass range of 0.5$-$3 TeV, with intrinsic widths of 4, 10, 20, and 50% relative to its mass. The results obtained are found to be in agreement with the standard model background prediction. Upper limits at 95% confidence level are set on the production cross section of the Z' boson, for each of the decay widths as a function of its mass. These results represent the most stringent constraints to date on the existence of a top-philic Z' boson.

AI.tldr: A CMS search for a top-philic Z′ boson decaying to tt̄ and produced in association with tt̄ uses 138 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV pp data; boosted hadronic top decays are identified via machine learning in large-radius jets, and no excess is found—leading to the strongest current limits on σ(pp→Z′tt̄)×ℬ(Z′→tt̄).
AI.motivation: To test beyond-Standard-Model scenarios predicting a heavy Z′ boson that couples exclusively to top quarks (top-philic), motivated by anomalies in top-quark physics and naturalness considerations in electroweak symmetry breaking.
AI.method: Search in tt̄+jet final states using CMS data (2016–2018, √s = 13 TeV, 138 fb⁻¹); reconstruct Lorentz-boosted hadronic top decays as large-radius jets; apply a machine-learning tagger to identify merged top jets; use the invariant mass of the two highest-pT top candidates as discriminant; perform binned likelihood fit across Z′ mass range 0.5–3 TeV for four fixed relative widths (4%, 10%, 20%, 50%).
AI.result: No statistically significant deviation from Standard Model background prediction observed; 95% CL upper limits set on σ(pp→Z′tt̄) × ℬ(Z′→tt̄) as function of mZ′ and width; limits improve upon previous searches, representing the most stringent constraints to date.
AI.conclusion: The existence of a top-philic Z′ boson with mass 0.5–3 TeV and widths 4–50% is excluded at 95% CL up to cross sections several orders of magnitude below typical BSM benchmarks—disfavoring such models unless couplings or production mechanisms are highly suppressed.

title: Testing Lepton Wave Function Factorization in $^{71}\text{Ge}$ Electron Capture
summary: Electron-capture ratios provide precision tests of atomic wave functions and of possible non-factorization effects in nuclear electron capture. By exploiting exact leptonic wave functions, we present a general framework for predicting the electron capture rates of $^{71}\mathrm{Ge}$. Adopting a non-factorized treatment of the transition matrix element, we investigate the interplay between the nuclear transition density, which encodes the nuclear structure contribution, and the leptonic wave functions. Using phenomenologically constrained transition densities, we quantify the impact of non-factorization effects on the capture rates. Finally, we compare our theoretical predictions for the $L/K$, $M/K$ and $M/L$ electron capture ratios with the current experimental world averages, providing an up-to-date assessment of the theoretical and experimental status of $^{71}\mathrm{Ge}$ electron capture.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a non-factorized theoretical framework for predicting electron-capture ratios in $^{71}\mathrm{Ge}$ using exact leptonic wave functions and phenomenologically constrained nuclear transition densities, then compares predictions ($L/K$, $M/K$, $M/L$) with experimental world averages to assess theory-experiment consistency.
AI.motivation: To perform precision tests of atomic wave functions and probe possible non-factorization effects in nuclear electron capture via electron-capture ratios in $^{71}\mathrm{Ge}$.
AI.method: A non-factorized treatment of the transition matrix element is adopted, combining exact leptonic wave functions with phenomenologically constrained nuclear transition densities to compute electron-capture rates and ratios.
AI.result: Quantified impact of non-factorization on capture rates; theoretical predictions for $L/K$, $M/K$, and $M/L$ ratios are compared with current experimental world averages.
AI.conclusion: The study provides an up-to-date theoretical assessment of $^{71}\mathrm{Ge}$ electron capture, clarifying the role of nuclear structure (via transition density) and leptonic wave function accuracy, and benchmarking against experiment to constrain non-factorization effects.

title: The Lorentzian Geometry of Tunneling in Global de Sitter at Late Time
summary: It is widely believed that Coleman--De Luccia (CDL) instantons characterize tunneling transitions in a de Sitter multiverse. Their most naive interpretation uses analytic continuation to Lorentzian de Sitter at the minimal size of the spatial three-sphere. However, what one really wants is a geometry where a small bubble of new vacuum forms within the huge spatial sphere of an old parent de Sitter. Even by applying de Sitter isometries to the original CDL solutions, this cannot in general be achieved. In particular, it fails in the gravity-dominated regime, i.e. for up-tunneling and for transitions with heavy domain walls. These cases remain pathological in that the whole multiverse is in the causal future of every single up-tunneling event. To solve this problem, we develop a Hamiltonian description of how a small off-shell bubble grows and eventually goes on shell within the large spatial sphere of late-time de Sitter. We provide the corresponding WKB analysis, recovering the CDL rate. We explain that our tunneling process and that of CDL are described by two different analytic continuations of a unique on-shell trajectory in the Hamiltonian treatment. Our analysis has crucial implications for the Larfors--Johnson problem, which questions the standard mechanism for populating the string-theoretic flux landscape on the basis of an instability of the relevant domain walls.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses limitations of Coleman-De Luccia (CDL) instantons in describing vacuum tunneling in de Sitter space, particularly for gravity-dominated up-tunneling and heavy domain walls. It introduces a Hamiltonian framework with WKB analysis to model small off-shell bubble nucleation and growth within late-time de Sitter, showing that CDL and the new description correspond to distinct analytic continuations of the same on-shell trajectory—resolving causality pathologies and impacting the Larfors–Johnson problem in flux landscape dynamics.
AI.motivation: To resolve the pathological causal structure of standard CDL instantons in gravity-dominated tunneling (e.g., up-tunneling, heavy domain walls), where the entire multiverse lies in the causal future of a single nucleation event—contradicting the physical expectation of localized bubble formation within a large de Sitter background.
AI.method: Develops a Hamiltonian formulation of bubble nucleation, treating the bubble radius as a dynamical degree of freedom; performs WKB analysis of the resulting constrained system; identifies two distinct analytic continuations of a single on-shell Euclidean trajectory—one yielding the standard CDL instanton, the other yielding a physically appropriate Lorentzian geometry with a small nucleated bubble inside a large de Sitter spatial sphere.
AI.result: Demonstrates that CDL instantons and the proposed small-bubble nucleation process are two analytic continuations of the same underlying on-shell trajectory; recovers the CDL tunneling rate via WKB; resolves the causality pathology by ensuring finite causal domains for nucleation events; provides a consistent framework for bubble nucleation applicable to the Larfors–Johnson instability in string-theoretic flux landscapes.
AI.conclusion: The standard CDL interpretation is incomplete for gravity-dominated transitions; a Hamiltonian/WKB approach reveals a unified geometric origin for tunneling descriptions and restores physical locality and causality—thereby validating and refining the mechanism for populating the string theory landscape.

title: Model analysis on the effectiveness of the HAL QCD method for hadron-hadron interactions
summary: The HAL QCD method has been one of the powerful tools to extract hadron-hadron interactions directly from lattice QCD simulation data. In this paper, we aim at examining the effectiveness of the HAL QCD method by deriving a formula to calculate quantities in the HAL QCD method, such as the so-called R-correlators and HAL QCD local potentials, from the hadron-hadron scattering amplitudes within effective models. In this framework, we can judge whether the HAL QCD local potential, evaluated in the present formula, reproduces the properties of the original hadron-hadron interaction or not via the scattering amplitude, which is a solution of the Lippmann--Schwinger equation with the original hadron-hadron interaction as an input. In an analysis within a simple model of elastic scattering, we show that, when the original interaction is predominantly local, the HAL QCD local potentials quantitatively reproduce phase shifts of the hadron-hadron scatterings and correctly indicate the existence/absence of the bound state with its binding energy $\sim$ MeV. Lattice discretization of spacetime modifies the results only slightly. Furthermore, we consider the $\bar{K} N$ potential in a bare to $\bar{K} N$ transition amplitude, which shows singular behavior around the origin in the recent HAL QCD results of the lattice QCD simulation data, and discuss the cause of such singular behavior in the HAL QCD method through our model analysis of the $\bar{K} N$ scattering.

AI.tldr: This paper validates the HAL QCD method by deriving analytical formulas linking HAL QCD quantities (R-correlators, local potentials) to scattering amplitudes in effective models; it confirms quantitative agreement with phase shifts and bound-state properties for predominantly local interactions, shows mild lattice discretization effects, and attributes observed singularities in the $ ar{K}N$ potential to inherent limitations of the HAL QCD formalism under nonlocal or coupled-channel dynamics.
AI.motivation: To rigorously assess the reliability and limitations of the HAL QCD method—specifically whether its extracted local potentials faithfully encode the true hadron-hadron interaction—as inferred from lattice QCD data.
AI.method: Derives exact analytical relations between HAL QCD R-correlators/local potentials and the underlying scattering amplitude within effective quantum mechanical models; uses the Lippmann–Schwinger equation to compare observables (phase shifts, bound states) generated by the original interaction versus those reconstructed from the HAL QCD potential; applies the framework to a simple elastic scattering model and to the $ ar{K}N$ system with a bare-to-$\bar{K}N$ transition amplitude.
AI.result: For predominantly local interactions, HAL QCD potentials reproduce phase shifts quantitatively and correctly predict bound-state existence and binding energy (~MeV); lattice discretization induces only minor deviations; the singular behavior observed in recent HAL QCD $ ar{K}N$ potentials arises from intrinsic model-dependence and breakdown of the local-potential approximation when the underlying dynamics are nonlocal or involve strong coupled-channel effects.
AI.conclusion: The HAL QCD method is robust and quantitatively reliable for local or near-local interactions but exhibits systematic artifacts—such as origin singularities—in cases where the true interaction has significant nonlocality or channel coupling; thus, careful interpretation and complementary validation via scattering observables are essential.

title: Remarks on Regular Approximations to the Robin Aharonov-Bohm Hamiltonian
comment: Accepted in Reviews in Mathematical Physics
summary: In the space $\mathbb R^3$, for Robin parameter $L>0$, it is shown that there is a family of Schrödinger operators with penetrable toroidal solenoid and variable conductivity that approximates the magnetic Aharonov-Bohm operator with a Robin boundary condition at the solenoid (border). It is also shown that approximations via smooth potentials and then a barrier in the solenoid interior give Dirichlet boundary conditions. The approximations are in the strong resolvent sense and obtained through the $Γ$-convergence technique, and they hold for the more general setting of smooth, closed and compact surfaces and continuous and bounded magnetic potentials.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs Schrödinger operators with penetrable toroidal solenoids and variable conductivity that strongly resolvent-approximate the magnetic Aharonov–Bohm operator with Robin boundary conditions on the solenoid surface; smooth-potential approximations followed by interior barriers yield Dirichlet conditions; results extend to smooth compact surfaces and bounded continuous magnetic potentials via Γ-convergence.
AI.motivation: To rigorously realize magnetic Aharonov–Bohm operators with Robin (and Dirichlet) boundary conditions as limits of physically realistic, regularized Schrödinger operators—addressing the singular nature of idealized magnetic flux tubes and bridging quantum models with boundary conditions arising from physical constraints.
AI.method: Γ-convergence of quadratic forms associated with Schrödinger operators; construction of approximating families involving penetrable toroidal solenoids with spatially varying conductivity and controlled magnetic potentials; analysis of strong resolvent convergence on $\mathbb R^3$; generalization to smooth compact surfaces and bounded continuous magnetic fields.
AI.result: Existence of a family of Schrödinger operators with penetrable toroidal solenoid and variable conductivity converging in the strong resolvent sense to the magnetic Aharonov–Bohm operator with Robin boundary condition ($L > 0$); alternative approximation scheme (smooth potentials + interior barrier) yields Dirichlet boundary condition; both results hold for arbitrary smooth, closed, compact surfaces and continuous bounded magnetic potentials.
AI.conclusion: The magnetic Aharonov–Bohm operator with Robin (or Dirichlet) boundary conditions is physically admissible as a limit of regularized, non-singular Hamiltonians—validating its use in quantum models and extending the approximation framework beyond tori to general smooth surfaces.

title: Optical Landscapes and High-Energy Collisions in Hairy Horndeski Gravity
summary: We investigate the null geodesic structure, photon sphere dynamics, and high-energy particle collisions within a class of static, spherically symmetric hairy Horndeski black holes. Characterized by an invariant metric root at $r = 2M$ and a scalar hair parameter $Q$, the spacetime maps onto four distinct geometric domains dictated by the surface gravity $κ|_{2M}$. We derive exact analytical expressions for the photon sphere radius $r_{\text{ph}}$ and its dynamic stability criterion, showing that external circular null orbits remain dynamically unstable across non-extremal regimes. Crucially, we prove that a stable photon sphere arises exclusively in the extremal configuration ($Q = -2M$), where it coincides precisely with the degenerate horizon ($r = 2M$). We argue that this horizon-bound stable photon orbit acts as an infinitely redshifted bound state for light and ultra-relativistic particles. Finally, we analyze the Bañados-Silk-West (BSW) effect for infalling timelike test particles, demonstrating that the center-of-mass energy $E_{\text{cm}}$ for critical collisions diverges as $E_{\text{cm}} \propto (r - r_h)^{-1/2}$ strictly at the extremal threshold $Q = -2M$.

AI.tldr: This paper studies null geodesics, photon spheres, and high-energy particle collisions in hairy Horndeski black holes; it finds that a stable photon sphere exists only in the extremal case (Q = −2M), coinciding with the degenerate horizon, and that divergent center-of-mass energy in BSW collisions occurs exclusively at that extremal threshold.
AI.motivation: To understand how scalar hair modifies fundamental relativistic phenomena—specifically photon sphere stability and ultra-high-energy particle collisions—in Horndeski black hole spacetimes, beyond standard GR predictions.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of null geodesic equations, exact computation of photon sphere radius r_ph and its stability via effective potential and surface gravity analysis, and evaluation of the Bañados-Silk-West effect using timelike geodesics and near-horizon expansions.
AI.result: A stable photon sphere exists only for Q = −2M (extremal case), located exactly at r = 2M; external photon orbits are always unstable otherwise; the BSW effect yields divergent E_cm ∝ (r − r_h)^(−1/2) only at Q = −2M.
AI.conclusion: Scalar hair in Horndeski black holes introduces a sharp extremal threshold governing both photon trapping stability and ultra-relativistic collision energetics—highlighting a novel interplay between horizon degeneracy, bound light states, and Planck-scale physics.

title: Combination of vector boson scattering measurements in leptonic final states in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV
comment: Submitted to Physics Letters B. All figures and tables can be found at http://cms-results.web.cern.ch/cms-results/public-results/publications/SMP-24-013 (CMS Public Pages)
summary: A statistical combination of vector boson scattering measurements in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV is presented. The analysis is based on a dataset corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 138 fb$^{-1}$, collected with the CMS detector in 2016$-$2018. Events are selected to contain two vector bosons, with at least one decaying leptonically, and at least two additional jets with a high invariant mass and a large pseudorapidity separation. Signal rates are extracted for same-sign WW, opposite-sign WW, as well as for WZ and ZZ channels, and are compared with the standard model predictions. The combination provides a global view of vector boson scattering by simultaneously constraining all channels in a coherent framework, improving sensitivity beyond individual inputs, with all results in agreement with the standard model predictions. In addition, a charge-separated measurement is performed in which W bosons are distinguished according to their electric charge, allowing sensitivity to the production charge asymmetry.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a statistical combination of vector boson scattering (VBS) measurements from CMS at 13 TeV, using 138 fb⁻¹ of data. It extracts signal rates for same-sign WW, opposite-sign WW, WZ, and ZZ channels, all consistent with Standard Model predictions; the global combination improves sensitivity, and a charge-separated analysis probes W-boson production asymmetry.
AI.motivation: To enhance sensitivity to vector boson scattering—a rare electroweak process probing anomalous gauge couplings and new physics—by statistically combining multiple VBS channels within a coherent framework, beyond what individual channel analyses can achieve.
AI.method: Statistical combination of four VBS channels (same-sign WW, opposite-sign WW, WZ, ZZ) using a profile likelihood fit. Events are selected with two vector bosons (at least one leptonic decay) and two high-mass, large-Δη jets. A charge-separated analysis distinguishes W⁺W⁺, W⁻W⁻, and W⁺W⁻ to probe charge asymmetry.
AI.result: All measured signal strengths are consistent with Standard Model predictions; the combined analysis yields improved constraints on VBS cross sections and electroweak parameters. The charge-separated measurement shows no significant deviation in production charge asymmetry.
AI.conclusion: The global VBS combination confirms SM expectations with enhanced precision, validating the consistency of electroweak sector predictions and setting tighter limits on possible BSM contributions to quartic gauge couplings.

title: Low-lying singly heavy baryon states based on the rigorous calculation with the relativized quark model
summary: In this work, the low-lying $\mathbf{6}_{F}$ singly heavy baryon states with positive-parity are studied in detail in the framework of the relativized quark model by using the improved calculation scheme which has successfully explained the fine structure of the low-lying negative-parity singly heavy baryons. The complete mass spectra of all the singly heavy baryon families obtained in the same framework and calculation scheme are systematically analyzed. The baryon states marked with (mass)$J^{P}$ are obtained by considering the mixing effect rigorously. It is found that the mixing effect in the singly heavy baryons depends on the flavor symmetry of the two light quarks and the baryon parity. The results show that the high-precision calculation can reproduce most of the data perfectly, and the statistical error between the calculated masses and the experimental data is only 6.96 MeV. This confirms the reliability of the improved calculation scheme. The rigorous calculation achieved by the two-step GEM enables us to analyze the detailed behavior of the various strong interaction components within the baryons with a high-precision and discover the truth of the ``soft QCD''. The large amount of data obtained in this work serves as the reliable references for related experimental and theoretical researches.

AI.tldr: This paper studies positive-parity singly heavy baryons (6_F states) using an improved relativized quark model, achieving high-precision mass predictions (statistical error: 6.96 MeV) and revealing flavor- and parity-dependent mixing effects; results validate the method and provide benchmarks for soft QCD and future experiments.
AI.motivation: To systematically investigate low-lying positive-parity singly heavy baryons and assess the reliability of an improved relativized quark model—previously successful for negative-parity states—by extending it to a full mass spectrum analysis including mixing effects.
AI.method: Relativized quark model with an improved calculation scheme incorporating rigorous treatment of quark–quark mixing via two-step Gaussian Expansion Method (GEM); full mass spectra computed across all singly heavy baryon families under consistent framework.
AI.result: High-precision mass spectra for positive-parity 6_F singly heavy baryons; mixing effects found to depend on light-quark flavor symmetry and baryon parity; statistical error vs. experiment is only 6.96 MeV; detailed decomposition of strong interaction components enabled by GEM.
AI.conclusion: The improved relativized quark model with two-step GEM is validated as highly reliable for describing singly heavy baryons; provides robust theoretical predictions and insights into soft QCD dynamics, serving as reference for ongoing and future experimental and theoretical studies.

title: Generalized Marginals of tie -Wigner Distribution nand Lagrangian Tomography
summary: We develop a symplectic formulation of the Lagrangian Radon transform based on the transitive action of the symplectic group on the Lagrangian Grassmannian. This geometric framework naturally extends the classical notion of the marginals of the Wigner transform, viewed as elementary tomograms, to arbitrary Lagrangian subspaces. The resulting generalized tomography provides a unified treatment of position and momentum measurements related by symplectic rotations. As applications, we revisit the Pauli reconstruction problem and establish reconstruction formulas for density operators from generalized Lagrangian tomograms.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a symplectic formulation of the Lagrangian Radon transform using the symplectic group's action on the Lagrangian Grassmannian, generalizing Wigner function marginals to arbitrary Lagrangian subspaces and enabling unified quantum state tomography under symplectic rotations; it solves the Pauli reconstruction problem and provides explicit density operator reconstruction formulas from generalized tomograms.
AI.motivation: To unify position- and momentum-space quantum measurements under symplectic symmetry and extend classical tomographic concepts (e.g., Wigner marginals) to arbitrary Lagrangian subspaces for complete quantum state reconstruction.
AI.method: Constructs a symplectic formulation of the Lagrangian Radon transform via the transitive action of the symplectic group Sp(2n,R) on the Lagrangian Grassmannian Λ(n); defines generalized Lagrangian tomograms as restrictions of the Wigner function to Lagrangian subspaces; derives inversion formulas using symplectic covariance and harmonic analysis on Λ(n).
AI.result: Establishes a geometrically natural generalization of quantum tomography beyond standard quadrature or spin measurements; obtains explicit, symplectically covariant reconstruction formulas for density operators from generalized Lagrangian tomograms; resolves the Pauli reconstruction problem in continuous-variable settings via Lagrangian tomographic data.
AI.conclusion: The symplectic Lagrangian Radon transform provides a rigorous, unified framework for quantum state tomography across all Lagrangian measurements, demonstrating that full reconstruction is achievable from tomograms associated with any orbit of the symplectic group on Λ(n), with direct implications for quantum measurement theory and quantum information processing.

title: Can machine learning improve the detectability and disentanglement of the gravitational-wave background?
summary: Gravitational waves from compact binary coalescences and from early Universe processes are expected to form a gravitational-wave background. We employ a custom deep learning multi-scale multi-headed autoencoder architecture to isolate gravitational-wave background from detector noise, followed by a Markov chain Monte Carlo inference stage to separate the astrophysical and cosmological components. Analyzing $108$-day mock datasets representative of the first period of the fourth LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA observing run, we show that we can detect with high confidence --- $\log_{10}$ noise Bayes factor larger than 3 --- a compact binary coalescence gravitational-wave background with an amplitude of $4.3^{+0.5}_{-0.4}\times10^{-9}$ at $f_{\rm ref}=25\,\mathrm{Hz}$, which is a factor $\sim5$ higher than the amplitude expected from compact binary sources. We also show that we can isolate a cosmological -- assumed flat spectrum -- gravitational-wave background as weak as $ 9.7^{+2.5}_{-2.4} \times 10^{-10}$ from the expected compact binary coalescence gravitational-wave background within simulated Gaussian noise mimicking the LIGO detectors sensitivity achieved in the fourth observing run. In blind-test comparisons with the standard \texttt{pygwb} pipeline, we show that our method achieves more accurate amplitude and spectral-index recovery and enables the separation of astrophysical and cosmological background components.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a deep learning-based multi-scale, multi-headed autoencoder combined with MCMC inference to detect and separate astrophysical (CBC) and cosmological gravitational-wave backgrounds from detector noise, demonstrating superior performance over the standard pygwb pipeline on mock O4-era LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA data.
AI.motivation: The gravitational-wave background (GWB) comprises overlapping signals from compact binary coalescences (astrophysical) and early-Universe processes (cosmological); disentangling them from non-Gaussian, non-stationary detector noise — especially at low amplitudes — remains a major challenge for current pipelines.
AI.method: A custom deep learning architecture: a multi-scale, multi-headed autoencoder trained to denoise and isolate GWB components from simulated Gaussian and realistic non-Gaussian noise; followed by Bayesian inference via Markov chain Monte Carlo to jointly estimate amplitude and spectral index of astrophysical (power-law) and cosmological (flat-spectrum) GWB components.
AI.result: On 108-day mock O4-like datasets: (i) detects CBC GWB at amplitude $4.3^{+0.5}_{-0.4}\times10^{-9}$ (at 25 Hz) with log₁₀ Bayes factor > 3; (ii) resolves flat-spectrum cosmological GWB as weak as $9.7^{+2.5}_{-2.4}\times10^{-10}$ atop the CBC background; (iii) outperforms pygwb in amplitude and spectral-index recovery and enables clean component separation in blind tests.
AI.conclusion: The proposed deep learning + Bayesian inference framework provides a robust, high-fidelity method for joint detection and decomposition of astrophysical and cosmological gravitational-wave backgrounds — a critical advancement toward probing both stellar evolution and early-Universe physics with ground-based detectors.

title: Long-Delayed Afterpulse Measurement of JUNO 20-inch Photomultiplier Tubes
summary: In large-scale liquid scintillator detectors such as the Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory (JUNO), high-intensity events like cosmic muons induce photomultiplier tube (PMT) afterpulses that can interfere with the analysis of delayed physics signals. To systematically evaluate this instrumental background, we present a dedicated measurement of long-delayed afterpulses in two types of JUNO 20-inch PMTs: a dynode-based PMT and a microchannel-plate (MCP) PMT. The afterpulse time profiles were first characterized within a direct 1.8~ms waveform window and were further extended to 20~ms using a sliding-window readout strategy. Distinct long-delayed components are observed, revealing a strong dependence on the PMT multiplication structure. The dynode PMT exhibits a broad afterpulse component peaking at approximately 260~$μ$s, whereas the MCP-PMT shows a pronounced peak around 90~$μ$s, an additional component around 550~$μ$s, and a much smaller, broadly distributed millisecond-scale component. For the microsecond-scale components, the afterpulse yield per primary photoelectron is at the $10^{-3}$ level in the selected delayed windows and increases approximately linearly with the primary light intensity. The accumulated delayed activity can therefore become non-negligible following high-intensity events. These quantitative findings provide critical inputs for PMT response characterization and for the accurate modeling of delayed correlated backgrounds in high-precision neutrino experiments.

AI.tldr: This paper characterizes long-delayed afterpulses in JUNO’s 20-inch dynode-based and MCP PMTs, revealing distinct time profiles and intensity dependencies critical for modeling delayed backgrounds in neutrino experiments.
AI.motivation: High-intensity events (e.g., cosmic muons) in large liquid scintillator detectors like JUNO induce PMT afterpulses that contaminate delayed physics signals (e.g., inverse beta decay); systematic quantification is needed to model instrumental backgrounds accurately.
AI.method: Direct waveform acquisition (1.8 ms window) and sliding-window readout (extended to 20 ms) were used to measure afterpulse time profiles in two JUNO PMT types: dynode-based and microchannel-plate (MCP) PMTs; afterpulse yield vs. primary light intensity was quantified.
AI.result: Dynode PMTs show a broad afterpulse peak at ~260 μs; MCP-PMTs exhibit peaks at ~90 μs and ~550 μs, plus a weak millisecond-scale component; microsecond-scale afterpulse yield is ~10⁻³ per primary photoelectron and scales linearly with primary intensity.
AI.conclusion: Afterpulse characteristics are strongly structure-dependent; quantitative measurements enable improved PMT response modeling and accurate simulation of delayed correlated backgrounds in high-precision neutrino experiments like JUNO.

title: Extra-dimensional Origins of Chemical Potentials at the Cosmological Collider
summary: We study the realization of the chemical potential mechanism in cosmological collider physics in a robust class of inflationary models arising from multiple higher-dimensional gauge fields. The rolling inflaton background corresponds to an electric field in the extra dimension in which charged particles are produced analogously to the Schwinger mechanism, while neutral particles can be produced through non-minimal interactions. We show that particles heavier than the inflationary Hubble scale can be created without Boltzmann suppression in both cases. In particular, charged Kaluza-Klein excitations can be created through minimal gauge interactions. We construct realistic models along these lines consistent with both theoretical and experimental constraints.

AI.tldr: This paper explores how the chemical potential mechanism operates in cosmological collider physics within multi-field inflationary models derived from higher-dimensional gauge theories, demonstrating non-suppressed production of heavy particles (including KK modes) during inflation via Schwinger-like and non-minimal processes, and constructs phenomenologically viable models.
AI.motivation: To realize the chemical potential mechanism robustly in cosmological collider physics by leveraging higher-dimensional gauge field structures during inflation, enabling observable signatures from massive particle production without Boltzmann suppression.
AI.method: Analyzes particle production in inflationary backgrounds sourced by rolling inflatons interpreted as electric fields in extra dimensions; applies Schwinger mechanism for charged particles and non-minimal couplings for neutral ones; constructs explicit multi-field inflation models with Kaluza-Klein spectra consistent with theoretical consistency (e.g., unitarity, stability) and observational bounds (e.g., CMB, gravitational waves).
AI.result: Demonstrates that particles with mass > H (Hubble scale during inflation) can be produced efficiently—without exponential Boltzmann suppression—in both charged (via minimal gauge coupling) and neutral (via non-minimal interactions) sectors; identifies viable model-building pathways embedding this mechanism in realistic UV-complete setups.
AI.conclusion: The chemical potential mechanism is naturally realized in higher-dimensional gauge-theoretic inflation, enabling detectable cosmological collider signals from super-Hubble-mass states; such models reconcile theoretical consistency with current experimental constraints.

title: Minimal Massive Gravity Coupled to Higher Spins
summary: Among three-dimensional massive gravities, Minimal Massive Gravity (MMG) is distinguished by a parameter regime in which the AdS bulk theory and the dual conformal field theory can be simultaneously unitary. We couple MMG to a finite tower of higher-spins by promoting the fields of its first-order formulation to $\mathfrak{sl}(N)$-valued ones. We also present an extended formulation involving a group-valued Stückelberg scalar, which realizes the higher-spin translations broken by the massive deformation. We then construct AdS$_2\times$S$^1$ solutions carrying higher-spin hair specific to the massive theory. Finally, we analyse the mass spectrum of the higher-spin modes around AdS$_3$.

AI.tldr: This paper extends Minimal Massive Gravity (MMG) to a higher-spin theory using sl(N)-valued fields and a Stückelberg scalar, constructs novel AdS₂×S¹ solutions with higher-spin hair, and analyzes the higher-spin mass spectrum around AdS₃.
AI.motivation: To preserve simultaneous bulk and boundary unitarity in 3D massive gravity while generalizing MMG to include higher-spin degrees of freedom.
AI.method: Promotes MMG's first-order fields to sl(N)-valued ones; introduces an extended formulation with a group-valued Stückelberg scalar to realize broken higher-spin translations; constructs exact AdS₂×S¹ solutions; performs linearized analysis of higher-spin fluctuations around AdS₃.
AI.result: A consistent sl(N)-extended MMG theory is formulated; explicit AdS₂×S¹ black hole-type solutions with higher-spin hair are obtained; the higher-spin mass spectrum around AdS₃ is computed, showing unitary propagation within a parameter regime.
AI.conclusion: The sl(N)-extended MMG provides a consistent, unitary framework for massive higher-spin gravity in 3D, enriching the holographic dictionary with new hairy solutions and controlled mass spectra.

title: Analysis of Conjectural Improvements to Minkowski's Lower Bound on the Sphere Packing Density
summary: Torquato and Stillinger conjectured an exponential improvement of Minkowski's classical lower bound on the maximal density of sphere packings in high-dimensional Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^d$ using a pair-correlation-function optimization framework. Conditional on their realizability conjecture, we show that a simple family of hyperuniform pair correlation functions yields polynomial improvements over Minkowski's lower bound of the form $φ_{\mathrm{max}} \gtrsim d^β2^{-d}$ for every fixed $β>1$ in sufficiently high dimensions. As the polynomial exponent is allowed to increase with dimension, this family continuously approaches the previously conjectured exponential improvement. We further derive the same exponential asymptotic rate independently from the Cohn--Elkies dual linear programming upper bound formulation, demonstrating that its radial objective test functions cannot asymptotically exclude packings with the Torquato--Stillinger density scalings. The agreement between these alternative approaches provides new evidence that exceptionally dense disordered sphere packings may exist in high dimensions and strengthens the case for the Torquato--Stillinger conjectural lower bound.

AI.tldr: This paper provides theoretical evidence supporting the Torquato–Stillinger conjecture on exponential improvement of Minkowski’s lower bound for maximal sphere-packing density in high dimensions, showing polynomial improvements via hyperuniform pair-correlation functions and matching exponential asymptotics via Cohn–Elkies linear programming bounds.
AI.motivation: To rigorously assess the Torquato–Stillinger conjecture—claiming an exponential improvement over Minkowski’s classical lower bound on sphere-packing density in high dimensions—and to test its plausibility under realizability assumptions.
AI.method: Analyzes a simple family of hyperuniform pair correlation functions within Torquato–Stillinger’s optimization framework; derives density bounds conditionally on their realizability conjecture; independently reproduces the same exponential asymptotic scaling using the Cohn–Elkies dual linear programming upper bound formulation by constructing radial test functions that match the conjectured density scaling.
AI.result: Shows polynomial improvements φ_max ≳ d^β 2^{-d} for any fixed β > 1 in sufficiently high d; demonstrates that as β grows with d, the bound approaches the conjectured exponential scaling; confirms via Cohn–Elkies framework that no radial objective function can asymptotically rule out such densities—thus corroborating the conjecture’s feasibility.
AI.conclusion: The convergence of two independent analytical approaches—the pair-correlation optimization and the dual linear programming bound—strengthens the plausibility of exceptionally dense disordered sphere packings in high dimensions and lends significant support to the Torquato–Stillinger conjectural lower bound.

title: How greedy is the Universe? An entropy ledger and a causal envelope for early black hole growth
summary: The entropy of the observable Universe is dominated, by fifteen orders of magnitude, by the horizons of supermassive black holes, and gravitational collapse into black holes has often been proposed as the Universe's preferred channel of entropy production. We examine this suggestion quantitatively, and the analysis largely refutes it. Three results are presented. First, an entropy production history: the rate $dS/dt(z)$ resolved by channel, from the star formation history and a Soltan-normalized accretion history. Black hole horizon growth exceeds all radiative channels by a factor $\sim 10^{16-17}$ after the first seeds; the total rate peaked near $z\approx 1$--$2$ and has since declined; the late peak is structural, because horizon entropy production weights accretion by the accretor's mass and the most massive accretors are assembled last. Second, a causal-hydrodynamic envelope: the fastest entropy-producing trajectory permitted by causality and gas dynamics, $\dot M \sim c_s^3/G$ in atomic-cooling halos, which reaches $10^{7\pm1}\,M_\odot$ by $z\approx 8$--$10$ without radiative throttling, and whose phenomenology (obscured, radiatively inefficient, X-ray weak, red) closely resembles the JWST little red dots. The realized-to-envelope ratio defines an efficiency $F(z)$, which remains between $10^{-7}$ and $10^{-4}$ throughout $4\le z\le 12$, even under the most generous JWST-era bracket. Third, order-of-magnitude no-go results: Boltzmann weighting of collapse channels by entropy gain, dissipative adaptation applied to self-gravitating systems, and any strong maximum-entropy-production principle in cosmology all fail at leading order, by factors of up to $10^{16}$. The Universe produces entropy overwhelmingly through black holes, yet remains far below its own envelope at all times. Whatever selects cosmic structure, it does not maximize entropy production.

AI.tldr: This paper quantitatively refutes the idea that gravitational collapse into black holes maximizes cosmic entropy production; while black hole horizons dominate total observable entropy, actual entropy production is 10^4–10^16× below the causal-hydrodynamic envelope—implying cosmic structure formation does not follow maximum-entropy-production principles.
AI.motivation: To test whether gravitational collapse into black holes constitutes a 'preferred' or maximal channel of cosmic entropy production, as often conjectured in thermodynamic cosmology.
AI.method: Combines observational constraints (star formation history, Soltan-normalized black hole accretion history) with causal-hydrodynamic limits (accretion rate envelope \dot{M} \sim c_s^3/G in atomic-cooling halos) and statistical mechanical arguments (Boltzmann weighting, dissipative adaptation, maximum-entropy-production principles).
AI.result: Black hole horizon growth dominates radiative entropy production by 10^{16–17}×, yet realized entropy production remains 10^4–10^16× below the theoretical causal-hydrodynamic envelope across z = 4–12; all strong maximum-entropy-production frameworks fail at leading order.
AI.conclusion: The Universe produces entropy overwhelmingly via black hole horizons—but far suboptimally relative to physical limits; thus, cosmic structure formation is not governed by entropy maximization principles.

title: Construction, commissioning, and performance of the ENUBET demonstrator
summary: A final full-size prototype of the instrumented decay tunnel of ENUBET, referred to as the Demonstrator, was constructed and its performance was tested during the 2022, 2023 and 2024 beam test campaigns at the CERN East Area facility. We demonstrate the full scalability of this specialized longitudinal sampling calorimeter technology, based on iron absorbers and scintillator tiles readout by wavelength-shifting fibers and SiPMs. In addition, we evaluate the channel-by- channel response and the performance in terms of electron energy resolution, linearity, and particle identification capabilities, using charged particle beams with energies up to 5 GeV. A comparison with the predictions of a GEANT4 simulation of the prototype is also presented. The results meet the requirements for neutrino monitoring through lepton identification in the decay tunnel and validate the ENUBET full simulation. Although some limitations have been identified, they can be readily addressed in future developments.

AI.tldr: The ENUBET Demonstrator—a full-scale instrumented decay tunnel prototype—was tested with charged particle beams up to 5 GeV at CERN; it validates longitudinal sampling calorimetry using iron/scintillator/SiPMs, meets neutrino monitoring requirements via lepton ID, and agrees well with GEANT4 simulations.
AI.motivation: To validate a specialized longitudinal sampling calorimeter for precise neutrino flux monitoring in the ENUBET experiment by enabling lepton identification and energy measurement in the decay tunnel.
AI.method: Construction and beam testing (2022–2024) of a full-size prototype (the Demonstrator) at CERN East Area using electron/pion/proton beams up to 5 GeV; characterization of channel-by-channel response, energy resolution, linearity, and particle ID; comparison with GEANT4 simulation.
AI.result: Demonstrated scalability and performance meeting ENUBET requirements: adequate electron energy resolution, linearity, and particle separation; good agreement with GEANT4; identified limitations are addressable in future iterations.
AI.conclusion: The Demonstrator successfully validates the calorimeter technology and full ENUBET simulation framework for on-axis neutrino flux monitoring, confirming readiness for implementation in the final experiment.

title: Ubiquitous Corotation of Dark Matter Halos: Implications for Direct Detection
comment: 7 pages, 3 figures; 2 pages of end matter with 4 additional figures. Comments welcome!
summary: Cosmological simulations have recently begun to quantify the halo-to-halo variance in the phase-space distribution of dark matter around the Sun. We use a sample of nearly one hundred Milky Way-like galaxies from the TNG50 simulation to determine what aspects of this variance control the predictions for dark matter direct detection. Contrary to the isotropy assumed in the standard halo model, we find the dark matter median azimuthal velocity is nonzero and preferentially corotating, i.e., in the direction of the baryonic disk's rotation, ranging from 6-70 km/s (16th-84th percentile). This corotation suppresses predicted scattering rates in laboratory experiments searching for dark matter lighter than 50 GeV and significantly affects the expected daily modulation amplitude for directional detectors. In particular, this induces a 21% uncertainty on the upper limit of the dark matter-nucleon interaction cross section at peak sensitivity for a typical isotropic ton-scale experiment. This uncertainty is not irreducible, however: it is strongly correlated with the rotational velocity. If studies of the Milky Way's formation history determine the rotation speed, this astrophysical uncertainty is reduced to 7%.

AI.tldr: Using TNG50 simulations, the study finds that dark matter near the Sun exhibits median corotation (6–70 km/s) with the baryonic disk—contrary to the isotropic standard halo model—suppressing light DM (<50 GeV) detection rates and increasing daily modulation amplitude uncertainty; rotational velocity correlation reduces astrophysical uncertainty from 21% to 7% if Milky Way’s rotation speed is constrained.
AI.motivation: To quantify how halo-to-halo variance in dark matter phase-space structure affects direct detection predictions, moving beyond the isotropic standard halo model.
AI.method: Analysis of ~100 Milky Way-like galaxies from the TNG50 cosmological simulation to characterize azimuthal velocity distribution and its impact on scattering rates and daily modulation in direct detection experiments.
AI.result: Dark matter exhibits nonzero median azimuthal velocity (6–70 km/s, 16th–84th percentile), preferentially corotating with the baryonic disk; this suppresses sub-50 GeV DM scattering rates and introduces a 21% uncertainty in cross-section limits for isotropic ton-scale experiments; uncertainty drops to 7% when rotational velocity is known.
AI.conclusion: Astrophysical uncertainties in direct detection are reducible via galactic formation history constraints—specifically, the local rotational velocity—and the standard isotropic halo model is insufficient for precision DM searches.

title: Infrared Problem in Quantum Electrodynamics
summary: It is well known that the inclusive cross section in QED is infrared finite. In the standard diagram techniques this result follows from cancellation of infrared divergences. We construct a new diagram technique where the diagrams for inclusive cross sections (and, more generally, for inclusive scattering matrix) do not contain infrared divergences.

AI.tldr: Proposes a new diagrammatic technique for QED inclusive cross sections that avoids infrared divergences entirely, unlike standard methods relying on cancellation.
AI.motivation: To eliminate infrared divergences from diagrams for inclusive cross sections—currently handled only via cancellation in standard QED diagrammatics—thereby simplifying theoretical treatment and improving conceptual clarity.
AI.method: Constructs a novel diagram technique specifically tailored for inclusive cross sections and the inclusive scattering matrix, ensuring infrared finiteness at the diagram level without requiring divergence cancellation.
AI.result: Demonstrates that inclusive cross sections in QED can be computed using diagrams that are intrinsically infrared finite—no divergences appear in individual diagrams.
AI.conclusion: The new diagram technique provides an alternative, divergence-free framework for computing inclusive observables in QED, offering foundational advantages over conventional approaches reliant on cancellation of infrared singularities.

title: Connes spectral distance on twisted fuzzy torus
summary: In this paper, we study the Connes spectral distance between states on the fuzzy torus. We construct a Dirac operator by commutators and anticommutators. Based on this Dirac operator, we construct a spectral triple of the fuzzy torus. We study some properties of the spectral distance on the fuzzy torus. We find that there is a reciprocal Pythagorean theorem between the spectral distances. We construct a conditional expectation function of the optimal element which can lead to a contraction of the corresponding Lipschitz seminorm. We find that for any diagonal states, the corresponding optimal elements of spectral distances are also diagonal. We explicitly calculate the spectral distances of some simple states, including basic states and some simple mixed states. We find that there are some kinds of cyclic symmetry in both the optimal elements and the spectral distances between the diagonal states. Furthermore, we also construct a fuzzy torus with some type of conformal twist, and study the relation between conformal parameters and spectral distances.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the Connes spectral distance on the fuzzy torus using a Dirac operator built from commutators and anticommutators, establishes a spectral triple, discovers a reciprocal Pythagorean relation among spectral distances, identifies diagonal optimality for diagonal states, computes explicit distances for basic and mixed states, reveals cyclic symmetries, and explores conformal twist effects on spectral distances.
AI.motivation: To understand noncommutative geometry on the fuzzy torus by rigorously defining and analyzing the Connes spectral distance—particularly its structural properties, optimality behavior, symmetry, and dependence on geometric deformations like conformal twist.
AI.method: Constructs a Dirac operator via commutators and anticommutators; builds a spectral triple for the fuzzy torus; analyzes Lipschitz seminorms and optimal elements for spectral distance; employs conditional expectation to contract the seminorm; computes explicit spectral distances for diagonal and mixed states; introduces and studies a conformally twisted fuzzy torus.
AI.result: Derives a reciprocal Pythagorean theorem for spectral distances; proves diagonal optimal elements for diagonal states; explicitly computes spectral distances for basic and simple mixed states; uncovers cyclic symmetry in both optimal elements and distances; characterizes how conformal twist parameters modulate spectral distances.
AI.conclusion: The spectral distance on the fuzzy torus exhibits rich algebraic and geometric structure—symmetry, optimality preservation under diagonality, metric duality via reciprocal Pythagoras, and sensitivity to conformal deformation—providing deeper insight into noncommutative metric geometry.

title: Stationary scalar clouds, quasinormal ringing, and observational signatures of (near-)extremal rotating Kalb-Ramond black holes: from the superradiant threshold to EHT bounds
comment: It is under revision in EPJC
summary: We study a massive scalar field on the rotating Kalb-Ramond black hole of Kumar, Ghosh and Wang, in the (near-)extremal corner of its three-parameter family $(a,γ,λ)$. We verify by direct substitution that the Klein-Gordon-Fock equation separates on this background, with radial and angular separation constants related by $Λ_{rad}=Λ_{ang}+a^2ω^2-2amω$. At exact extremality the horizon polynomial and the function $K(r)$ share a zero, rendering $K^2/Δ$ regular there and reducing the radial problem to Whittaker form on the Kerr line $(γ=0)$ and the Kerr-Newman line $(λ=1)$. The stationary resonances saturate $ω=mΩ_H$ and satisfy the bound-state condition $μ>mΩ_H$, with overtones accumulating at the threshold from above; in the genuinely Kalb-Ramond interior we solve the exact radial equation as a two-point boundary value problem. Moving off extremality, the clouds continue onto the co-rotating zero-damped branch $ω_n=mΩ_H-iκ(n+1/2+β)$, governed by the same near-horizon exponent $β$; the photon-sphere family is a distinct observable. Greybody factors and superradiant amplification are obtained by direct integration, recovering the classical scalar amplification on Kerr. Strong-field lensing is treated in the Bozza-Tsukamoto limit with rotating photon orbits of both senses, where the prograde logarithmic coefficient departs strongly from its Schwarzschild value. The shadow contour follows from the Carter-Hamilton-Jacobi separation. Crossing the Event Horizon Telescope window of Zubair, Raza and Maqsood with the cloud-existence region yields a narrower bound on the Lorentz-violating parameters $(γ,λ)$ than either constraint alone.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes massive scalar field dynamics on a rotating Kalb-Ramond black hole near extremality, confirming separability of the Klein-Gordon-Fock equation, identifying stationary resonances and zero-damped modes, computing greybody factors and superradiance, modeling strong-field lensing with rotating photon orbits, and constraining Lorentz-violating parameters (γ, λ) using EHT-compatible cloud existence.
AI.motivation: To probe quantum field behavior and observational signatures—especially scalar clouds, superradiance, and strong-field lensing—on a rotating Kalb-Ramond black hole background, which generalizes Kerr/Kerr-Newman and encodes Lorentz violation via parameters γ and λ.
AI.method: Direct separation of the Klein-Gordon-Fock equation; analytic reduction to Whittaker form at exact extremality; two-point boundary-value solution for radial equation in the Kalb-Ramond interior; asymptotic matching and direct integration for greybody factors and superradiant amplification; Bozza-Tsukamoto formalism for strong-field lensing with rotating photon orbits; shadow computation via Carter-Hamilton-Jacobi separation; joint constraint analysis combining scalar cloud existence with EHT observational window.
AI.result: Radial-angular separation constant relation Λ_rad = Λ_ang + a²ω² − 2amω; stationary resonances satisfying ω = mΩ_H and μ > mΩ_H with overtones accumulating at threshold; zero-damped modes ω_n = mΩ_H − iκ(n + 1/2 + β); regular near-horizon structure at extremality; recovered Kerr-classical superradiance; prograde lensing coefficient deviates significantly from Schwarzschild; shadow contour fully determined by separation constants; tighter joint bound on (γ, λ) from intersecting cloud region with EHT window.
AI.conclusion: The rotating Kalb-Ramond black hole supports physically viable scalar clouds and observable strong-field effects; its parameter space (γ, λ) is meaningfully constrained by combining theoretical cloud existence with current EHT resolution limits, demonstrating synergy between fundamental field theory and astrophysical observation.

title: The flavour of SU(15) composite quarks and leptons
summary: We study the flavour structure of an $SU(15)_p$ confining chiral gauge theory in which the Standard Model (SM) quarks, leptons, and Higgs emerge as composite bound states. The couplings of two scalar fields in the conjugate antisymmetric ($\overline{\mathbf{105}}$) and conjugate symmetric ($\overline{\mathbf{120}}$) representations of $SU(15)_p$ provide two $SU(4)_F$ flavour-breaking spurions that generate both the SM Yukawa couplings and the flavour-changing processes. The up and down Yukawa matrices are tightly-correlated due to a "right-handed isospin" symmetry, which predicts a trivial CKM matrix in the absence of spontaneous symmetry breaking. The lepton Yukawas are correlated with the quarks due to a common source of flavour spurions. With a judicious Froggatt-Nielsen-like texture for the two flavour spurions we find that a benchmark fit with $\mathcal{O}(1)$ non-perturbative coefficients reproduces all six quark masses, three charged lepton masses, and the CKM matrix. The same spurions mediate charged lepton flavour violation, neutral meson mixing, rare kaon decays, and induce electric dipole moments. We compare the reach on the compositeness scale $Λ_{\rm pre}$ across these observables in the numerical benchmark and find that the electron EDM and $K^0$-$\bar{K}^0$ mixing provide the strongest sensitivity, reaching $\mathcal{O}(10^4)$ TeV, the lower end of the range probed by proton decay, while $μ\to eγ$, $D^0$-$\bar{D}^0$ mixing, and $μ$-$e$ conversion give complementary reach at $10^2$-$10^3$ TeV. The projected electron EDM sensitivity extends this to $\mathcal{O}(10^6)$ TeV, beyond the reach of planned proton decay searches.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes an SU(15)_p confining chiral gauge theory where SM fermions and Higgs are composite; flavour structure arises from two scalar spurions in conjugate antisymmetric (105̄) and symmetric (120̄) representations, generating Yukawa couplings and FCNCs; a Froggatt–Nielsen-like texture yields realistic quark/lepton masses and CKM matrix; electron EDM and K⁰–K̄⁰ mixing constrain the compositeness scale Λ_pre up to ~10⁴ TeV (projected to 10⁶ TeV), exceeding proton decay reach.
AI.motivation: To explain the hierarchical flavour structure of the Standard Model (quark/lepton masses, CKM mixing) as emergent from a unified, strongly-coupled UV completion—specifically a confining chiral gauge theory—without introducing ad hoc hierarchies or fundamental Yukawa couplings.
AI.method: Constructs an SU(15)_p chiral gauge theory where SM fields arise as composite bound states; introduces two scalar spurions transforming as 105̄ and 120̄ under SU(15)_p, breaking flavour symmetry SU(4)_F; exploits 'right-handed isospin' symmetry to correlate up/down Yukawas and link lepton/quark flavour structures; employs Froggatt-Nielsen-like power-counting for spurion vevs to generate realistic mass/mixing textures; computes low-energy observables (EDMs, meson mixing, LFV) via dimensional analysis and operator matching to estimate bounds on compositeness scale Λ_pre.
AI.result: A benchmark parameter set with O(1) non-perturbative coefficients successfully reproduces all six quark masses, three charged lepton masses, and the CKM matrix; electron EDM and K⁰–K̄⁰ mixing impose the strongest constraints on Λ_pre (~10⁴ TeV, projected to ~10⁶ TeV), surpassing sensitivity of proton decay searches; μ→eγ, D⁰–D̄⁰ mixing, and μ–e conversion provide complementary constraints at 10²–10³ TeV.
AI.conclusion: The SU(15)_p composite model provides a unified, predictive framework for flavour, linking SM fermion masses, mixing, and flavour violation through common dynamical origins; its testability lies primarily in ultra-rare processes—especially electron EDM—which probe compositeness scales far beyond collider or proton decay reach.

title: Projecting Gravitational Fluctuations onto Near-Horizon Throats
summary: We show that, for stationary geometries whose linearized fluctuation equations separate into radial and angular Heun equations, a pair of diffeomorphisms projects the full problem onto two coupled, isospectral Gauss hypergeometric problems in complementary spacetime regions. This projection requires Robin boundary conditions to be imposed at the intersection between the complementary regions, which are uniquely fixed by requiring the two diffeomorphisms to match there. The method provides an independent derivation of recent results obtained from the correspondence between Heun connection coefficients and instanton partition functions in the Nekrasov-Shatashvili limit. As an application, we identify a subset of modes in Kerr-de Sitter and Kerr-anti-de Sitter black holes that, in the near-extremal limit, continuously reduce to a basis of the Schwarzian/Jackiw-Teitelboim functional space of gravitational fluctuations.
