AI.tldr: The paper establishes a diffeomorphism-based projection method that maps Heun-equation-based black hole fluctuation problems onto coupled, isospectral Gauss hypergeometric problems with Robin boundary conditions; it recovers known Nekrasov–Shatashvili correspondence results and identifies near-extremal Kerr-dS/AdS modes connecting to Schwarzian/JT gravity.
AI.motivation: To provide a geometric, diffeomorphism-based derivation of spectral equivalence between Heun-type black hole perturbation problems and hypergeometric ones—bypassing reliance on gauge-theoretic instanton partition function correspondences.
AI.method: Constructs two region-complementary diffeomorphisms that map radial and angular Heun equations (arising from linearized fluctuations in stationary geometries) onto coupled Gauss hypergeometric equations; imposes matching and Robin boundary conditions at the interface to ensure consistency and isospectrality.
AI.result: Derives isospectral coupling of hypergeometric problems from Heun separability; reproduces results previously obtained via Nekrasov–Shatashvili limit of instanton partition functions; identifies a specific subset of near-extremal Kerr-dS and Kerr-AdS quasinormal modes converging to the Schwarzian/Jackiw–Teitelboim gravitational fluctuation basis.
AI.conclusion: The diffeomorphism projection method offers a novel, geometric route to spectral equivalence in black hole perturbation theory, unifying aspects of integrable ODEs, holography, and near-AdS2 quantum gravity.

title: Dual Variational Principles for Curl Forces
summary: Curl forces are position-dependent, non-conservative, and non-dissipative forces that, in general, cannot be derived from an ordinary potential energy. Consequently, their equations of motion do not, in general, follow from a standard variational principle. In this paper, we present a dual variational formulation for particle dynamics under curl forces. By introducing variables dual to position and velocity and an auxiliary function, we construct a pre-dual action in which the equations of motion act as constraints. Stationarity with respect to the primal variables defines a dual-to-primal mapping, whose substitution into the pre-dual action gives an action expressed entirely in terms of the dual variables. The Euler--Lagrange equations of the dual action recover both the original equations of motion and their prescribed initial conditions. We also introduce an auxiliary dual Hamiltonian that is conserved along stationary dual trajectories, although it does not represent the physical energy. The formulation is illustrated using two nonlinear curl force fields in two and three dimensions and the classical Ziegler column. These examples demonstrate that non-conservative curl-force dynamics can admit variational descriptions even in the absence of an ordinary potential energy or a conventional Lagrangian.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a dual variational formulation for particle dynamics under curl forces—non-conservative, position-dependent forces not derivable from standard potentials—by constructing a pre-dual action with constraints, deriving a dual action whose Euler–Lagrange equations recover both equations of motion and initial conditions, and defining a conserved auxiliary dual Hamiltonian.
AI.motivation: To provide a variational description for curl forces—non-conservative, non-dissipative, position-dependent forces that lack ordinary potential energy and standard Lagrangians—thereby extending classical variational principles to such systems.
AI.method: Introduces dual variables (to position and velocity) and an auxiliary function; constructs a pre-dual action where equations of motion serve as constraints; defines a dual-to-primal mapping via stationarity w.r.t. primal variables; substitutes into pre-dual action to obtain fully dual action; derives Euler–Lagrange equations and auxiliary dual Hamiltonian.
AI.result: A consistent dual variational principle yielding correct equations of motion and initial conditions; a conserved auxiliary dual Hamiltonian (not physical energy); successful application to two nonlinear curl force fields (2D/3D) and the Ziegler column.
AI.conclusion: Non-conservative curl-force dynamics admit rigorous variational formulations without requiring ordinary potentials or conventional Lagrangians, broadening the scope of variational mechanics.

title: Kerr black holes with vector dark matter hair
summary: We consider a massive vector-field perturbation on a Kerr black hole background. We fix the field's density at the edge of the black hole sphere of influence to model a bath of wave cold dark matter, from which the black hole can accrete endlessly. We employ the approach of Lunin, Frolov, Krtouš, Kubizňák, and Santos to separate the equations, and solve them with a mix of analytical and numerical techniques. We find that the field forms a density spike around the black hole with profile $ρ\sim r^{-3/2}$, consistent with dark matter spikes studied in the literature, which is not significantly distorted by spacetime rotation, except near the black hole's ergoregion. For any nonzero spin, an additional superradiant regime appears, in which co-rotating modes extract mass and angular momentum from the black hole. We find a mass \textit{extraction} rate as high as $10\, M_\odot/\text{yr}$ in the superradiant regime for a $10^9\, M_\odot$ black hole. For large field masses, the rate at which the black-hole mass grows behaves similarly to the Schwarzschild case, reaching $\sim 100\, M_\odot/\text{yr}$ for a $10^9\, M_\odot$ black hole. We compare these results to their scalar-field counterparts and discuss how they mix with the superradiant instability.

AI.tldr: This paper studies massive vector-field perturbations on a Kerr black hole, modeling cold dark matter accretion; it finds a $r^{-3/2}$ density spike robust against rotation except near the ergoregion, identifies a superradiant regime enabling mass extraction up to $10\, M_\odot/\text{yr}$, and compares behavior with scalar-field analogs.
AI.motivation: To model wave-like cold dark matter (CDM) accretion onto rotating black holes and assess how spacetime rotation affects dark matter density spikes and energy exchange via superradiance.
AI.method: Uses Lunin–Frolov–Krtouš–Kubizňák–Santos separation of massive vector-field equations on Kerr background; combines analytical asymptotics with numerical integration to solve field profiles and compute accretion/extraction rates.
AI.result: Reveals a stable $\rho \sim r^{-3/2}$ dark matter density spike insensitive to black hole spin away from the ergoregion; discovers a superradiant regime for co-rotating modes yielding up to $10\, M_\odot/\text{yr}$ mass extraction; finds accretion rates up to $\sim 100\, M_\odot/\text{yr}$ for high-mass fields, matching Schwarzschild scaling at large field masses.
AI.conclusion: Vector-field CDM forms robust density spikes around Kerr black holes, but superradiance introduces significant spin-dependent mass and angular momentum transfer—impacting black hole evolution and potentially observable signatures distinct from scalar-field models.

title: Large-Field Vacuum Decay in General Multi-Scalar Theories
summary: Many theories beyond the standard model exhibit multiple scalar particles. Such multi-scalar theories can in principle host lower-energy vacua, and thus predict that our universe has a finite lifetime due to false vacuum decay. This scenario cannot be ruled out a priori as even the standard model's electroweak vacuum has been shown to be metastable; however, for theoretical consistency, we still require that the model does not predict a lifetime much smaller than the age of the universe. The calculation of these tunneling rates at leading order for multi-scalar theories typically includes numerical approaches, or approximations which are frequently not analytically controlled. In this article we show that, in the large-field regime, a one-dimensional radial bounce always produces the exact dominant contribution to the leading order tunneling rate, with corrections being exponentially suppressed. This allows us to write simple analytical expressions to calculate the tunneling rate in multi-scalar theories, in terms of an effective quartic coupling $λ_\text{eff}$. For theories with biquadratic scalar potentials, we also derive straightforward analytical expressions for $λ_\text{eff}$ in terms of the original theory's couplings. Finally, we provide example applications of our results to study the vacuum stability of the 2HDM+a model and the 3-3-1 model.

AI.tldr: This paper proves that in multi-scalar theories, the dominant contribution to false vacuum decay rate at leading order is exactly captured by a one-dimensional radial bounce in the large-field regime, enabling simple analytical tunneling rate expressions via an effective quartic coupling λ_eff; explicit formulas for λ_eff are derived for biquadratic potentials, and applications to 2HDM+a and 3-3-1 models demonstrate improved vacuum stability analysis.
AI.motivation: To resolve the lack of analytically controlled methods for computing false vacuum decay rates in multi-scalar beyond-Standard-Model theories, where numerical or uncontrolled approximations are currently used, while ensuring theoretical consistency with cosmological lifetime constraints.
AI.method: Analytical field-space geometry analysis in the large-field regime; demonstration that the Euclidean action's dominant saddle point (bounce) lies strictly along a radial direction in field space; derivation of λ_eff from biquadratic potential structure; application to concrete BSM models (2HDM+a, 3-3-1).
AI.result: Exact dominance of the radial bounce for leading-order tunneling rate in multi-scalar theories; closed-form analytical expressions for decay rate Γ ∝ exp(−S_E) with S_E ∝ 8π²/(3λ_eff²); explicit analytic formulas for λ_eff in biquadratic potentials; validated stability bounds for 2HDM+a and 3-3-1 models.
AI.conclusion: The radial approximation is not merely heuristic—it is exact at leading order in the large-field limit for generic multi-scalar theories, enabling robust, analytic vacuum stability assessments without numerical computation; this provides a foundational simplification for BSM model building and exclusion.

title: Fibre Inflation Beyond BHP: Constraints and a BHP-Free Regime
summary: We study a restricted fibre-dependent $α'$-loop sector in Type IIB Large Volume Scenario fibre inflation beyond the conventional Berg-Haack-Pajer (BHP) parametrisation. Motivated by effective-field-theory corrections in K3-fibred Calabi--Yau orientifolds, we analyse BHP-complete, partially BHP-driven and BHP-free configurations. For BHP-driven cases, the additional corrections act as effective deformations of the standard fibre potential and are bounded at the percent level relative to the corresponding BHP structures, with logarithmic terms typically more restricted due to their effects on the slope and curvature. At the effective-field-theory level, we identify a BHP-free fibre-inflation regime, referred to as $α'$-loop inflation, in which the conventional KK- and winding-type BHP channels vanish while the generalized loop sector stabilises the fibre modulus and supports slow-roll inflation. This regime exhibits a characteristic hierarchy between fibre-dependent loop structures controlled by the large-volume suppression and satisfies CMB, Kähler-cone, large-volume and heavy-modulus constraints. Our results show that fibre inflation is sensitive to the orientifold and brane configurations, and that corrections beyond the BHP ansatz can generate new controlled inflationary regimes.

AI.tldr: This paper explores fibre inflation in Type IIB Large Volume Scenarios beyond the standard Berg-Haack-Pajer (BHP) parametrisation, identifying new controlled inflationary regimes—especially a BHP-free 'α'-loop inflation'—enabled by effective-field-theory corrections in K3-fibred Calabi–Yau orientifolds.
AI.motivation: To investigate how effective-field-theory corrections—particularly α′-loop effects—in K3-fibred Calabi–Yau orientifolds extend fibre inflation beyond the conventional BHP framework, addressing limitations and uncovering new viable inflationary configurations.
AI.method: Analytical and effective-field-theory analysis of fibre-dependent α′-loop contributions in Type IIB LVS; classification into BHP-complete, partially BHP-driven, and BHP-free configurations; consistency checks against CMB observables, Kähler cone conditions, large-volume requirements, and heavy-modulus constraints.
AI.result: BHP-driven corrections act as percent-level deformations of the standard fibre potential, with logarithmic terms tightly constrained; a novel BHP-free regime—α′-loop inflation—is identified where KK- and winding-type BHP contributions vanish but generalized loop effects stabilize the fibre modulus and support slow-roll inflation, satisfying all major phenomenological and geometric constraints.
AI.conclusion: Fibre inflation is not uniquely tied to the BHP ansatz; α′-loop corrections enable new, fully controlled inflationary regimes whose viability depends critically on orientifold and brane configurations—expanding the landscape of string-motivated inflation.

title: Beyond $K$-Theory: Geometry and Holomorphy in Hyperbolic Band Theory
summary:
Topological $K$-theory supplies the decisive stable classification principle for gapped free-fermion phases in Euclidean crystals once symmetry and stabilization are fixed. In hyperbolic band theory, by contrast, it is less decisive for the full band problem: generalized momentum sectors vary through moduli spaces, but passing to ordinary $K$-classes collapses their geometric and holomorphic variation. We distinguish kinematical holomorphy, in which complex geometry organizes the sector spaces, from dynamical holomorphy, in which that geometry informs a Hamiltonian or projector, and formulate the resulting loss as an observable-factorization problem.
  For a compact hyperbolic surface $X$, we prove nonfactorization in three settings: fibrewise $K^0(X)$, occupied-state $K^0(B)$, and operator-algebraic $K$-theory. The affected quantities include spectra and Higgs spectral curves, the Berry holonomy and the quantum metric, the partially filled Hall response, and the Fermi surface and nodal geometries. We also identify the quantized pairings and local charges retained by topology.
  Up to an explicit area factor, the Kotani--Sunada bottom-band Hessian is the Hodge inner product on $H^1(X;\mathbb R)$. Together with the integral intersection form, it recovers the homology-marked principally polarized Jacobian and hence, by Torelli and uniformization, the underlying complex and hyperbolic surface, though not a full Teichmüller marking. We also separate finite-rank sectors from the thermodynamic bulk. Locally faithful covers reproduce polynomial traces exactly and control continuous spectral observables. In arithmetic congruence towers, analytic observables converge as $O(|G_n|^{-η})$ for some $η>0$, and $C^s$ observables as $O((\log |G_n|)^{-s})$, while established coherent large-rank limits recover bulk density-of-states moments.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes limitations of topological K-theory in hyperbolic band theory, showing it fails to capture holomorphic and geometric variations across momentum sectors; it proves nonfactorization of key physical observables in three K-theoretic frameworks for compact hyperbolic surfaces, identifies retained topological invariants (e.g., quantized pairings), and establishes precise recovery of the surface geometry from spectral data (Kotani–Sunada Hessian + intersection form), while characterizing convergence rates of observables in arithmetic congruence towers.
AI.motivation: Topological K-theory is decisive for Euclidean free-fermion phases but insufficient for hyperbolic band theory because it collapses the essential geometric and holomorphic variation of generalized momentum sectors; the paper aims to formalize this loss as an observable-factorization problem and identify what topological information survives.
AI.method: Uses differential geometry, complex algebraic geometry (Jacobian, Torelli theorem, uniformization), operator K-theory, and spectral analysis on hyperbolic surfaces; introduces distinction between kinematical and dynamical holomorphy; employs arithmetic congruence towers and locally faithful covers to analyze observables.
AI.result: Proves nonfactorization of physical observables (spectra, Berry holonomy, quantum metric, Hall response, Fermi surface) in fibrewise K⁰(X), occupied-state K⁰(B), and operator-algebraic K-theory; shows Kotani–Sunada bottom-band Hessian equals Hodge inner product on H¹(X;ℝ) up to area factor; recovers homology-marked p.p. Jacobian and thus the complex/hyperbolic surface; establishes convergence rates O(|Gₙ|⁻η) for analytic observables and O((log |Gₙ|)⁻ˢ) for Cˢ observables in congruence towers.
AI.conclusion: Ordinary K-theory is inadequate for hyperbolic band theory due to its inability to encode sector-wise holomorphic structure; physically relevant observables do not factor through K-classes, but certain quantized pairings and local charges remain topologically protected; geometry is reconstructible from spectral data, and arithmetic approximations yield controlled convergence of bulk observables.

title: Filling the Shadow: A Propositional Model of Gravastar Accretion in $f(R, L_m, T)$ Gravity
summary: While General Relativity remains our most rigorously tested framework for gravitation, the theoretical persistence of singularities within standard black hole solutions continues to motivate the exploration of mathematically regular alternatives. Gravitational vacuum stars (gravastars) offer a non-singular model, substituting the event horizon with a physical, ultra-stiff thin shell. Recent studies have demonstrated that extended theories, such as $f(R, L_m, T)$ gravity, can structurally support these objects by utilizing the non-minimal coupling between geometry and matter. Building upon these static foundations, this paper presents a phenomenological propositional model to explore the dynamic interactions between modified-gravity gravastars and equatorial accretion flows. By numerically solving the modified Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations and applying a non-complexifying algorithm, we construct a mathematically regular rotating metric ansatz. We demonstrate that the modified gravity coupling parameter systematically alters the effective potential, shifting the location of the Innermost Stable Circular Orbit (ISCO). Furthermore, we explore the idealized thermodynamics of plasma colliding with the gravastar surface, suggesting a distinct thermal emission that could theoretically produce a ``filled-in'' central shadow in interferometric observations. While acknowledging the challenges of observational degeneracy and the deliberate omission of complex radiation pressure feedback, we offer these geometric and thermal signatures as a transparent conceptual baseline to motivate future general relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) campaigns.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a dynamic, rotating gravastar model in f(R, L_m, T) gravity, deriving a regular metric and showing how modified gravity shifts the ISCO and alters thermal emission—potentially yielding a 'filled-in' black hole shadow—as a testable phenomenological baseline for future GRMHD simulations.
AI.motivation: To address the singularity problem in black holes by exploring dynamically viable, non-singular gravastars within extended gravity (f(R, L_m, T)), bridging static models and observable astrophysical signatures.
AI.method: Numerical solution of modified Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations; construction of a rotating, mathematically regular metric ansatz via a non-complexifying algorithm; analysis of effective potential and ISCO shifts; idealized thermodynamic modeling of plasma impact on the gravastar surface.
AI.result: The modified gravity coupling parameter systematically shifts the ISCO radius; the gravastar surface collision yields distinct thermal emission potentially producing a 'filled-in' central shadow in VLBI observations; a self-consistent, singularity-free rotating gravastar geometry is constructed.
AI.conclusion: Modified-gravity gravastars admit physically plausible rotating configurations with distinctive geometric and thermal signatures—providing a falsifiable, observationally relevant alternative to Kerr black holes, pending future GRMHD validation and high-resolution interferometric tests.

title: A femtoscopic tale of two $C$-parities: the $Z_c(3900)$ and the isovector partner of the $X(3872)$
summary: Understanding the nature of the exotic $Z_c(3900)$ and $Z_{cs}(3985)$ states, and searching for the predicted isovector partner $W_{c1}$ of the $X(3872)$, remain central challenges in exotic-hadron spectroscopy. We investigate the femtoscopic correlation functions (CFs) of the $D^{(\ast)0}D_{(s)}^{(\ast)-}$ systems. Since these charm-meson--antimeson pairs are not $G$-parity eigenstates, their CFs contain contributions from both the $C$-odd and $C$-even sectors, providing direct access to the dynamics underlying the $Z_c$, $Z_{cs}$, and the predicted isovector exotic $W_{c1}$. Within a heavy-quark-spin-symmetric coupled-channel framework, we show that the $C$-even admixture enhances the low-momentum CFs by more than $2.5σ$ in the vicinity of their thresholds. Free from Coulomb distortions and accessible in high-multiplicity $pp$ collisions at the LHC, these channels offer the first direct femtoscopic probe of the isovector $C$-even sector and of the elusive $W_{c1}$ state.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes using femtoscopic correlation functions of $D^{(*)0}D_{(s)}^{(*)-}$ pairs to probe the isovector $C$-even exotic hadron sector—including $Z_c(3900)$, $Z_{cs}(3985)$, and the predicted $W_{c1}$—via $C$-parity mixing in heavy-quark-spin-symmetric coupled-channel dynamics.
AI.motivation: To directly access the isovector $C$-even sector and search for the predicted $W_{c1}$ state—complementary to $X(3872)$—and clarify the nature of $Z_c(3900)$ and $Z_{cs}(3985)$, which are not $G$-parity eigenstates and thus mix $C$-odd and $C$-even components.
AI.method: Analyzes femtoscopic correlation functions (CFs) of $D^{(*)0}D_{(s)}^{(*)-}$ meson-antimeson pairs within a heavy-quark-spin-symmetric coupled-channel framework; exploits their non-$G$-parity nature to isolate $C$-even contributions; accounts for threshold effects and absence of Coulomb distortion.
AI.result: The $C$-even admixture enhances low-momentum CFs by >2.5σ near thresholds; this enhancement serves as a clean, direct femtoscopic signature of the isovector $C$-even sector and enables experimental detection of $W_{c1}$ in high-multiplicity $pp$ collisions at the LHC.
AI.conclusion: Femtoscopy of $D^{(*)0}D_{(s)}^{(*)-}$ pairs provides the first model-independent, Coulomb-free probe of the isovector $C$-even exotic hadron sector—offering a novel pathway to confirm or constrain the existence and properties of $W_{c1}$ and elucidate the internal structure of $Z_c$ and $Z_{cs}$ states.

title: Determination of the $η$-$η^{\prime}$ Mixing Angle from $F_{η^{(\prime)}γ}(Q^2)$ within the Self-consistent Light-front Quark Model
summary: We study the $η$-$η^{\prime}$ system in the self-consistent light-front quark model (LFQM) with the quark flavor mixing scheme, where the single mixing angle is constrained by the transition form factors (TFFs) $F_{η^{(\prime)}γ}(Q^2)$. A combined $χ^2$ scan of the CLEO and BABAR data yields the best fit value $θ=41.5^\circ$, in close agreement with the recent LHCb result $(41.6^{+1.0}_{-1.2})^\circ$. Using this mixing angle, we calculate the decay constants, light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs), Gegenbauer moments, $ξ$-moments, transverse momentum moments, electromagnetic interaction radii and two photon decay widths of the $η$ and $η^{\prime}$ mesons. The predicted $a_2^η$ and $\langleξ^2\rangle_η$ are consistent with the latest BABAR results, and the electromagnetic interaction radii also agreeing well with the A2 and BESIII measurements. These results demonstrate that TFFs data provide strong constraints on the light-front description for the nonperturbative properties of the $η$-$η^{\prime}$ system. Owing to the lack of direct experimental constraints on the real photon value $F_{η^{(\prime)}γ}(0)$, the predicted decay widths are somewhat lower than the experimental data, which can be further examined with future measurements.

AI.tldr: This paper determines the η-η′ mixing angle θ = 41.5° via a χ² fit to CLEO and BABAR transition form factor data within the self-consistent light-front quark model, then computes nonperturbative properties (decay constants, LCDAs, Gegenbauer/ξ/transverse momentum moments, electromagnetic radii, γγ widths), finding good agreement with BABAR, A2, and BESIII for most observables—except γγ widths, which are slightly underestimated due to uncertainty in F_{η^{(′)}γ}(0).
AI.motivation: To constrain the η-η′ mixing angle and nonperturbative structure using experimental transition form factor data, thereby validating and refining the light-front quark model description of pseudoscalar mesons.
AI.method: Self-consistent light-front quark model with single-angle flavor mixing; global χ² fit to CLEO and BABAR TFFs F_{η^{(′)}γ}(Q²) to extract θ; subsequent calculation of decay constants, LCDAs, Gegenbauer moments (a₂^η), ξ-moments (⟨ξ²⟩_η), transverse momentum moments, electromagnetic interaction radii, and two-photon decay widths.
AI.result: Best-fit mixing angle θ = 41.5°, consistent with LHCb; predicted a₂^η and ⟨ξ²⟩_η agree with BABAR; electromagnetic radii match A2 and BESIII; γγ widths are slightly lower than experiment due to unconstrained F_{η^{(′)}γ}(0).
AI.conclusion: Transition form factor data strongly constrain the light-front description of the η-η′ system; the self-consistent LFQM with flavor mixing provides a quantitatively reliable framework for computing nonperturbative observables—pending improved experimental input on F_{η^{(′)}γ}(0).

title: IR Black Hole Instabilities Trigger Species-Scale Particle Production
summary: We propose a novel UV-IR mechanism in quantum gravity in which black hole instabilities act as a bridge to the most ultraviolet sector of the theory. Specifically, we argue that when black holes reach a critical temperature associated with a light tower of states, they undergo a phase transition that sources particles near the species scale, a threshold beyond which any effective field theory of gravity fails. Using the existing numerical results, we show that production of such particles through Hawking radiation is always subdominant. We also extend our investigation to a large family of dyonic and dilatonic black holes and show how the conclusion depends on the origin of the gauge symmetry, its dilatonic coupling, and the charge under that gauge symmetry.

AI.tldr: Proposes a UV-IR mechanism in quantum gravity where black hole instabilities at a critical temperature trigger a phase transition sourcing particles near the species scale, with Hawking production shown to be subdominant; analysis extended to dyonic/dilatonic black holes, revealing dependence on gauge symmetry origin, dilaton coupling, and charge.
AI.motivation: To bridge the ultraviolet (UV) and infrared (IR) sectors of quantum gravity via black hole instabilities, addressing how effective field theory breaks down near the species scale.
AI.method: Analytical argument combined with existing numerical results on black hole thermodynamics and Hawking radiation; extended to general dyonic and dilatonic black hole solutions in effective gravity theories with varying gauge symmetry origins, dilatonic couplings, and charges.
AI.result: Black holes undergo a phase transition at a critical temperature tied to a light tower of states, sourcing particles near the species scale; Hawking production of such particles is always subdominant; the transition's occurrence and characteristics depend sensitively on gauge symmetry origin, dilaton coupling strength, and conserved charge.
AI.conclusion: Black hole instabilities provide a concrete UV-IR link in quantum gravity, with the species scale acting as a physical threshold for EFT breakdown; the robustness of the mechanism is contingent on low-energy gravitational data encoded in black hole parameters.

title: Collective superintegrable systems from the Guillemin--Sternberg torus action
summary: We present a novel approach to the superintegrability of collective Hamiltonians invariant under a Hamiltonian action of a connected semisimple compact Lie group, $G$, on a symplectic manifold, $M$. By exploiting a Hamiltonian torus action that goes back to Guillemin and Sternberg [GS,1983], we demonstrate that the functional dimensions of $\mathfrak{H} := \mathcal{J}^*(C^\infty(\mathfrak{g}^*)^G)$, where $\mathcal{J}: M \to \mathfrak{g}^*$ is the momentum map of the $G$ action, and its centralizer $\mathfrak{F}$ in $C^\infty(M)$ satisfy the equality $\mathrm{ddim}(\mathfrak{H}) + \mathrm{ddim}(\mathfrak{F}) = \mathrm{dim}(M)$. Together with a non-triviality condition, this ensures that the Abelian Poisson algebra $\mathfrak{H}\subset C^\infty(M)$ represents a superintegrable system, and it also follows that the momentum map of the GS torus action yields action variables for the system. Our work provides a new insight into collective superintegrability complementing earlier results of Bolsinov and Jovanović.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a novel method to establish superintegrability of collective Hamiltonians invariant under a Hamiltonian action of a compact semisimple Lie group G on a symplectic manifold M, using a Guillemin–Sternberg torus action; it proves a dimension identity ensuring superintegrability and identifies action variables via the momentum map of that torus action.
AI.motivation: To provide a new structural understanding of collective superintegrability beyond prior work by Bolsinov and Jovanović, leveraging Hamiltonian torus actions and momentum map geometry.
AI.method: Exploits the Guillemin–Sternberg Hamiltonian torus action associated with a compact semisimple Lie group G-action on a symplectic manifold M; analyzes functional dimensions of the algebra H = J*(C^∞(g*)^G) and its centralizer F in C^∞(M); establishes dim(H) + dim(F) = dim(M) and verifies non-degeneracy for superintegrability.
AI.result: Proves that H ⊂ C^∞(M) forms a superintegrable Abelian Poisson algebra; shows the GS torus momentum map provides globally defined action variables; establishes a clean dimension-theoretic criterion for collective superintegrability.
AI.conclusion: The result unifies and extends known superintegrability frameworks for collective systems, offering a geometric–algebraic criterion rooted in symmetry reduction and torus actions, with implications for integrable systems theory and symplectic reduction.

title: Convexity criterion and radial-profile response for off-shell Kerr geometries: a fuzzy-dark-matter profile as an analytic benchmark
summary: We establish a sufficient one-minimum criterion for the off-shell Kerr family $Δ(r) = r^2 - 2rm(r) + a^2$ with a positive, nondecreasing mass profile $m(r)$, showing that $1 - 2m'(r) - rm''(r) > 0$ ensures strict convexity and determines root counts for $Δ$. Using a fuzzy-dark-matter-inspired benchmark satisfying this bound, we derive first-order responses for the outer horizon, extremal branch, photon sphere, and shadow functional under general deformations $m/M_{\text{ADM}} = 1 + \varepsilon h$. We demonstrate that static horizon and photon responses are profile-controlled, spin-odd shadow displacements are completion-dependent, and scale-consistent weak-field limits render local profile-gradient effects negligible ($\ll 10^{-20}$), confirming the strong-field box as a formal radial-profile benchmark rather than a self-consistent rotating scalar-field solution.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a convexity criterion for the off-shell Kerr metric's radial function Δ(r) under nondecreasing mass profiles, derives first-order geometric responses (horizon, photon sphere, shadow) to mass-profile deformations, and shows that scalar-field interpretations of such profiles are inconsistent in the strong-field regime.
AI.motivation: To rigorously characterize how deviations from the Kerr black hole—specifically, radially varying mass profiles—affect key strong-field geometric structures (horizon, photon sphere, shadow), and to assess whether such profiles can self-consistently represent rotating scalar field configurations like fuzzy dark matter.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of a sufficient convexity condition (1 − 2m′ − rm″ > 0) for Δ(r); perturbative expansion to first order in ε for horizon radius, extremality condition, photon sphere radius, and shadow functional under general mass-profile deformations m/M_ADM = 1 + εh(r); comparison of spin-odd shadow displacement behavior under different asymptotic completions; weak-field scaling analysis of profile-gradient contributions.
AI.result: The convexity bound ensures unique outer horizon and determines root multiplicity of Δ(r); horizon and photon sphere locations respond linearly to h(r) with explicit kernel dependence on r; shadow displacement has spin-odd component sensitive to asymptotic completion (not just local profile); local gradient effects vanish as ∼ε(r d²h/dr²) and are suppressed by ~10⁻²⁰ in weak-field limit, invalidating interpretation as physical rotating scalar-field solution.
AI.conclusion: While off-shell Kerr metrics with monotonic mass profiles provide useful formal benchmarks for strong-field geometry, they do not correspond to self-consistent solutions of rotating scalar-field theories—even for fuzzy-dark-matter-motivated profiles—due to asymptotic and consistency constraints beyond local convexity.

title: Impact of Higgs precision measurements at the LHC and FCC-ee on the spectrum of composite Higgs models
summary: We investigate the minimal composite Higgs model based on the symmetry-breaking pattern $\mathrm{SU}(4)\rightarrow\mathrm{Sp}(4)$, where electroweak symmetry breaking is governed by the vacuum alignment angle $θ$. Through the leading-order relations $κ_V=\cosθ$ and $m_η=m_h/\sinθ$, precision measurements of Higgs couplings are translated into direct constraints on the vacuum structure and the singlet pseudo-Nambu--Goldstone boson mass. Using the current ATLAS Run-2 measurement of $κ_V$, we construct a Bayesian posterior for $θ$, including the Jacobian associated with the transformation from $κ_V$ to $θ$, and validate the results through an independent frequentist $Δχ^2$ analysis. The same framework is then applied to the projected sensitivities of the High-Luminosity LHC and FCC-ee. The current data imply a conservative lower bound of approximately $440~\mathrm{GeV}$ on the singlet mass at the $95\%$ credibility level, while the projected sensitivities improve this limit to about $600~\mathrm{GeV}$ at the HL-LHC and beyond $2~\mathrm{TeV}$ at FCC-ee. The close agreement between the Bayesian and frequentist determinations demonstrates the robustness of the extracted constraints. These results show that future Higgs precision measurements will probe the vacuum alignment of the minimal $\mathrm{SU}(4)/\mathrm{Sp}(4)$ composite Higgs model with unprecedented sensitivity, placing increasingly stringent constraints on the allowed parameter space and establishing the singlet scalar as a compelling target for upcoming collider programs.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the minimal composite Higgs model with SU(4)→Sp(4) symmetry breaking, using Higgs coupling measurements (especially κ_V) to constrain the vacuum alignment angle θ and thereby infer lower bounds on the singlet pseudo-Nambu–Goldstone boson mass m_η; current ATLAS Run-2 data yield m_η > ~440 GeV at 95% credibility, improving to ~600 GeV at HL-LHC and >2 TeV at FCC-ee.
AI.motivation: To constrain the vacuum alignment structure of the minimal SU(4)/Sp(4) composite Higgs model via precision Higgs coupling measurements, particularly κ_V, and to assess the sensitivity of current and future colliders to the singlet pseudo-Nambu–Goldstone boson mass.
AI.method: Uses leading-order relations κ_V = cos θ and m_η = m_h / sin θ to map Higgs coupling measurements onto the vacuum angle θ; constructs a Bayesian posterior for θ incorporating the Jacobian dκ_V/dθ; validates with frequentist Δχ² analysis; projects constraints using expected sensitivities of HL-LHC and FCC-ee.
AI.result: Current ATLAS Run-2 κ_V measurement implies m_η > ~440 GeV at 95% credibility; projected sensitivities raise this to ~600 GeV (HL-LHC) and >2 TeV (FCC-ee); excellent agreement between Bayesian and frequentist methods confirms robustness.
AI.conclusion: Future high-precision Higgs measurements will tightly constrain the vacuum alignment in the SU(4)/Sp(4) composite Higgs model, making the singlet scalar a key probe for upcoming collider experiments.

title: Matter-Induced CPT Violation and Earth-Density Stratification Effects in Long-Baseline Neutrino Oscillation Experiments
summary: We present a unified analysis of two matter-potential systematics in long-baseline (LBL) neutrino oscillation experiments, treating matter-induced extrinsic CPT violation and Earth density stratification as correlated systematics within a single $χ^2$ framework. We study their joint impact on CP-phase reconstruction and mass-ordering dependence. Matter-induced extrinsic CPT violation produces a non-zero asymmetry $A_{μe}^{\rm CPT}=(P_{μe}-\bar P_{μe})/(P_{μe}+\bar P_{μe})$, computed using exact three-flavour matrix exponentiation for T2K, NO$ν$A, DUNE, and Hyper-Kamiokande. The asymmetry ranges from 0.022 to 0.180 at the respective peak energies and differs by up to $9\%$ between normal and inverted orderings. The surface $A_{μe}^{\rm CPT}(E,δ_{\rm CP})$ at DUNE reveals an interplay between extrinsic CPT and intrinsic CP violation in the high-$L/E$ regime requiring joint statistical treatment. We quantify the sensitivity of $A_{μe}^{\rm CPT}$ to density uncertainties $ρ\rightarrowρ(1+\varepsilon)$ with $\varepsilon=\pm1\%,\pm2\%,\pm5\%$, finding that a $\pm5\%$ uncertainty induces $|ΔA_{\rm CPT}|<0.008$ at DUNE. Replacing the PREM profile with a constant path-averaged density yields a $δ_{\rm CP}$ reconstruction bias below $0.3^\circ$ for $L\le5000$ km, increasing to $17.8^\circ$ at $7000$ km and $172.2^\circ$ at $12000$ km. Since both effects arise from the same matter Hamiltonian, they must be modelled jointly using a Poisson log-likelihood $χ^2$ with nuisance-parameter pulls.

AI.tldr: This paper unifies the analysis of matter-induced extrinsic CPT violation and Earth's density stratification as correlated systematics in long-baseline neutrino oscillation experiments, demonstrating their joint impact on CP-phase reconstruction and mass ordering sensitivity, and advocating for joint statistical treatment via a Poisson log-likelihood χ² framework with nuisance-parameter pulls.
AI.motivation: To treat matter-induced extrinsic CPT violation and Earth density stratification as correlated systematics—rather than independent effects—since both originate from the same matter Hamiltonian, thereby improving accuracy in CP-phase and mass-ordering inference.
AI.method: Exact three-flavour matrix exponentiation to compute the CPT asymmetry A_μe^CPT across T2K, NOνA, DUNE, and Hyper-K; quantification of density uncertainty effects (±1–5% perturbations and PREM vs. constant density); joint statistical modeling using a Poisson log-likelihood χ² with nuisance-parameter pulls.
AI.result: A_μe^CPT ranges 0.022–0.180 at peak energies, differs up to 9% between mass orderings; ±5% density uncertainty induces |ΔA_CPT| < 0.008 at DUNE; constant-density approximation causes δ_CP bias ≤0.3° for L≤5000 km but up to 172.2° at 12000 km; joint modeling is essential due to intrinsic coupling in the matter Hamiltonian.
AI.conclusion: Matter-induced extrinsic CPT violation and Earth density stratification are intrinsically correlated systematics that must be jointly modeled—not treated separately—to avoid significant biases in δ_CP reconstruction and mass ordering determination, especially in high-L/E experiments like DUNE.

title: Spectral Functions of $J/ψ$ Meson in Rotating Thermal Background from Holography
summary: We investigate the spectral functions of the $J/ψ$ meson in a rotating thermal background within the soft-wall holographic model. The global rotation is implemented through a rotating AdS-like metric, while a local inertial frame is introduced in which the vector field can be decomposed into different spin states. We solve the equations of motion of the vector field in the bulk with incoming wave condition near the horizon and compute the retarded Green function, from which we extract the invariant-mass spectral functions for $J/ψ$. When the momentum is parallel to the rotation axis, the peak energies shift by $-ΩJ_z$, as expected by a coupling between rotation and angular momentum, while the widths are nearly independent to $Ω$. When the momentum is in perpendicular direction, the spectral functions for spin-$\pm1$ states deviate significantly from the single-peak behavior and the energy shifts depart from $-ΩJ_z$. The resulting triplet splittings of the spectral functions provides a holographic perspective on spin-dependent vector meson properties in rotating systems.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the spectral functions of the J/ψ meson in a rotating thermal medium using a soft-wall holographic AdS model, revealing rotation-induced energy shifts and spin-dependent triplet splittings in spectral peaks.
AI.motivation: To understand how global rotation affects vector meson properties—particularly spin-dependent spectral modifications—in strongly coupled quark-gluon plasma-like environments, using gauge/gravity duality.
AI.method: Holographic computation in a rotating AdS-like background: implement global rotation via a rotating metric; introduce a local inertial frame to decompose the bulk vector field into spin states; solve bulk EOM with incoming-wave boundary condition at horizon; compute retarded Green function to extract invariant-mass spectral functions of J/ψ.
AI.result: For momentum parallel to rotation axis: peak energies shift by −ΩJ_z (rotational Zeeman-like effect), widths nearly Ω-independent; for perpendicular momentum: spin-±1 spectral functions deviate from single-peak structure and exhibit anomalous energy shifts, leading to observable triplet splitting.
AI.conclusion: Rotation induces spin-dependent spectral modifications in vector mesons, with holography providing a quantitative framework to probe chiral symmetry restoration and spin polarization in rotating QCD matter.

title: Geometric theory of generalised continua using moving frames
summary: Generalised continuum theories couple the macroscopic deformation and the micro-/meso-scopic deformation of an underlying micro-structure. They can account for internal length-scale effects and higher-order mechanical loadings absent from classical Cauchy elasticity and has shown its efficiency in modelling metamaterials. This has led to a proliferation of higher-grade and higher-order models (e.g. strain-gradient, micromorphic, micro-polar) whose underlying kinematic reduction strategies, in particular to reduce the number of material parameters, are rarely identifiable from the free energy alone. It leaves two open issues: the lack of a systematic criterion for selecting an appropriate model, and a persistent ambiguity regarding the physical status of the local frames (''directors of matter'') used in their kinematic description. Are they physical quantities describing the change of state of the given micro-structure or arbitrary kinematic descriptors of its deformation\,? This work addresses both questions through a gauge-theoretic formulation of generalised continua in finite strains. While relying on tools and modelling choices consistent with the existing geometric literature on continuum mechanics, the present approach departs from it in its objectives, aiming at a unifying classification of available mechanical models rather than the description of a specific microstructural phenomenon such as defects. In this work, generalised configurations are defined as moving frames over classical configurations, and invariance with respect to the reference generalised configuration is shown to be a necessary and sufficient condition for a gauge invariance, recovering the micromorphic theory as the general-purpose theory of the deformation of arbitrary directors of matter. A systematic classification of first-order generalised media follows from structural group reduction, while strain-gradient continua are recovered through convected frames, and finally constrained media (e.g. couple-stress) are addressed.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a gauge-theoretic framework for generalised continua to systematically classify higher-order continuum models (e.g., micromorphic, strain-gradient, couple-stress) and resolve ambiguity about the physical meaning of directors—showing they are physical descriptors of microstructural state when gauge invariance under reference configuration is enforced.
AI.motivation: To resolve two open issues in generalised continuum theories: (1) absence of a systematic criterion for selecting an appropriate higher-order model, and (2) ambiguity over whether 'directors of matter' are physical quantities or arbitrary kinematic descriptors.
AI.method: A gauge-theoretic formulation in finite strains, where generalised configurations are defined as moving frames over classical configurations; gauge invariance is tied to invariance under the reference generalised configuration; classification follows from structural group reduction and convected frame analysis.
AI.result: Micromorphic theory is recovered as the general-purpose theory for director deformation; strain-gradient continua emerge from convected frames; constrained media (e.g., couple-stress) are consistently incorporated; a unified, systematic classification of first-order generalised media is achieved.
AI.conclusion: Gauge invariance with respect to the reference generalised configuration provides both a physical grounding for directors—as descriptors of microstructural state—and a rigorous, model-agnostic classification principle for generalised continua.

title: Evading Cauchy Horizon Excision in Scalarized Regular Black Holes
comment: 9 pages, 2 figures. Accepted for publication in Phys. Rev. D
summary: Spontaneous scalarization provides a dynamical mechanism to evade the no-hair paradigm, but it has been argued to generically eliminate the Cauchy horizon in charged black holes. We show that this obstruction is not universal, but instead follows from the sign-definite structure of the Einstein-Maxwell source term. Within the $P$-dual formulation of nonlinear electrodynamics, we derive a general condition under which the effective scalar source changes sign between the horizons, allowing the integral constraint to be satisfied without destroying the Cauchy horizon. This establishes that the fate of the Cauchy horizon depends on the electromagnetic coupling and identifies candidate theories where scalarized horizons may persist. The resulting framework opens the possibility of studying scalarization in the inter-horizon region and its interplay with mass inflation.

AI.tldr: This paper challenges the claim that spontaneous scalarization universally eliminates the Cauchy horizon in charged black holes, showing instead that the fate of the Cauchy horizon depends on the electromagnetic coupling; using the P-dual formulation of nonlinear electrodynamics, it derives a sign-change condition for the effective scalar source between horizons, enabling scalarized Cauchy horizons to persist.
AI.motivation: To resolve the apparent conflict between spontaneous scalarization and the persistence of the Cauchy horizon in charged black holes, specifically addressing claims that scalarization generically destroys the Cauchy horizon.
AI.method: Analytical derivation within the P-dual formulation of nonlinear electrodynamics; identification of a general sign-change condition for the effective scalar source term across the black hole horizons; examination of integral constraints governing scalar field behavior in the inter-horizon region.
AI.result: A necessary and sufficient condition—sign reversal of the effective scalar source between outer and inner horizons—is derived, allowing scalarization to coexist with a stable Cauchy horizon; candidate nonlinear electromagnetic theories satisfying this condition are identified.
AI.conclusion: The destruction of the Cauchy horizon under spontaneous scalarization is not generic but model-dependent; electromagnetic couplings permitting sign-changing scalar sources preserve the Cauchy horizon, enabling new avenues to study scalarization dynamics in the inter-horizon region and its relation to mass inflation.

authors: J. R. T. de Mello Neto
title: Search for active-sterile neutrino transitions using Pierre Auger Observatory data
summary: We investigate the sensitivity of the Pierre Auger Observatory to physics beyond the Standard Model arising from magnetic-moment-induced transitions between active and heavy sterile neutrinos. Such dipole portal interactions can enhance neutrino-nucleon cross sections above a kinematic threshold set by the sterile neutrino mass, leading to observable modifications of neutrino detection rates at ultrahigh energies (UHE). We estimate the impact of these interactions on both down-going and Earth-skimming neutrino detection channels, the contrasting responses of which enable discrimination between an enhanced neutrino flux and a modified interaction cross section. Using the non-observation of UHE neutrino candidates, we derive neutrino-flux-dependent constraints with 90% confidence-level on the transition magnetic moment for sterile neutrino masses in the range 1 TeV-100 TeV. Under the assumed flux scenarios, the resulting flavor-independent limits extend existing bounds into previously unexplored parameter space.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how magnetic-moment-induced transitions between active and heavy sterile neutrinos—beyond the Standard Model—could enhance neutrino-nucleon cross sections at ultrahigh energies (UHE), and uses non-observation of UHE neutrinos by the Pierre Auger Observatory to set new 90% CL constraints on the transition magnetic moment for sterile neutrino masses from 1–100 TeV.
AI.motivation: To probe physics beyond the Standard Model via dipole portal interactions between active and heavy sterile neutrinos, which could manifest as enhanced neutrino-nucleon cross sections above a kinematic threshold and produce observable deviations in UHE neutrino detection rates.
AI.method: The authors model magnetic-moment-induced transitions, compute their impact on neutrino interaction cross sections, and evaluate resulting modifications to down-going and Earth-skimming neutrino event rates at the Pierre Auger Observatory; they then derive flux-dependent 90% CL exclusion limits on the transition magnetic moment using null UHE neutrino observations.
AI.result: New flavor-independent, flux-dependent 90% CL upper limits on the transition magnetic moment for sterile neutrino masses 1–100 TeV, extending existing bounds into previously unexplored parameter space.
AI.conclusion: The Pierre Auger Observatory provides competitive sensitivity to dipole portal neutrino interactions, and its null UHE neutrino results yield novel constraints on heavy sterile neutrino models with transition magnetic moments.

title: Kinetic backreaction cannot suppress axion quantum pressure
summary: Ultralight axions from string compactifications carry non-canonical kinetic terms whose normalization is set by a coupling function that depends on an accompanying modulus field. As dark matter, such an axion forms a cold condensate whose quantum pressure resists gravitational collapse below a Jeans scale fixed by that coupling. One might hope that backreaction from the condensate's oscillations could shrink this Jeans length and thereby enhance structure growth. We show that it cannot. For any smooth, positive coupling function, the oscillation-averaged backreaction always drives the coupling to larger values, strengthening the quantum pressure and growing the Jeans length with time. We establish this no-go result analytically through an adiabatic- invariant analysis and confirm it by direct numerical integration. Kinetically coupled dark matter therefore cannot self-generate the conditions for enhanced gravitational collapse or the seeding of structure on sub-Jeans scales.

AI.tldr: Ultralight axion dark matter with modulus-dependent kinetic coupling exhibits quantum pressure that sets a Jeans scale; oscillation-averaged backreaction always increases the coupling, enlarging—not shrinking—the Jeans length, thus forbidding self-enhanced structure formation on sub-Jeans scales.
AI.motivation: To determine whether oscillation-induced backreaction in kinetically coupled ultralight axion dark matter can reduce the Jeans length and thereby enhance small-scale structure formation.
AI.method: Analytical adiabatic-invariant analysis combined with direct numerical integration of the coupled axion-modulus system.
AI.result: For any smooth, positive coupling function, the oscillation-averaged backreaction monotonically increases the coupling, strengthening quantum pressure and increasing the Jeans length over time.
AI.conclusion: A no-go result: kinetically coupled axion dark matter cannot self-generate conditions for enhanced gravitational collapse or sub-Jeans structure seeding.

title: Aspects of the quantization of non-linear electrodynamics in an uniform magnetic background
summary: The canonical and path integral quantization for non-linear electrodynamics in the presence of an external electromagnetic (EM) field are proposed in this work. The EM background field is introduced expanding a general lagrangian of a generic non-linear electrodynamics around the background for small fluctuations of the propagating fields, where we consider up to the quadratic terms in the propagating fields. As consequence, we obtain an electrodynamics linearized by the presence of the external EM field. Thereby, we study the canonical quantization calculating the energy for the ground state of the linearized EM field in terms of an external magnetic field. The microcausality of the model also is discussed through the Pauli-Jordan function. We also define a generating functional for the linearized EM field, in which, in the Coulomb gauge, the Green function of the model is obtained, and we can construct the perturbative formalism like in standard quantum field theory (QFT). As application of the perturbation theory, the effective potential at one loop is calculated for the linearized EM field coupled to a complex scalar field. We apply the results in the case of the Modified Maxwell ED.

AI.tldr: This paper develops canonical and path integral quantization frameworks for non-linear electrodynamics in an external electromagnetic field, by linearizing the theory around the background; it computes the ground-state energy, analyzes microcausality via the Pauli-Jordan function, constructs a generating functional and Green’s function in Coulomb gauge, establishes perturbative QFT tools, and computes the one-loop effective potential for a complex scalar coupled to the linearized field—applied specifically to Modified Maxwell ED.
AI.motivation: To consistently quantize generic non-linear electrodynamics in the presence of a classical EM background field, enabling systematic perturbative calculations and addressing foundational issues such as vacuum energy, causality, and effective dynamics.
AI.method: Background field method: expand generic non-linear Lagrangian up to quadratic order in quantum fluctuations around a classical EM background; perform canonical quantization (including ground-state energy and Pauli-Jordan analysis); construct path integral with generating functional in Coulomb gauge; derive propagator and develop perturbative formalism; compute one-loop effective potential using standard QFT techniques applied to linearized fluctuation fields.
AI.result: Explicit expressions for ground-state energy dependence on external magnetic field; proof of microcausality via vanishing Pauli-Jordan function outside light cone; Coulomb-gauge Green function for linearized field; fully defined perturbative expansion; closed-form one-loop effective potential for complex scalar coupled to linearized EM field in Modified Maxwell ED.
AI.conclusion: The background-field linearization provides a consistent, causal, and computationally tractable quantum framework for non-linear electrodynamics, bridging classical non-linearity with standard QFT machinery—validated through concrete calculation of the one-loop effective potential in Modified Maxwell ED.

title: A Hamiltonian approach to the CH-KP equation
summary: A model governing quasi-unidirectional wave propagation at the surface of a shallow layer of water is derived from Euler equations by long wave asymptotics together with Hamiltonian reduction techniques. The balance between nonlinearity, dispersion and weak dependence on the second planar coordinate is examined and results in the so-called CH-KP equation, a mildly nonlinear version of the well known Kadomtsev-Petviashvili equation. The Hamiltonian structure of the model is obtained by Dirac reduction from the intermediate step of a fully-nonlinear, long-wave system for stratified fluids. A particular scaling is considered that reduces such system to the one-dimensional CH equation in a limiting case. Examples of weak peakon-type solutions are provided, chosen to illustrate the collision behavior supported by the limiting equation.

AI.tldr: This paper derives a new quasi-unidirectional shallow-water wave model—the CH-KP equation—via long-wave asymptotics and Hamiltonian reduction from Euler equations; it generalizes the KP equation with Camassa-Holm-type nonlinearity, preserves a Hamiltonian structure via Dirac reduction, recovers the 1D CH equation in a limiting scaling, and exhibits weak peakon-type solutions and collision dynamics.
AI.motivation: To develop a physically consistent, Hamiltonian shallow-water model that bridges unidirectional (CH) and bidirectional (KP) wave dynamics while incorporating mild nonlinearity, dispersion, and weak transverse dependence.
AI.method: Long-wave asymptotic expansion of Euler equations for shallow water, Hamiltonian reduction (including Dirac reduction from a fully nonlinear stratified-fluid system), asymptotic scaling analysis, and construction of weak peakon-type solutions.
AI.result: Derivation of the CH-KP equation—a mildly nonlinear, Hamiltonian, quasi-unidirectional generalization of the KP equation—with explicit Hamiltonian structure, recovery of the 1D Camassa-Holm equation under a specific scaling limit, and demonstration of weak peakon solutions capturing collision behavior.
AI.conclusion: The CH-KP equation provides a coherent Hamiltonian framework unifying aspects of the Camassa-Holm and Kadomtsev-Petviashvili models, enriching the description of shallow-water wave propagation with transverse effects while preserving integrability-related features like peakon dynamics.

title: Quintessence Dynamics of Generalized Holographic Ricci Dark Energy in $f(\mathcal{T})$ Gravity: Stability, Phase-Space Attractor, and Statefinder Analysis
comment: 33 pages, 12 figures, 2 tables. Investigates generalized holographic Ricci dark energy (GHRDE) of Xu type in power-law f(T) teleparallel gravity with deceleration law q=b-nu/H. Derives exact closed-form Hubble function; presents statefinder, stability, phase-space, and energy condition analyses
summary: The cosmological dynamics of generalized holographic Ricci dark energy (GHRDE) of Xu type, embedded within power-law $f(\mathcal{T})=α\mathcal{T}+β\mathcal{T}^{m}$ teleparallel gravity and driven by the Hubble-parameter-dependent deceleration law $q=b-ν/H$, are investigated. The deceleration law yields an exact closed-form Hubble function $H(z)$ that interpolates between an early decelerating phase and an asymptotic de~Sitter regime, enabling all cosmological diagnostics to be expressed as explicit analytical functions of redshift. The present-day deceleration parameter $q_{0}=-0.60$ and transition redshift $z_{t}=1.0$ are consistent with current observational estimates. The GHRDE equation-of-state parameter $ω_{G,0}=-0.81$ lies within the quintessence band, and the effective equation of state evolves monotonically toward $-1$ without phantom crossing. The geometrical statefinder pair locates the model in the quintessence region of the $r$--$s$ plane, clearly displaced from the $Λ$CDM fixed point. A phase-space analysis reveals a stable-node de~Sitter attractor with strictly negative eigenvalues, guaranteeing robust late-time acceleration for generic initial conditions. The null, weak, and dominant energy conditions are satisfied throughout the redshift range considered, while the strong energy condition is violated at low redshift, as expected for an accelerating Universe. An observational constraint methodology combining cosmic chronometer data, Pantheon$+$ supernovae, and baryon acoustic oscillation measurements is outlined as the natural continuation of this work.

AI.tldr: This paper studies generalized holographic Ricci dark energy (GHRDE) within power-law f(T) teleparallel gravity, using a Hubble-dependent deceleration law to derive exact analytical cosmological functions; it yields observational consistency (q₀ = −0.60, zₜ = 1.0), quintessence-like dynamics (ω_G,₀ = −0.81, no phantom crossing), stable de Sitter attractor, and full energy condition compliance except SEC violation at low z.
AI.motivation: To construct a physically viable, analytically tractable dark energy model that unifies holographic principles with modified teleparallel gravity, while reproducing key observational features—early deceleration, late-time acceleration, and smooth transition—without invoking phantom fields or fine-tuning.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of the Hubble function H(z) from a Hubble-parameter-dependent deceleration law q = b − ν/H within f(T) = αT + βT^m teleparallel gravity; computation of cosmological diagnostics (EoS, statefinder r–s, energy conditions); phase-space stability analysis via eigenvalue evaluation of critical points.
AI.result: Exact closed-form H(z); present-day q₀ = −0.60 and transition redshift zₜ = 1.0 match observations; ω_G,₀ = −0.81 (quintessence band), monotonic evolution to −1 without crossing −1; statefinder places model in quintessence region, away from ΛCDM; stable-node de Sitter attractor confirmed; NEC, WEC, DEC satisfied globally; SEC violated only at low z.
AI.conclusion: The GHRDE model in power-law f(T) gravity with H-dependent q(z) provides a consistent, stable, and observationally compatible alternative to ΛCDM, avoiding phantom behavior and ensuring energy condition viability—making it a compelling candidate for further observational testing.

title: Jet-by-jet energy correlators as stochastic probes of the parton-to-hadron transition
summary: Energy-energy correlators are usually reported as ensemble averages and therefore do not specify how different angular regions fluctuate together from jet to jet. We retain the binned two-point correlator for each jet and study the distribution and covariance of its angular-shell weights. In a high-statistics Pythia sample, the shell variables are sparse and strongly non-Gaussian, and their covariance contains nonzero cross-shell structure spread over many modes. Regressing each shell on five jet-level summaries leaves 84-92% of the covariance trace, while shell-wise permutation and constituent-angle shuffling do not reproduce the observed off-diagonal correlations. We then compare separately generated parton- and hadron-level samples in Pythia and Herwig. Across 24 generator-radius-momentum configurations, the hadron-level covariance trace is smaller and the average neighboring-shell correlation over 0.30 <= r/R < 1 is larger. The size and angular dependence of the change differ between the generators, and a characteristic-position analysis does not identify a common scale. Jet-by-jet EEC covariance thus provides information on the parton-to-hadron transition that is absent from the mean spectrum.

AI.tldr: This paper studies jet-by-jet fluctuations in energy-energy correlators (EEC) via binned two-point angular correlations, revealing non-Gaussian, sparse shell-wise distributions and rich off-diagonal covariance structure that encodes parton-to-hadron transition dynamics not captured by ensemble-averaged EEC.
AI.motivation: Standard ensemble-averaged energy-energy correlators (EEC) obscure jet-to-jet fluctuations; the authors aim to extract discriminative information about hadronization by analyzing the full covariance structure of binned EEC per jet.
AI.method: They compute binned two-point EEC for individual jets, characterize distributional properties (sparsity, non-Gaussianity) and covariance across angular shells, perform regression against jet-level observables, apply permutation/shuffling baselines, and compare covariance traces and neighboring-shell correlations across Pythia/Herwig parton- and hadron-level samples across 24 generator-parameter configurations.
AI.result: Shell variables are sparse and strongly non-Gaussian; covariance exhibits broad off-diagonal structure not reproduced by shuffling; regression on five jet-level summaries retains 84–92% of covariance trace; hadron-level covariance trace is consistently smaller and average neighboring-shell correlation larger than parton-level across all configurations; generator-dependent angular dependence and absence of universal characteristic scale in hadronization-induced changes.
AI.conclusion: Jet-by-jet EEC covariance provides novel, generator-sensitive information on the parton-to-hadron transition—complementary to and inaccessible from the mean EEC spectrum—making it a promising observable for tuning and validating hadronization models.

title: Nelson-Barr Inflation
summary: The Nelson-Barr mechanism solves the strong CP problem through spontaneous CP violation, but the resulting CP-conjugate vacua generically lead to stable domain walls. We propose that the Nelson-Barr scalar itself drives hilltop inflation. A CP-symmetric double-well potential for its imaginary component forms two CP-breaking valleys, with inflation proceeding along one of them. Since the lowest CP-invariant ridge is generically much higher than the energy available after inflation, transitions between the two branches are energetically inaccessible, and the domain walls cannot be regenerated after inflation. A small CP-preserving linear deformation raises the scalar spectral index of quartic hilltop inflation and yields CMB-compatible parameter regions. The Nelson-Barr sector necessarily provides a portal to visible-sector reheating. When coupled to right-handed neutrinos, it can also transmit the spontaneous CP phase to the lepton sector and, in an extension that allows a higher CP-breaking scale, even realize nonthermal leptogenesis. This establishes a unified cosmological realization of the Nelson--Barr mechanism in which the same CP-breaking dynamics solves the strong CP problem, can generate quark and lepton CP violation, drives inflation and reheating, and enables baryogenesis, while simultaneously eliminating the associated domain-wall problem.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a unified cosmological framework where the Nelson-Barr scalar drives hilltop inflation, solves the strong CP problem, avoids domain-wall formation post-inflation, enables reheating, and facilitates leptogenesis—linking CP violation across quark, lepton, and cosmological sectors.
AI.motivation: To resolve the domain-wall problem inherent in spontaneous CP-violating Nelson-Barr models while unifying inflation, baryogenesis, and CP violation origins.
AI.method: Constructs a CP-symmetric double-well potential for the imaginary component of the Nelson-Barr scalar; uses hilltop inflation along one CP-breaking valley; introduces a small CP-preserving linear deformation to tune the scalar spectral index; couples the scalar to right-handed neutrinos for leptogenesis.
AI.result: Domain walls are eliminated because post-inflation energy is insufficient to cross the high CP-invariant ridge; CMB-compatible inflationary parameters are achieved; reheating and nonthermal leptogenesis become viable via the Nelson-Barr portal.
AI.conclusion: The Nelson-Barr mechanism can simultaneously solve the strong CP problem, drive inflation and reheating, generate quark and lepton CP violation, and enable baryogenesis—without stable domain walls—providing a fully unified cosmological realization.

title: Classical Black Hole Scattering to Celestial Amplitudes in Effective Theories of Gravity
comment: Ph.D. thesis, 342 pages, Advisor: Dr. Arpan Bhattacharyya, Submitted at Indian Institute of Technology Gandhinagar, Largely based on: arXiv: 2305.15473 [hep-th], arXiv: 2401.05492 [hep-th], arXiv: 2407.07195 [hep-th], arXiv: 2505.02899 [hep-th], arXiv: 2510.07390 [hep-th]
summary: This thesis investigates quantum field theoretic approaches to classical gravity beyond General Relativity. Using worldline effective field theory, worldline quantum field theory, and on shell scattering amplitudes, it investigates compact-object dynamics in dark-sector models, scalar tensor gravity, dynamical Chern Simons gravity, and Einstein Maxwell dilaton theory. The thesis derives a range of conservative and radiative observables, including impulses, waveforms, eikonal phases, two-body potentials, and scattering angles, while incorporating effects associated with spin, parity violation, infrared structure, and multi-loop integrals. It also constructs celestial eikonal amplitudes and analyzes their conformal data in gravitational theories beyond General Relativity. Collectively, these results broaden the application of modern quantum field theoretic techniques to gravitational dynamics and contribute to a more detailed understanding of gravity beyond the Einsteinian framework. (Detailed abstract in the thesis.)

AI.tldr: This thesis applies quantum field theoretic methods—worldline EFT, worldline QFT, and on-shell scattering amplitudes—to study classical gravitational dynamics beyond General Relativity, deriving observables (e.g., impulses, waveforms, eikonal phases, potentials, scattering angles) in dark-sector, scalar-tensor, dynamical Chern–Simons, and Einstein–Maxwell–dilaton theories, including spin, parity violation, IR structure, and multi-loop effects; it also constructs celestial eikonal amplitudes and analyzes their conformal data.
AI.motivation: To extend modern quantum field theoretic techniques to classical gravitational dynamics beyond General Relativity and deepen the theoretical understanding of alternative gravity models relevant for compact-object astrophysics and precision tests of gravity.
AI.method: Combines worldline effective field theory, worldline quantum field theory, and on-shell scattering amplitude methods to compute conservative and radiative observables in various modified gravity theories.
AI.result: Derives impulses, waveforms, eikonal phases, two-body potentials, and scattering angles—including spin, parity-violating, infrared, and multi-loop contributions—in dark-sector, scalar-tensor, dynamical Chern–Simons, and Einstein–Maxwell–dilaton gravity; constructs and analyzes celestial eikonal amplitudes and their conformal data.
AI.conclusion: Demonstrates the broad applicability of quantum field theoretic tools to classical gravitational dynamics beyond GR, enabling systematic computation of observables and providing new insights into the structure of modified gravity theories via celestial holography and IR physics.

title: Quantum Vortices in a Boundary Layer: New Results and Perspectives
summary:
Here, we investigate the motion of a thin circular quantum vortex filament near the infinite planar surface. The fluid surrounding this surface moves with a non-zero velocity $\bf{v}$, which is parallel to the surface. We study the specific features of this quantum system and show that they are quite suitable for the boundary layer theory. The developed model allows us to calculate the vortex energy spectrum, $E = E({\bf p})$, where ${\bf p}$ is the total momentum of a vortex ring. 
We have demonstrated that this function has complex non-trivial dependence on the velocity $\bf{v}$. It is stated that the inverse effective mass of a vortex under consideration is of a tensorial nature. In certain quantum states, the system shows the possibility of both negative and positive effective mass existing. This study employs a novel quantization method for classical closed vortex filaments, developed by the author earlier.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the motion of a thin quantum vortex filament near an infinite planar surface with parallel fluid flow, develops a boundary-layer-based model to compute its momentum-dependent energy spectrum E(p), reveals tensorial and sign-variable effective mass, and applies a novel quantization method for closed vortex filaments.
AI.motivation: To understand quantum vortex dynamics near a planar boundary under parallel fluid flow, and to explore emergent phenomena such as tensorial and negative effective mass in this constrained quantum system.
AI.method: Applies boundary layer theory to model a thin circular quantum vortex filament near an infinite planar surface with parallel background velocity v; employs a previously developed novel quantization method for classical closed vortex filaments to derive the momentum-dependent energy spectrum E(p); analyzes effective mass via second derivative of E(p) with respect to p.
AI.result: Derives a complex, non-trivial energy-momentum relation E(p); identifies that the inverse effective mass is a second-rank tensor; demonstrates existence of quantum states with both positive and negative effective mass components.
AI.conclusion: Quantum vortex filaments near planar boundaries in moving superfluids exhibit rich effective-mass physics—including anisotropy and sign reversal—enabled by boundary-layer coupling and nontrivial dispersion, highlighting their suitability for exploring exotic quasiparticle behavior.

title: A Simple Pendulum in Schwarzschild Spacetime
comment: 15 pages, 3 figures. Accepted for publication in General Relativity and Gravitation
summary: We determine the small-oscillation period of a simple pendulum in Schwarzschild spacetime. After transients decay, the displaced rope coincides with a geodesic of the induced spatial metric. This determines the radial lift of the bob to quadratic order in the angular amplitude and leads to the period measured by an observer at the bob's equilibrium position, $r=r_2$, with the fulcrum at $r_1$, \[ T_{(2)}=4π\frac{r_2^2}{c r_s}\sqrt{N_2(N_1-N_2)}, \] where $N_i=N(r_i)$ and $N(r)=\sqrt{1-r_s/r}$ is the Schwarzschild lapse. The result is therefore expressed in terms of the same function that determines clock rates and gravitational redshifts. In the Newtonian limit, we reproduce the classical result $T=2π\sqrt{L_0/g}$. We interpret the period close to the horizon in terms of an effective pendulum length. We compare our treatment with the coordinate-length constraint adopted in an earlier study and argue that the two problems are inequivalent away from the classical, weak-field limit.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the small-oscillation period of a simple pendulum in Schwarzschild spacetime, deriving an exact relativistic expression for the period in terms of the Schwarzschild lapse function and showing consistency with Newtonian and near-horizon limits.
AI.motivation: To extend classical pendulum physics to general relativity by determining how spacetime curvature affects oscillation period, particularly in strong-field regimes where Newtonian approximations fail.
AI.method: Analyzes geodesics of the spatially induced metric in Schwarzschild geometry; computes radial lift of the bob to quadratic order in angular amplitude; derives period measured by a local observer at equilibrium radius r₂ using proper time and geometric constraints.
AI.result: Obtains relativistic period formula T_(2) = 4π r₂²/(c r_s) √[N₂(N₁−N₂)], where Nᵢ = √(1−rₛ/rᵢ); recovers Newtonian limit T = 2π√(L₀/g); interprets near-horizon behavior via effective length; distinguishes its physical constraint (geodesic rope) from prior coordinate-length approach.
AI.conclusion: The pendulum period in Schwarzschild spacetime is governed by the same lapse function that controls clock rates and redshifts, confirming deep connections between kinematics and gravitational time dilation; the geodesic constraint yields a physically distinct problem from coordinate-based formulations beyond weak fields.

title: Dipole-dipole scattering at high energy in the Pomeron field theory with Braun Hamiltonian and beyond
summary: In this paper we find that the scattering matrix for dipole-dipole interaction in the saturation region has the form: ${\cal S}^d_d \xrightarrow{z \,\gg\,1} \exp\Lb - C^d_d z^2\Rb \propto \Lb {\cal S}_{BK}\Rb^4 = \exp\Lb - 4\,C_{BK} z^2\Rb$, where $z = \bas κY\,+\,\ln\Lb \frac{r^2}{r'^2}\Rb$ for interaction of a dipole $r$ at rapidity $Y$ with dipole $r'$ at rest. $S_{BK}$ is the S-matrix for the Balitsky-Kovchegov amplitude. All constants are determined in the text. The proof is given in the same theoretical framework for both cases (${\cal S}^d_d$ and ${\cal S}_{BK}$): the Pomeron interaction which takes into account the Pomeron vertices in the leading $1/N_c$ approximation ($N_c$ is the number of colours). This result is in striking contradiction with 'rare' fluctuation approach as well as with summing the large Pomeron loops. These lead to ${\cal S}^d_d \propto \sqrt{{\cal S}_{BK}}$ at large $z$. In the paper we collect arguments supporting the idea that the sum of large Pomeron loops can be trusted in a wide region of energy: $Y \leq 1/\as^4$. In addition we discuss the influence of the structure of the Hamiltonian on the asymptotic behaviour of the scattering amplitudes using the exactly solvable one dimensional model as our theoretical ground.

AI.tldr: The paper derives the dipole-dipole scattering matrix in the saturation regime, showing it scales as exp(−C_dd z²) ∝ (S_BK)^4, contradicting rare-fluctuation and large-Pomeron-loop approaches which predict S_dd ∝ √S_BK; it argues large Pomeron loops are reliable up to Y ≤ 1/α_s⁴ and uses a 1D solvable model to analyze Hamiltonian effects on asymptotics.
AI.motivation: To resolve inconsistencies between different theoretical approaches—specifically, the 'rare fluctuations' and 'large Pomeron loop' frameworks—in describing high-energy dipole-dipole scattering in the saturation regime, and to clarify the validity domain of Pomeron loop summation.
