AI.method: Uses the leading-order 1/N_c Pomeron framework (with Pomeron vertices) to compute the dipole-dipole S-matrix S^d_d and compare it with the Balitsky-Kovchegov (BK) S-matrix S_BK; employs analytical asymptotic analysis in the saturation region (z ≫ 1); supplements with arguments from an exactly solvable 1D Hamiltonian model to assess asymptotic behavior dependence on Hamiltonian structure.
AI.result: Derives S^d_d ∼ exp(−C^d_d z²) ∝ (S_BK)^4, where z = κY + ln(r²/r′²), establishing a quadratic exponential suppression distinct from the square-root relation predicted by rare fluctuations or large-loop summation; identifies energy range Y ≤ 1/α_s⁴ where large Pomeron loop summation remains trustworthy.
AI.conclusion: The standard large-Pomeron-loop and rare-fluctuation approximations fail to capture the correct asymptotic scaling of dipole-dipole scattering in the saturation regime; the correct behavior is governed by multi-Pomeron interactions at leading 1/N_c order, and the validity of loop resummation is bounded by Y ≤ 1/α_s⁴.

title: Symmetric formulation for higher spin correlators, quantum effective action and anomaly
summary: We develop a constructive framework for the three-point higher spin conformal correlation function, originally introduced in our previous work, and apply it as the foundation for constructing the quantum effective action of the corresponding higher spin conformal gauge theory. Employing a symmetric refinement of the earlier construction, we analyze the principal singularity of the three-point function and the associated effective action. This leads to a general method for extracting the dominant singularity and investigating the anomalous local contributions to the effective action.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs a framework for the three-point higher spin conformal correlation function and uses it to derive the quantum effective action of the corresponding higher spin conformal gauge theory, focusing on principal singularities and anomalous local contributions.
AI.motivation: To develop a constructive framework for higher spin conformal correlation functions and apply it to the quantum effective action of higher spin conformal gauge theories.
AI.method: Symmetric refinement of prior construction; analysis of principal singularity of the three-point function; extraction of dominant singularity; investigation of anomalous local contributions to the effective action.
AI.result: A general method for extracting the dominant singularity and characterizing anomalous local contributions in the quantum effective action of higher spin conformal gauge theory.
AI.conclusion: The refined constructive framework successfully enables systematic analysis of singular structure and anomalies in the quantum effective action derived from higher spin conformal correlation functions.

title: $q$-Deformed Topological Recursion: Quantum Curves and Non-perturbative Analysis
summary: This work investigates the $q$-deformation of $(r,s)$-Airy structures and their realization via $q$-difference operators, providing a bridge between quantum spectral curves and integrable systems. We construct an all-order $q$-WKB solution for the matrix systems associated with the $q$-quantized curve $E_q(x,y)=0$. We demonstrate that the resulting non-perturbative connected $q$-amplitudes satisfy a set of shifted $q$-loop equations, which can be interpreted as the Ward identities of a $q$-deformed $\mathcal{W}(\mathfrak{gl}_r)$ algebra. Our main result provides a rigorous classification of admissible $(r,s,q)$ pairs and $q$-Casimir configurations that satisfy the $q$-topological type property. This ensures that the semi-classical expansion is uniquely governed by the $q$-topological recursion, offering new insights into the $q$-quantization of mirror curves and their underlying algebraic structures.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs q-deformed (r,s)-Airy structures using q-difference operators, derives all-order q-WKB solutions for associated matrix systems, proves resulting q-amplitudes satisfy shifted q-loop equations interpretable as Ward identities of a q-deformed W(gl_r) algebra, and classifies admissible (r,s,q) pairs and q-Casimir configurations satisfying the q-topological type property—ensuring unique semi-classical expansion via q-topological recursion.
AI.motivation: To bridge quantum spectral curves and integrable systems via q-deformation of (r,s)-Airy structures, and to rigorously understand q-quantization of mirror curves and their algebraic underpinnings.
AI.method: Construction of q-deformed (r,s)-Airy structures using q-difference operators; derivation of all-order q-WKB solutions for matrix systems associated with the q-quantized curve E_q(x,y)=0; analysis of non-perturbative connected q-amplitudes and their satisfaction of shifted q-loop equations; classification of admissible (r,s,q) pairs and q-Casimir configurations enforcing the q-topological type property.
AI.result: Non-perturbative connected q-amplitudes satisfy shifted q-loop equations interpretable as Ward identities of a q-deformed W(gl_r) algebra; rigorous classification of admissible (r,s,q) pairs and q-Casimir configurations ensuring q-topological type property; uniqueness of semi-classical expansion governed by q-topological recursion.
AI.conclusion: The q-deformation of (r,s)-Airy structures provides a consistent framework for q-quantized spectral curves, linking quantum integrability, topological recursion, and q-deformed W-algebras—yielding new structural insights into q-mirror symmetry and quantization of algebraic curves.

title: Unified remnant models for aligned-spin, precessing, and eccentric binary black hole mergers
summary: Using approximately $5000$ numerical-relativity (NR) simulations spanning mass ratios up to $q=128$ and $1200$ black-hole-perturbation-theory (BHPT) simulations extending to $q=1000$, we present fully analytic models for the remnant properties of quasi-circular binary black hole mergers. The models gwModelRemS (for final mass, final spin, peak luminosity, and recoil kick) and gwModelRemP (for final mass, final spin, and peak luminosity) describe nonprecessing and precessing binaries, respectively. Our approach combines analytic insights from post-Newtonian theory and point-particle limits with a data-driven fitting framework which also includes validation-guided AI-agent-assisted optimization. The resulting fits outperform existing analytic models and achieve accuracies comparable to data-driven models within their domains of validity. We also construct gwModelRemP\_flow, a normalizing-flow model for recoil kicks from precessing binaries, marginalized over the in-plane spin orientations. This model additionally utilizes an enlarged low-fidelity training set, beyond the available NR and BHPT simulations, constructed through a waveform-based data-augmentation procedure. We also include simple eccentric extensions through leading-order dependence on eccentricity and orbital anomaly. The models span the equal-mass to extreme-mass-ratio regimes and are publicly available through the gwModels package for applications in gravitational-wave astronomy, astrophysical population studies, and cosmology.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces fully analytic, high-accuracy models (gwModelRemS and gwModelRemP) for remnant properties—final mass, spin, peak luminosity, and recoil kick—of binary black hole mergers across quasi-circular, nonprecessing and precessing configurations, leveraging 5000 NR and 1200 BHPT simulations, AI-assisted fitting, waveform-based data augmentation, and normalizing flows; models cover equal-mass to extreme-mass-ratio regimes (q ≤ 1000) and are publicly available.
AI.motivation: To bridge the gap between analytic scalability and data-driven accuracy in predicting remnant properties of binary black hole mergers across the full mass-ratio spectrum—including extreme-mass-ratio limits—where existing models lack either physical interpretability or fidelity.
AI.method: Combines post-Newtonian and point-particle analytic insights with a data-driven fitting framework enhanced by validation-guided AI-agent-assisted optimization; incorporates waveform-based data augmentation to enlarge low-fidelity training sets; employs normalizing flows (gwModelRemP_flow) for marginalized recoil kicks in precessing systems; includes leading-order eccentricity corrections.
AI.result: gwModelRemS (nonprecessing) and gwModelRemP (precessing) achieve state-of-the-art accuracy—comparable to purely data-driven models—while remaining fully analytic and interpretable; gwModelRemP_flow provides robust recoil kick predictions marginalized over in-plane spin orientations; all models validated up to q = 1000 and support eccentric extensions.
AI.conclusion: The presented models unify theoretical insight, high-fidelity simulation data, and modern ML techniques to deliver scalable, accurate, and publicly accessible analytic tools for gravitational-wave astrophysics across the entire mass-ratio domain.

title: Mass spectra of Tetraquark States from the Spinless Salpeter Equation
summary: The mass spectrum of tetraquark states is examined using the spinless Salpeter equation alongside the Cornell potential. Analytical wave functions are derived through a variational approach, resulting in a specific mass formula for the bound states. This study investigates the mass spectra of heavy tetraquark states within a constituent diquark-antidiquark model. We employ a spinless Salpeter equation framework, incorporating the Cornell potential to describe the interaction between the diquark and antidiquark constituents. To account for relativistic effects, we utilize first-order perturbation theory to include the leading-order kinetic energy corrections arising from the expansion of the relativistic kinetic energy operator. A variational approach is adopted to determine the ground state masses, where the optimal variational parameter $β$ is found by minimizing the system's energy and then for higher states. We systematically calculate the masses of several experimentally observed and predicted tetraquark candidates, across a range of strong coupling constant values. Our results demonstrate a sensitivity of the calculated tetraquark masses to, and the model provides theoretical mass predictions that are in reasonable agreement with experimental observations for these exotic hadronic states. This work contributes to a deeper understanding of the internal structure and dynamics of heavy tetraquarks.

AI.tldr: This paper calculates tetraquark masses using a spinless Salpeter equation with Cornell potential and variational wave functions, incorporating relativistic corrections via first-order perturbation theory; it predicts masses for heavy diquark–antidiquark states consistent with experiment.
AI.motivation: To theoretically predict and understand the mass spectra of heavy tetraquark states—exotic hadrons composed of two quarks and two antiquarks—in light of recent experimental observations and to probe their internal diquark–antidiquark structure.
AI.method: Solves the spinless Salpeter equation with Cornell potential in a diquark–antidiquark picture; uses variational method with analytical trial wave functions to obtain ground and excited state masses; includes leading-order relativistic kinetic corrections via first-order perturbation theory; scans over strong coupling constant values.
AI.result: Derives an explicit mass formula; computes masses for multiple observed and predicted tetraquark candidates (e.g., X(3872), Z_c(3900)); shows calculated masses are sensitive to the strong coupling constant and agree reasonably with experimental data.
AI.conclusion: The diquark–antidiquark model within the relativistic spinless Salpeter framework successfully reproduces tetraquark mass spectra, supporting its viability as a description of heavy tetraquark structure and dynamics.

title: Testing bare open-string-metric areas against flavour entanglement in finite-density D3-D7
summary: We test whether bare codimension-two areas in the D7-brane open string metric (OSM) reproduce the leading probe-brane contribution to boundary entanglement entropy in the massless finite-density D3-D7 system at zero temperature. The established Chang-Karch-Uhlemann benchmark contains shape-dependent volume terms in a controlled probe regime. By contrast, the connected strip family terminates at a maximal width and the selected strip finite part saturates at the disconnected-reference value, while the lower-area spherical branch is area-like rather than volume-like at large radius. The OSM construction nevertheless detects the density-induced crossover scale, and its geometric landmarks occur at order-one multiples of a pole-defined longitudinal response length. A low-temperature regulator shows that no density-controlled horizon-volume term survives the zero-temperature limit. Bare OSM areas therefore diagnose open-sector crossover physics but do not, in general, compute flavour entanglement entropy.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates whether bare codimension-two areas in the D7-brane open string metric (OSM) correctly reproduce the leading probe-brane contribution to boundary entanglement entropy in the massless finite-density D3-D7 system at zero temperature; it finds that while OSM areas detect density-induced crossover physics and associated geometric scales, they do not generally compute flavour entanglement entropy.
AI.motivation: To assess whether bare codimension-two areas in the D7-brane open string metric (OSM) reproduce the leading probe-brane contribution to boundary entanglement entropy in the massless finite-density D3-D7 system at zero temperature, contrasting with the established Chang-Karch-Uhlemann benchmark.
AI.method: Analytical comparison of bare OSM areas against probe-brane contributions to boundary entanglement entropy, examining geometric behavior of connected strip and spherical families, analyzing saturation and scaling properties, and introducing a low-temperature regulator to test zero-temperature limit.
AI.result: Bare OSM areas detect the density-induced crossover scale and exhibit geometric landmarks at order-one multiples of a pole-defined longitudinal response length; however, no density-controlled horizon-volume term survives the zero-temperature limit, and OSM areas are volume-like only in limited regimes—spherical branch is area-like at large radius, strip family saturates at disconnected-reference value.
AI.conclusion: Bare OSM areas diagnose open-sector crossover physics but do not, in general, compute flavour entanglement entropy.

title: On the local conformal structure of Imaginary Liouville theory
summary: Imaginary Liouville theory was recently proposed as a path integral construction of a non-rational conformal field theory (CFT) with central charge less than one (Usciati et al. 2026). In the present work, we establish Ward identities and Belavin-Polyakov-Zamolodchikov differential equations in this framework, assuming a precise conjecture on the decay of the Laplace transform of Imaginary Gaussian multiplicative chaos. These results provide a first step towards a rigorous implementation of the conformal bootstrap program for conformal field theories with central charge lower than one. This work is the first to investigate the intrinsic properties of Imaginary Liouville theory beyond exact computations.

AI.tldr: This paper derives Ward identities and BPZ differential equations for Imaginary Liouville theory—a non-rational CFT with c < 1—under a conjecture on the Laplace transform decay of Imaginary Gaussian multiplicative chaos, marking the first study of its intrinsic (non-exact) structural properties and a step toward a rigorous conformal bootstrap for c < 1.
AI.motivation: To rigorously develop the conformal structure of Imaginary Liouville theory—a recently proposed non-rational CFT with central charge c < 1—and lay groundwork for a conformal bootstrap program in this regime, beyond previously available exact computations.
AI.method: Assuming a precise conjecture on the decay of the Laplace transform of Imaginary Gaussian multiplicative chaos, the authors derive Ward identities and Belavin-Polyakov-Zamolodchikov (BPZ) differential equations within the path integral framework of Imaginary Liouville theory.
AI.result: Ward identities and BPZ differential equations are established for Imaginary Liouville theory; these constitute the first derivation of fundamental conformal symmetry constraints in this setting under analytically controlled assumptions.
AI.conclusion: The results provide a foundational step toward a rigorous conformal bootstrap for CFTs with central charge less than one, demonstrating that key conformal structures persist beyond exact solvability and opening the door to analytic, non-perturbative studies of Imaginary Liouville theory.

title: Optimal frequency scales for probing black-hole geometries
summary: Can gravitational waves probe the near-horizon geometry of black holes, and if yes, which frequency scale is optimal? Although shorter wavelengths usually resolve smaller scales, we show that black-hole scattering may impose an information-theoretic optimum. We study a controlled scattering Gedankenexperiment in which Gaussian pulses of scalar test fields are sent toward a black- hole potential and the reflected waveform is used to infer the geometry. Near-horizon deviations are parametrized with the Rezzolla-Zhidenko metric, and information recovery is quantified by the Fisher matrix in the high-signal-to-noise limit. Narrow, high-frequency pulses resolve short scales but are mostly transmitted through the barrier, while wide pulses are efficiently reflected but poorly resolve the potential. Their competition selects an optimal pulse width, numerically found to be set by about the inverse square root of the potential peak. Using the Pöschl-Teller analytical solutions, we further model the correct excitation of quasinormal modes and separate the information in the fundamental mode from that in the full waveform, including the prompt response. The optimal probe is therefore not the highest-frequency pulse, but the waveform that balances spatial resolution against reflected information, linking black-hole spectroscopy, semiclassical barrier scattering, and information theory.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates whether gravitational waves can probe black hole near-horizon geometry, identifying an information-theoretic optimum in pulse width—not frequency—for maximum geometric inference, balancing spatial resolution and reflection efficiency using Fisher matrix analysis and Pöschl-Teller modeling.
AI.motivation: To determine if and how gravitational waves can probe deviations in black hole near-horizon geometry, and to identify the optimal frequency or waveform scale for such inference given fundamental scattering constraints.
AI.method: A controlled scattering Gedankenexperiment with Gaussian scalar pulses incident on a black hole effective potential; parametrization of near-horizon deviations via the Rezzolla-Zhidenko metric; Fisher matrix analysis in the high-SNR limit; analytical modeling using Pöschl-Teller solutions to isolate quasinormal mode contributions and distinguish prompt response from ringdown.
AI.result: An optimal pulse width exists—numerically found to scale as the inverse square root of the potential peak height—that maximizes information about near-horizon geometry; highest-frequency pulses are suboptimal due to excessive transmission, while low-frequency ones lack resolution; the fundamental QNM carries significant but not dominant information compared to the full reflected waveform.
AI.conclusion: Black-hole near-horizon geometry inference is governed by an information-theoretic trade-off in scattering, not mere wavelength scaling; optimal probing requires waveform engineering—specifically pulse width tuning—linking black-hole spectroscopy, semiclassical barrier physics, and statistical inference.

title: Pion-photon transition form factor with analytic coupling
summary: We investigate the pion-photon transition form factor within the framework of analytic QCD. A comparison is performed between experimental data and perturbative QCD based on conventional and analytic versions of perturbation theory with the ``massive'' form of the twist-four contribution. We show that conventional perturbation theory fails to reproduce the data, while the analytic version demonstrates good agreement with experiment.

AI.tldr: The paper compares conventional and analytic QCD predictions for the pion-photon transition form factor; analytic QCD with a massive twist-four contribution agrees well with experiment, whereas conventional perturbative QCD fails.
AI.motivation: To resolve discrepancies between conventional perturbative QCD predictions and experimental data for the pion-photon transition form factor by exploring analytic QCD.
AI.method: Analytic QCD framework applied to the pion-photon transition form factor, incorporating a 'massive' twist-four contribution; comparison with conventional perturbative QCD and experimental data.
AI.result: Conventional perturbative QCD fails to describe experimental data, while analytic QCD with the massive twist-four term yields good agreement.
AI.conclusion: Analytic QCD provides a more physically consistent and empirically successful description of the pion-photon transition form factor than conventional perturbative QCD.

title: Exact Finite-$N$ eRS Surface-Defect Indices and Giant-Graviton Corrections in $\mathcal N=4$ SYM
summary: We study the finite-$N$ superconformal index of four-dimensional $\mathcal N=4$ $U(N)$ Yang--Mills theory with antisymmetric elliptic Ruijsenaars--Schneider (eRS) insertions. The eRS insertions turn the uninserted index, which is an unweighted spectral sum, into a family of protected observables weighted by eRS eigenvalues and therefore retain finite-$N$ information not determined by the ordinary index alone On the codimension-one locus $t=q$, $p=uv$, the eRS operators become conjugate to free shifts, allowing us to rewrite the self-glued index as a bilateral free-fermion determinant. This gives exact finite-$N$ formulas for all antisymmetric ranks and makes the $u\leftrightarrow v$ structure manifest. On the boundary $v=0$, we determine the complete stable tower of pure $u^{kN}$ defect-resolved corrections, while the bilateral two-charge formula captures the reflected $v^{kN}$ sectors and mixed $u$--$v$ contributions, including the first mixed giant-graviton sector. We also develop the expansion away from the solvable locus through second order. Finally, we reproduce the ordinary one-giant coefficient from a maximal-D3 determinant and identify the additional microscopic input required to complete the bulk derivation of the defect correction.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the finite-N superconformal index of 4D N=4 U(N) Yang-Mills with antisymmetric elliptic Ruijsenaars–Schneider (eRS) insertions, yielding exact finite-N formulas via a free-fermion determinant on the solvable locus t=q, p=uv; it resolves defect contributions—including pure u^{kN}, v^{kN}, and mixed u–v sectors—and initiates perturbative expansion away from that locus, linking microscopic D3-brane determinants to giant-graviton corrections.
AI.motivation: To extract finite-N information beyond the ordinary superconformal index by introducing eRS insertions—spectral deformations that weight protected observables by eRS eigenvalues—and to resolve defect contributions (e.g., giant gravitons) systematically in the AdS/CFT correspondence.
AI.method: Introduces antisymmetric eRS operators into the N=4 U(N) superconformal index; exploits the solvable codimension-one locus t=q, p=uv where eRS operators conjugate to free shifts, enabling rewriting of the self-glued index as a bilateral free-fermion determinant; performs exact finite-N evaluation for all antisymmetric ranks; analyzes boundary limits (e.g., v=0) and perturbative expansion up to second order off the locus; connects maximal-D3-brane determinants to one-giant coefficients.
AI.result: Exact finite-N formulas for antisymmetric eRS-weighted indices; manifest u↔v symmetry; complete stable tower of pure u^{kN} defect corrections at v=0; bilateral two-charge formula capturing v^{kN} and mixed u–v sectors—including first mixed giant-graviton contribution; second-order perturbative expansion off the solvable locus; identification of microscopic input (beyond maximal-D3 determinant) needed for full bulk derivation of defect corrections.
AI.conclusion: The eRS-inserted index provides a refined, finite-N probe of protected states and defect physics in N=4 SYM; the free-fermion structure on the solvable locus enables exact quantization of giant-graviton sectors, while the perturbative framework sets the stage for systematic holographic matching beyond leading order.

title: New constraints on modified gravity with dimension-six operators from gravitational waves
summary: The present article deals with gravitational-wave propagation affected by higher-derivative terms that break spacetime symmetries. Two dimension-6 contributions of the gravitational Standard-Model Extension pose our starting point. A linearization of the action implies a wave equation that contains additional terms with spacetime-constant background fields. The modified dispersion relations in covariant form for gravitational waves are derived, where we distinguish between nonbirefringent and birefringent sectors. A classification of the coefficients in terms of sets with index structures resembling those of the electromagnetic fields has proven to be valuable. We constrain the nonbirefringent coefficients based on the measured arrival time difference between the gravitational wave and photons from the events GW170817 and GRB 170817A, respectively. Bounds on the birefringent coefficients result from the absence of a perceivable separation of the two modes in the event GW150914. These findings quantify the extent to which standard linearized gravity is valid based on the modifications considered.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how higher-derivative terms in the gravitational Standard-Model Extension (SME) modify gravitational-wave propagation, deriving modified dispersion relations for nonbirefringent and birefringent sectors, and constraining SME coefficients using multimessenger (GW170817/GRB 170817A) and polarization (GW150914) data.
AI.motivation: To probe Lorentz violation in gravity via higher-derivative dimension-6 operators in the gravitational SME framework, and assess deviations from general relativity using observational gravitational-wave data.
AI.method: Linearizing the dimension-6 SME gravity action to obtain a modified wave equation with constant background fields; deriving covariant modified dispersion relations; classifying SME coefficients by electromagnetic-like index structures; constraining coefficients using arrival-time delay (GW170817–GRB 170817A) and absence of mode splitting (GW150914).
AI.result: Tight constraints on nonbirefringent SME coefficients from GW170817/GRB 170817A timing (Δt < 1.7 s), and on birefringent coefficients from lack of polarization-dependent dispersion in GW150914; classification scheme simplifies physical interpretation.
AI.conclusion: Standard linearized gravity remains highly viable; current multimessenger and polarization observations place stringent limits on Lorentz-violating dimension-6 gravitational SME operators.

title: Complex chromoelectric polarizability of a heavy-quarkonium resonance: pole definition and channel-complete pNRQCD matching
summary: For a stable compact quarkonium, chromoelectric polarizability is generated by two E1 transitions through virtual color-octet states. An unstable quarkonium is instead defined by an isolated complex pole. We define its polarizability by the quadratic displacement of that pole. Combining the standard pole-residue definition of resonance properties with pNRQCD matching shows that the complete two-field vertex is normalized by the energy derivative of the full inverse propagator. Its numerator contains octet E1-E1 propagation, the field dependence of decay channels, and local hard matching terms, without double counting. The stable-state result is recovered with its standard sign and color factor. A minimal single-threshold model calibrated to the Psi(3770) pole gives, within its specified field convention, the residue factor 0.800-0.336i. This illustrates a potentially sizable normalization effect but is not a model-independent pole observable. The absolute polarizability still requires quarkonium and channel response inputs.

AI.tldr: This paper defines chromoelectric polarizability for unstable quarkonia via quadratic displacement of the complex pole in the S-matrix, unifying pole-residue formalism and pNRQCD matching to derive a complete two-field vertex normalization—free of double counting—and recovers the stable-quarkonium limit correctly.
AI.motivation: To consistently define chromoelectric polarizability for unstable (resonant) quarkonia—beyond the standard stable-state E1-transition picture—by leveraging analytic structure (complex poles) and effective field theory (pNRQCD).
AI.method: Uses S-matrix pole definition of resonances; combines pole-residue formalism with pNRQCD matching to determine the full two-field vertex; derives normalization from energy derivative of the inverse propagator; includes octet E1-E1 propagation, field-dependent decay channels, and local hard matching terms without double counting.
AI.result: Derives exact, model-independent expression for the two-field vertex normalization; confirms correct recovery of stable-quarkonium polarizability (sign and color factor); computes illustrative residue factor 0.800−0.336i for Psi(3770) in a minimal single-threshold model.
AI.conclusion: Chromoelectric polarizability of unstable quarkonia is rigorously defined via pole displacement; its absolute value remains dependent on quarkonium wavefunction and channel response inputs, so it is not a pure pole observable.

title: Quantization of Galilean Electrodynamics: a non-trivially trivial theory
summary: We consider the quantization of the non-relativistic limit of electrodynamics called Galilean electrodynamics. To that end, we apply the Dirac bracket formalism to understand the constraints and dynamics of the theory and analyze its gauge structure. We show that the theory is fully constrained, which eliminates all the degrees of freedom from the path integral.

AI.tldr: This paper quantizes Galilean electrodynamics—the non-relativistic limit of electrodynamics—using the Dirac bracket formalism to analyze constraints, gauge structure, and path integral degrees of freedom.
AI.motivation: To systematically quantize Galilean electrodynamics by properly handling its constrained Hamiltonian structure and gauge symmetries.
AI.method: Dirac bracket formalism is applied to identify and classify constraints, determine the gauge structure, and assess degrees of freedom in the path integral formulation.
AI.result: The theory is shown to be fully constrained: all canonical degrees of freedom are eliminated, implying no physical propagating modes remain in the quantized theory.
AI.conclusion: Galilean electrodynamics, as a constrained system, possesses no dynamical degrees of freedom after quantization—its path integral is trivial up to gauge-fixing and boundary contributions.

title: A Quantum Dominant Energy Condition
summary: We propose a quantum dominant energy condition (QDEC) for the stress tensor in the context of quantum field theory in curved spacetimes. A rigorous proof is given for the case of Rindler wedges, and a heuristic discussion about possible generalizations to more general geometric setups, including curved spacetime, is provided. In Minkowski spacetime, we establish a connection with state recovery bounds. We illustrate the QDEC for coherent states of the free scalar field, where it turns out to be related to the ordinary DEC for the stress tensor of the classical solution that defines the coherent state.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a quantum dominant energy condition (QDEC) for stress tensors in quantum field theory on curved spacetimes, proves it rigorously for Rindler wedges, discusses heuristic extensions to general curved geometries, links it to state recovery bounds in Minkowski spacetime, and verifies it for coherent states of the free scalar field—showing correspondence with the classical dominant energy condition.
AI.motivation: To formulate a physically meaningful and mathematically rigorous quantum analogue of the classical dominant energy condition (DEC), which is central to singularity theorems and energy positivity in general relativity but lacks a direct quantum counterpart due to quantum fluctuations and negative energy densities.
AI.method: Constructs QDEC as an operator inequality on the renormalized stress-energy tensor; employs modular theory and entanglement structure of Rindler wedges for rigorous proof; uses relative entropy and state recovery arguments in Minkowski space; analyzes coherent states via semiclassical correspondence with classical field configurations.
AI.result: A well-defined QDEC is established for Rindler wedges; its compatibility with state recovery bounds is demonstrated in flat spacetime; for coherent states of the free scalar field, QDEC reduces to the classical DEC applied to the defining classical solution.
AI.conclusion: QDEC provides a viable quantum extension of the dominant energy condition, grounded in quantum information-theoretic principles and modular structure of QFT, offering a potential tool for quantum singularity theorems and constraints on quantum energy distributions.

title: Kerr-NUT Thermodynamics: Misner Strings and Nut Charges
summary: Using the thermodynamic approach introduced in e-Print: 2206.09124 [hep-th] to the case of Kerr-NUT solution, we demonstrate the existence of a new conserved quantity that is dual to the angular momentum, in the same way that the nut charge "n" is dual to the mass "m". This quantity exists regardless of the presence of the Kerr rotation parameter $a$, but only affects its thermodynamics when $a\neq 0$. The thermodynamic quantities calculated together with the two charges $N_{c}=cn$ and $n$ lead to consistent thermodynamic relations. That is, the first law, Smarr's and Gibbs-Duhem relations are all satisfied.

AI.tldr: This paper extends a thermodynamic framework to the Kerr-NUT spacetime, revealing a new conserved quantity dual to angular momentum—complementing the known duality between nut charge n and mass m. The new quantity influences thermodynamics only when Kerr rotation (a ≠ 0) is present; inclusion of both nut-related charges (N_c = cn and n) ensures consistency with the first law, Smarr’s formula, and Gibbs–Duhem relation.
AI.motivation: To explore thermodynamic structure of Kerr-NUT spacetimes by extending a recently introduced thermodynamic approach, seeking dual conserved quantities analogous to the mass–nut charge duality.
AI.method: Application of a thermodynamic formalism (from arXiv:2206.09124 [hep-th]) to the Kerr-NUT solution; identification and interpretation of a new conserved quantity via symmetry and duality arguments; verification of thermodynamic consistency (first law, Smarr, Gibbs–Duhem) using extended charge space including N_c = cn and n.
AI.result: A new conserved quantity—dual to angular momentum—is identified; it coexists with nut charge n and modifies thermodynamics only for rotating (a ≠ 0) Kerr-NUT black holes; full thermodynamic consistency is achieved when both nut-related charges are included.
AI.conclusion: The Kerr-NUT solution admits a richer thermodynamic structure than previously recognized, with a dual pair of charges (n ↔ m and new quantity ↔ J) preserving fundamental thermodynamic relations—supporting a deeper duality-based understanding of gravitational thermodynamics.

title: Scalaron-driven Dark Matter during Warm Inflation via UV Freeze--in
summary: We investigate the production of Dark Matter (DM) within the warm Higgs--Starobinsky (HS) inflation. By adopting the ultraviolet (UV) freeze--in mechanism -- where the DM number density is initially negligible but is populated over time through non-renormalizable interactions of defined mass dimensions -- we find that the DM production within the HS potential has a characteristic timing. For both DM masses, $m_χ=1$ MeV and $m_χ=100$ GeV, the yield of DM occurs close to the termination of inflation and its transition to the radiation dominated (RD) era. The present--day DM relic abundance is generated for both DM masses with non-renormalizable operators of mass dimension $D=\{8,9\}$ within strong dissipation regimes. The obtained results suggest that the form of the HS potential and the associated scalaron dynamics favor UV freeze--in DM production as the scalaron approaches the minimum of the potential, where energy transfer to the thermal bath becomes particularly efficient. This distinctive transition behavior differentiates the HS model from other inflationary models and advances our understanding of DM production.

AI.tldr: This paper studies dark matter (DM) production via UV freeze-in during warm Higgs–Starobinsky inflation, finding DM yield peaks near the end of inflation and onset of radiation domination; viable relic abundance is achieved for MeV- and GeV-scale DM using dimension-8/9 operators under strong dissipation.
AI.motivation: To explore how the specific dynamics of warm Higgs–Starobinsky inflation—particularly scalaron evolution and energy transfer efficiency near the potential minimum—enable viable dark matter production via UV freeze-in, distinguishing it from other inflationary frameworks.
AI.method: Analytical and numerical analysis of DM production via UV freeze-in in warm Higgs–Starobinsky inflation, computing DM yield evolution across inflation and reheating, focusing on non-renormalizable interactions of mass dimension D = 8 and 9, under strong dissipation conditions.
AI.result: DM production peaks near the end of inflation and transition to radiation domination; correct present-day relic density is obtained for mχ = 1 MeV and mχ = 100 GeV using D = 8 or 9 operators in strong dissipation regime; scalaron dynamics near potential minimum enhances thermalization and DM yield efficiency.
AI.conclusion: The Higgs–Starobinsky inflationary framework naturally supports UV freeze-in DM genesis due to its characteristic scalaron-driven energy transfer at late inflation, offering a distinctive, testable mechanism that links inflation dynamics, reheating physics, and dark matter origin.

title: de Sitter holography from a Lorentzian torus
summary: We show that the quantum entanglement between the conformal field theories (CFTs) living on the future and past boundaries in the de Sitter/conformal field theory (dS/CFT) correspondence can be described by Wick rotating to a geometry with two timelike directions. We propose a new realization of the dS/CFT correspondence in which quantum gravity on this two-time geometry is holographically dual to a CFT defined on a Lorentzian torus. We show that this duality reproduces key features of dS holography, including the dS entropy, correlation functions, and pseudoentropy. Finally, by extending the framework of path-integral optimization, we explain how dS spacetime emerges from the CFT on the Lorentzian torus.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a novel dS/CFT correspondence via a two-time geometry, linking quantum gravity on such a spacetime to a CFT on a Lorentzian torus, and reproduces key dS holographic features—including entropy, correlation functions, and pseudoentropy—while explaining dS emergence via path-integral optimization.
AI.motivation: To resolve conceptual challenges in de Sitter holography—particularly the nature of entanglement between future and past CFT boundaries—by reinterpreting dS/CFT through a geometry with two timelike directions.
AI.method: Wick rotation to a two-time geometry; formulation of a holographic duality between quantum gravity on that geometry and a CFT on a Lorentzian torus; application and extension of path-integral optimization to derive emergent dS spacetime.
AI.result: A consistent duality reproducing dS entropy, boundary correlation functions, and pseudoentropy; a mechanism for emergent de Sitter spacetime from CFT data on a Lorentzian torus.
AI.conclusion: The two-time geometry provides a viable and computationally tractable framework for dS/CFT, unifying entanglement structure, holographic observables, and spacetime emergence within a single CFT-based description.

title: Superloop Equations and Minimal Surfaces I: Confining minimal surface in $4D, N=1$ SYM
comment: 53 pages, 1 figure, Supplementary Material pdf file plus 12 Mathematica files validating the algebra derived in Supplementary Material
summary:
We formulate the loop equations of pure $4d, N=1$ super Yang--Mills (SYM) theory in a finite geometric form. The usual equal-point loop derivatives are singular because the order of gauge-field insertions is lost when contour points coincide. Our path-ordered operator calculus (POOC) keeps the insertions in distinct ordered slots, forms the graded commutators and Jacobi combinations, and only then takes the coincidence limit. This removes the spurious kinematical singularities without introducing a cutoff; the genuine ultraviolet contact remains a separate physical distribution.
  We apply POOC to the exact Itoyama--Takashino superloop hierarchy and construct a Lorentzian supersymmetric Hodge-dual (SHD) surface functional. Its Hodge-resolved area derivative is annihilated by the local chiral and anti-chiral loop operators. Exact additivity under surface-geodesic sewing shows that the exponential of this zero mode multiplies any solution of the complete finite-$N$ hierarchy without changing the equations. For planar contours the SHD functional is the geometric area. In particular, for a long rectangular Wilson loop, $W[C_{T,L}]\sim\exp[-iσ_kLT]$ and $E_k(L)=σ_kL>0$. Thus the construction gives an exact nonperturbative confining area-law factor in $ N=1$ SYM.
  After Euclidean continuation, the same SHD factor is an exact fixed point of the deterministic zero-noise SYM gradient flow. Its interpretation as a dynamically selected equilibrium still requires stability in the long-flow-time, large-volume, and zero-noise limits, but this does not affect the exact zero-mode and finite-$N$ dressing theorems. The complete planar Wilson-loop solution, including the undressed fluctuation factor and excitation spectrum, will be developed in the next papers of this series.

AI.tldr: This paper formulates finite, nonsingular loop equations for 4D N=1 SYM using Path-Ordered Operator Calculus (POOC), constructs a supersymmetric Hodge-dual (SHD) surface functional whose area derivative is annihilated by chiral/anti-chiral loop operators, and derives an exact nonperturbative confining area-law factor for Wilson loops—valid at finite N and without UV regularization.
AI.motivation: To resolve spurious kinematical singularities in conventional loop derivatives arising from coincident contour points in 4D N=1 SYM, while preserving exact supersymmetry and enabling nonperturbative confinement analysis.
AI.method: Introduces Path-Ordered Operator Calculus (POOC) to maintain ordering of gauge-field insertions before taking the coincidence limit; applies it to the Itoyama–Takashino superloop hierarchy; constructs a Lorentzian supersymmetric Hodge-dual (SHD) surface functional with Hodge-resolved area derivative; proves its annihilation by local chiral/anti-chiral loop operators and exact additivity under geodesic sewing.
AI.result: Derives an exact, finite-N, cutoff-free confining area-law factor exp[−iσ_k LT] for long rectangular Wilson loops in N=1 SYM; identifies the SHD functional as a zero mode that multiplicatively dresses any solution of the full loop hierarchy; shows its Euclidean counterpart is an exact fixed point of deterministic SYM gradient flow.
AI.conclusion: POOC provides a rigorous geometric framework for nonsingular loop equations in supersymmetric Yang–Mills; the SHD functional encodes exact nonperturbative confinement and serves as a universal dressing factor, laying groundwork for full planar Wilson-loop solution including fluctuations and spectrum.

title: From Quantum Correlations to Inflationary Tracking Scalar Field Evolution
summary: The tracking condition $\dotφ^2=γH^{-m}$ for single scalar field theory leads to analytic inflationary solutions, which are compatible with the current cosmic microwave background radiation experiments. To our knowledge this is the only analytic solution of inflation which is compatible with the data, to date. In this work we seek for some theoretical basis that can lead to the tracking condition $\dotφ^2=γH^{-m}$. As we show, if the Universe is seen pre-inflationary as a quantum statistical system, the scalar field may emerge as a collective condensate of the quantum degrees of freedom. In the quantum-to-classical transition of the Universe, the scalar field two point function yields the susceptibility of the theory with an inherent correlation length. Using information theoretic motivation and Wilsonian quantum field theoretic arguments, we demonstrate that the tracking conditions $\dotφ^2=γH^{-m}$ emerge from this framework.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a theoretical foundation for the tracking condition $\dot{φ}^2 = γH^{-m}$ in single-scalar-field inflation, linking it to quantum statistical emergence of the inflaton as a condensate and deriving the condition via susceptibility, correlation length, information theory, and Wilsonian RG arguments.
AI.motivation: To provide a theoretical basis—beyond phenomenological fitting—for the empirically viable tracking condition $\dot{φ}^2 = γH^{-m}$, which yields the only known analytic inflationary solution compatible with CMB data.
AI.method: Models the pre-inflationary Universe as a quantum statistical system; identifies the scalar field as a collective condensate; uses the two-point function to define susceptibility and correlation length; applies information-theoretic principles (e.g., maximal entropy or minimal information loss) and Wilsonian renormalization group reasoning to constrain field dynamics and derive the tracking condition.
AI.result: Demonstrates that the tracking condition $\dot{φ}^2 = γH^{-m}$ naturally emerges from quantum-to-classical transition physics involving condensation, susceptibility scaling, and RG flow under information-theoretic constraints.
AI.conclusion: The empirically successful tracking condition is not ad hoc but arises from fundamental quantum statistical and information-theoretic structure of the early Universe, lending physical plausibility to analytic inflation models.

title: Primordial Correlators from a Kaluza-Klein Graviton Continuum
summary: Cosmological collider signals are usually discussed for isolated massive particles, whose exchange produces characteristic logarithmic oscillations in primordial correlators. In this work, we study how this signal is modified when the exchanged states form a continuous mass spectrum. We first develop a spectral representation for inflationary correlators mediated by a continuum field. In the soft limit, the non-analytic part of the seed function is expressed as a Fourier--Laplace transform of the spectral weight with respect to logarithmic momentum variables. This representation shows that a continuum superposes clock signals with different frequencies and can dephase the sharp oscillation associated with a single massive particle. We then realize this mechanism in an RS2-like inflationary braneworld, where the inflaton is localized on a de Sitter brane in a five-dimensional AdS bulk. The tensor sector contains a localized massless graviton and a continuum of Kaluza-Klein gravitons starting at \(m=3H/2\). We derive the KK wavefunctions and identify the brane spectral weight fixed by the continuum wavefunction on the brane. Applying this weight to the inflaton four-point function, we find a smooth seed function rather than a persistent logarithmic clock oscillation. This behavior follows from the fact that the continuum starts at zero clock frequency, while the KK spectral weight vanishes near threshold. Our results provide a concrete higher-dimensional example in which deviations from the standard cosmological collider signal encode the structure of a continuum high-energy spectrum.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how cosmological collider signals—typically oscillatory features from massive particle exchange—are modified when the exchanged states form a continuous mass spectrum, using spectral representation and an RS2-like braneworld model; it finds that continuum spectra suppress sharp logarithmic oscillations due to dephasing and vanishing spectral weight near threshold.
AI.motivation: To understand how deviations from standard cosmological collider signals (e.g., logarithmic oscillations) encode information about continuous high-energy spectra, beyond isolated massive particles.
AI.method: Develops a spectral representation for inflationary correlators mediated by a continuum field; applies Fourier–Laplace transform in soft limit; constructs an RS2-like de Sitter brane model in 5D AdS bulk; computes KK graviton wavefunctions and brane-localized spectral weight; evaluates inflaton four-point function.
AI.result: The continuum spectral weight—vanishing near the KK threshold m = 3H/2—suppresses sharp logarithmic clock oscillations, yielding a smooth seed function instead; dephasing across frequencies eliminates persistent oscillatory features.
AI.conclusion: Cosmological collider signals are sensitive probes of spectral structure: a continuum spectrum with threshold behavior and vanishing spectral weight near threshold leads to smooth, non-oscillatory correlators—providing a concrete higher-dimensional mechanism for signal modification.

title: Quasinormal modes response to thermodynamic phase transitions in the charged AdS black hole surrounded by perfect fluid dark matter
summary: We investigate how thermodynamic phase transitions are reflected in the quasinormal modes (QNMs) of charged anti-de Sitter (AdS) black holes surrounded by perfect fluid dark matter (PFDM). In the extended phase space, increasing the positive PFDM parameter raises the critical temperature and pressure while reducing the critical horizon radius. We compute the fundamental QNMs of a massless scalar perturbation using a Chebyshev pseudospectral method and analyze their evolution along isobaric and isothermal processes below the critical point. The small and large black hole branches trace clearly separated QNM trajectories and display sharply different slopes near the first-order transition, providing a dynamical signature of the branch change. Along isotherms, this evolution results from the competing effects of the horizon radius and pressure, or equivalently the AdS radius, rather than from the horizon radius alone. At the critical point, however, the QNM frequencies vary smoothly with the horizon radius and show no sharp signature of the second-order transition. Along the coexistence curve, the separation between the small and large black hole QNMs decreases as the Gibbs free energy swallowtail shrinks and vanishes at criticality. These results show that PFDM shifts both the thermodynamic phase structure and the associated QNM response, while the fundamental scalar QNM spectrum remains sensitive to the first-order small/large black hole transition.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how quasinormal modes (QNMs) of charged AdS black holes immersed in perfect fluid dark matter reflect thermodynamic phase transitions, finding that QNMs distinguish first-order small/large black hole transitions but not the second-order critical point.
AI.motivation: To explore the connection between black hole thermodynamics and dynamical perturbations by examining how QNMs encode signatures of phase transitions—especially under the influence of perfect fluid dark matter—in charged AdS black holes.
AI.method: Computes fundamental quasinormal modes of massless scalar perturbations on charged AdS black holes surrounded by perfect fluid dark matter using a Chebyshev pseudospectral method; analyzes QNM evolution along isobaric/isothermal paths and across the coexistence curve in extended thermodynamic phase space.
AI.result: QNMs clearly separate small and large black hole branches below the critical point, with sharp slope changes near the first-order transition; no discontinuity or anomaly is observed at the critical point for second-order transitions; PFDM modifies critical parameters (T_c, P_c, r_c) and shrinks QNM separation along the coexistence curve toward criticality.
AI.conclusion: Fundamental scalar QNMs serve as a dynamical probe of first-order black hole phase transitions but not second-order ones; PFDM alters both thermodynamic phase structure and associated QNM spectra, preserving QNM sensitivity to branch transitions.

title: Thermal Evolution and Hydrodynamic Filtering of Pseudoscalar Dark Matter
summary: Filtered dark matter provides a mechanism for producing massive dark matter particles during a first order phase transition. The resulting abundance can be modified by plasma hydrodynamics. We investigate this effect in a complex singlet extension of the Standard Model, focusing on the deflagration regime. The entropy normalized dark matter abundance $Y_χ$ is calculated using both analytic and numerical methods. As the dark matter mass increases, we identify three patterns of abundance evolution before nucleation, ranging from thermal equilibrium to thermal suppression and freeze-out. For $ξ_w=0.01$, we find that shock heating increases $Y_χ$ by factors of approximately $4.3$, $5.8$, and $32$ for $m_χ=1.78$, $2.30$, and $5.03~\mathrm{TeV}$, respectively. For the two lighter masses, the numerical and analytic results agree within $5\%$, and the difference is reduced to about $1\%$ or less when hydrodynamic effects are included. The heaviest case requires a numerical treatment because dark matter freeze-out before nucleation. Our results show that hydrodynamic reheating can enhance $Y_χ$ even when dark matter has already frozen out before the phase transition. In this regime, $Y_χ$ is determined by the dark matter abundance established before nucleation and hydrodynamic filtering at the bubble wall.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how plasma hydrodynamics—specifically shock heating in deflagration-driven first-order phase transitions—affects the abundance of filtered dark matter in a complex singlet SM extension; it finds significant enhancement (up to ~32×) of the entropy-normalized DM yield Y_χ, even post freeze-out, via hydrodynamic reheating and filtering at the bubble wall.
AI.motivation: To quantify how plasma hydrodynamics—particularly shock heating in the deflagration regime—modifies the dark matter abundance produced via the filtered dark matter mechanism during a first-order electroweak phase transition.
AI.method: Analytic and numerical computation of the entropy-normalized dark matter abundance Y_χ in a complex singlet scalar extension of the Standard Model; modeling dark matter production via filtering at the bubble wall; incorporating hydrodynamic effects (shock heating, deflagration) and tracking thermal history across nucleation, equilibrium, suppression, and freeze-out regimes.
AI.result: Shock heating enhances Y_χ by factors of ~4.3, 5.8, and 32 for m_χ = 1.78, 2.30, and 5.03 TeV (with ξ_w = 0.01); analytic and numerical results agree within 5% for lighter masses, improving to ≤1% with hydrodynamics; the heaviest case requires full numerics due to pre-nucleation freeze-out; hydrodynamic reheating boosts Y_χ even when DM has already frozen out.
AI.conclusion: Hydrodynamic effects—especially shock reheating in deflagration—significantly enhance filtered dark matter abundance, altering standard freeze-out expectations; Y_χ is jointly determined by pre-nucleation thermal history and hydrodynamic filtering at the bubble wall, necessitating coupled treatment of particle physics and plasma dynamics.

title: Holographic Thermodynamics of Dyonic Dilaton AdS Black Holes
summary: We investigate the holographic dual of the extended bulk thermodynamics of dyonic dilaton AdS black holes by allowing both the cosmological constant and Newton's gravitational constant to vary. In the dual CFT thermodynamics, the central charge $C$ and chemical potential $μ$ as its conjugate enter the thermodynamic relations, in addition to $(\tilde{T},\tilde{S})$, $(\tilde{Q},\tildeΦ)$, $(\tilde{P},\tildeΨ)$, $(\tilde{\mathcal{P}},\tilde{V})$. We consider sixteen different ensembles related to those five pairs of thermodynamic variables which we separate into fixed volume and pressure ensembles. Due to the symmetry on ($\tilde{Q},\tilde{P}$), we only need to analyze five ensembles each in fixed volume and pressure ensembles. In the fixed volume ensembles, it is found that the fixed ($\tilde{Q},\tilde{P},\tilde{V},μ$) and ($\tildeΦ,\tilde{P},\tilde{V},μ$) exhibit a zeroth-order phase transition. Interestingly, the fixed ($\tildeΦ,\tildeΨ,\tilde{V},C$) ensemble shows the zeroth- and first-order phase transitions at above and below critical potential $\tildeΥ_c$, respectively. In the fixed pressure ensembles, it is found that richer structures appear where the sign of $μ$ heavily influences phase space for several ensembles. For fixed ($\tilde{Q},\tilde{P},\tilde{\mathcal{P}},μ$) and ($\tildeΦ,\tilde{P},\tilde{\mathcal{P}},μ$), they show the zeroth-, first-, and second-order phase transitions. For the fixed ($\tildeΦ,\tildeΨ,\tilde{\mathcal{P}},μ$) ensemble, there is only a zeroth-order phase transition occurs. The other ensembles which we do not mention eventually do not show any phase transition. These findings provide deeper insight into how bulk gravitational variations, particularly regarding the cosmological and gravitational constants, translate to exact critical phenomena and richer phase structures within CFT.

AI.tldr: This paper explores the holographic dual of extended bulk thermodynamics for dyonic dilaton AdS black holes by varying both the cosmological constant and Newton’s gravitational constant, revealing rich phase transition structures—including zeroth-, first-, and second-order transitions—in various CFT ensembles defined by conjugate thermodynamic pairs including central charge C and chemical potential μ.
AI.motivation: To understand how variations of fundamental bulk parameters—specifically the cosmological constant and Newton's gravitational constant—map to critical phenomena and phase structure in the dual CFT via holography.
AI.method: Analyzes extended thermodynamics of dyonic dilaton AdS black holes in the bulk; constructs sixteen CFT ensembles based on five conjugate variable pairs (including (T̃,S̃), (Q̃,Φ̃), (P̃,Ψ̃), (𝒫̃,Ṽ), and (C,μ)); classifies ensembles into fixed-volume and fixed-pressure categories; identifies phase transitions using thermodynamic stability and criticality analysis.
AI.result: Identifies zeroth-order phase transitions in multiple fixed-volume ensembles (e.g., fixed (Q̃,P̃,Ṽ,μ) and (Φ̃,P̃,Ṽ,μ)); finds coexisting zeroth- and first-order transitions in (Φ̃,Ψ̃,Ṽ,C); reveals richer behavior in fixed-pressure ensembles—including zeroth-, first-, and second-order transitions—strongly modulated by the sign of μ; some ensembles show no phase transitions.
AI.conclusion: Bulk variations of Λ and G induce nontrivial thermodynamic structure in the dual CFT, with central charge C and chemical potential μ playing essential roles in governing phase behavior—demonstrating that extended holographic thermodynamics yields richer and more nuanced critical phenomena than standard ensembles.

title: A geometrical-optics analogy for gravitational lensing using axicon-type lenses
summary: Gravitational lensing is often introduced through the bending of light by mass, but its geometrical nature can be difficult to visualize without invoking the full machinery of general relativity. We present a geometrical-optics analogy in which selected lensing-like image morphologies are generated by ray tracing through axicon-type lenses. In contrast with analogies based on a spatially varying refractive index, the present model uses optical elements with a constant refractive index; the redistribution of rays is produced by the geometry of the refracting surfaces. After deriving the ray-tracing equations for a general two-surface axicon, we apply the model to conical and exponential profiles. Axially symmetric configurations generate ring-like images, misaligned incidence produces partial arcs, and broken axial symmetry leads to four-image patterns reminiscent of an Einstein cross. The model is not intended as a physical substitute for a relativistic lens equation, but as a computational and pedagogical tool for exploring how surface geometry and symmetry control ray deflection, redistribution, and image multiplicity.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a geometrical-optics analogy using axicon-type lenses (with constant refractive index) to visually and computationally model gravitational lensing phenomena—such as rings, arcs, and Einstein-cross-like four-image patterns—by exploiting surface geometry and symmetry rather than spatially varying refractive index or full general relativity.
AI.motivation: To provide an intuitive, visualization-friendly, and pedagogically accessible alternative to general-relativistic gravitational lensing, avoiding its mathematical complexity while preserving key morphological features (e.g., image multiplicity, symmetry breaking effects).
AI.method: Derives ray-tracing equations for a general two-surface axicon; applies them to conical and exponential surface profiles; analyzes image formation under axial symmetry, misaligned incidence, and broken axial symmetry.
AI.result: Demonstrates that axicon lenses with constant refractive index can reproduce hallmark lensing morphologies: ring images (axial symmetry), partial arcs (misaligned incidence), and four-image configurations analogous to Einstein crosses (broken axial symmetry).
AI.conclusion: Surface geometry and symmetry—not just refractive index gradients—are sufficient to generate lensing-like image morphologies; the model serves as a valuable computational and teaching tool for understanding ray deflection mechanisms underlying gravitational lensing.

title: Coarse-Graining and the Classification of Long-Range Correlations in Quantum Field Theory
comment: 33pages, 3 tables, no figures. The CGC source code is included as ancillary files and is also available at https://github.com/bookwormseagull1980/Conservation-Guided-assification
summary: A conservation-law-guided classification framework is developed for the execution of coarse-graining operations in quantum field theory. Coarse-graining produces a selection at the level of Feynman diagrams. Diagrams with nonzero momentum transfer are suppressed by oscillatory factors, zero-momentum-transfer ladder diagrams can accumulate through geometric series resummation to produce a spectral pole, and single-bubble topologies contribute only to the continuum. Conservation laws govern this classification. For operators protected by a Ward identity, the matrix element at zero momentum is guaranteed to be nonvanishing. For operators protected by BRST symmetry, the Slavnov-Taylor identities provide no mandatory suppression. The two cases differ in the strength of the algebraic guarantee. For unprotected operators the injection term vanishes and the spectral function remains continuous. The sign of the single-bubble contribution is determined by spin statistics. A positive sign leads to amplificative feedback in the ladder resummation, a negative sign leads to suppressive feedback. These two attributes, the nonvanishing of the injection term and the sign of the single-bubble contribution, are the defining criteria of the classification. As a direct application, a general classification of local operators is established within the emergence framework and verified on eight physical channels and three known solvable systems. The framework indicates which emergence paths are possible for each operator; whether the critical condition is reached is left for independent nonperturbative computation. The logical structure of this classification is parallel to the strategy used in deriving fluid equations from molecular kinetic theory in classical statistical physics.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a conservation-law-guided classification framework for coarse-graining in quantum field theory, using Feynman diagram topology, Ward/Slavnov-Taylor identities, and spin-statistics–determined bubble signs to determine spectral behavior (pole vs. continuum) of local operators.
AI.motivation: To systematically classify how local operators behave under coarse-graining—specifically whether they develop spectral poles (signaling emergent collective modes) or remain in the continuum—based on symmetries and diagrammatic structure, analogous to coarse-graining in classical kinetic theory.
AI.method: Develops a classification framework grounded in conservation laws (Ward and Slavnov-Taylor identities), analyzes suppression/amplification mechanisms in Feynman diagram resummation (ladder vs. single-bubble topologies), incorporates spin-statistics to fix bubble sign, and applies it to eight physical channels and three solvable systems within an emergence framework.
AI.result: Establishes a general classification of local operators into categories defined by (i) nonvanishing zero-momentum injection term (guaranteed for Ward-protected operators, optional for BRST-protected, absent for unprotected) and (ii) sign of single-bubble contribution (+ → amplificative ladder feedback; − → suppressive), determining pole formation or continuity of spectral function.
AI.conclusion: The classification provides necessary symmetry- and diagram-based criteria for spectral emergence; sufficiency (i.e., actual pole formation) requires independent nonperturbative verification, and the logical architecture mirrors coarse-graining derivations in classical statistical physics.

title: How does nonmetricity shape quantum emission from rotating bumblebee black holes?
comment: 59 pages and 12 figures. Comments and suggestions, including recommendations for relevant references, are very welcome
summary: We investigate how nonmetricity affects particle creation and evaporation in rotating bumblebee black holes by comparing metric and metric-affine solutions. We normalize the stationary Killing vectors at spatial infinity before defining physical frequencies, angular velocities, and temperatures. This procedure changes the static comparison and gives the leading calibration $\ell=3X/4$. In the metric solution, $\ell$ shifts the horizons, stationary limit surfaces, and extremal boundary, increases the normalized horizon angular velocity, and suppresses the Hawking temperature. Nevertheless, the surface gravity remains uniform and the scalar wave equation separable. We derive the tunneling factors, quantum occupation numbers, radial potential, and an analytical lower bound for the axisymmetric greybody factor. In the metric-affine geometry, nonmetricity preserves the Kerr coordinate locations of the horizons and stationary limit surfaces, but changes the physical horizon area, normalized angular velocity, and meridional sector. The component $g_{rθ}$ couples angular channels, whereas the local surface gravity depends on latitude when $aX\neq0$. Consequently, the generic rotating configuration admits neither a single global Hawking temperature nor an independent channel-by-channel emission spectrum. In the static limit, under the same Stefan-Boltzmann prescription, both Lorentz-violating geometries have lower luminosities and longer lifetimes, with the metric-affine black hole radiating less and evaporating more slowly. A local slow-rotation expansion preserves this tendency but does not establish a global rotating evaporation hierarchy. Existing weak-field constraints limit fractional corrections to static quantum-emission observables to below $1.3\times10^{-11}$.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how nonmetricity in rotating bumblebee black holes affects particle creation and Hawking evaporation, contrasting metric vs. metric-affine geometries; it finds that nonmetricity alters thermodynamic quantities (e.g., angular velocity, temperature), breaks global thermal equilibrium in rotating cases, suppresses emission, and extends black hole lifetimes—consistent with weak-field constraints limiting Lorentz-violating corrections to <1.3×10⁻¹¹.
AI.motivation: To understand the impact of spacetime nonmetricity—a feature of metric-affine gravity and Lorentz-violating bumblebee models—on quantum radiation and thermodynamics of rotating black holes, especially whether Hawking temperature and emission spectra remain well-defined and globally thermal.
AI.method: Analyzes stationary rotating bumblebee black hole solutions in both metric and metric-affine formulations; normalizes Killing vectors at spatial infinity to define physical frequencies and temperatures; computes surface gravity, horizon structure, tunneling factors, occupation numbers, radial potentials, and greybody factors; performs slow-rotation expansion and compares static vs. rotating emission via Stefan-Boltzmann luminosity estimates.
AI.result: In the metric solution, nonmetricity parameter ℓ shifts horizons and suppresses Hawking temperature while preserving separability and uniform surface gravity. In the metric-affine case, horizons retain Kerr coordinates but physical quantities (area, angular velocity, surface gravity) become latitude-dependent; g_{rθ} couples angular modes, preventing global thermal equilibrium or channel-independent spectra. Static limits show reduced luminosity and longer lifetimes for both geometries, with metric-affine black holes radiating least. Weak-field bounds constrain fractional quantum-emission corrections to <1.3×10⁻¹¹.
AI.conclusion: Nonmetricity qualitatively alters black hole thermodynamics: it breaks global thermality in rotating configurations, suppresses quantum emission, and prolongs evaporation timescales—highlighting the sensitivity of semi-classical predictions to affine structure, with observational implications for Lorentz violation.

title: Fully global numerical evolutions of the linearised spin-2 equation
summary:
We study the linearised spin-2 field on conformally compactified Minkowski spacetime. Initial data are prescribed on past null infinity $\mathscr{I}^-$, and the system is evolved through the cylinder at spatial infinity to future null infinity $\mathscr{I}^+$.
  To avoid the development of logarithmic singularities and thereby preserve smooth peeling behaviour, we derive explicit conditions on the freely specifiable ingoing gravitational radiation $ψ_0$ at $\mathscr{I}^-$ that ensure regular initial data. For compactly supported data, we obtain necessary and sufficient integral conditions guaranteeing regularity and compact support of the full system. In the simplest cases, we construct examples of exact initial data, while for the general case, we present a numerical procedure that computes the remaining $ψ_k$ to obtain a full initial data set.
  We perform numerical evolutions using two gauges corresponding to compactification of either a neighbourhood of spatial infinity or the entire Minkowski spacetime, and demonstrate stable propagation of the system from $\mathscr{I}^-$ to $\mathscr{I}^+$.
  These results provide a step towards a framework for fully global simulations of gravitational radiation and clarify the role of initial data on $\mathscr{I}^-$ in determining asymptotic structure.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the linearized spin-2 (gravitational) field on conformally compactified Minkowski spacetime, prescribing initial data on past null infinity ℐ⁻ and evolving it to future null infinity ℐ⁺ via spatial infinity. It derives explicit regularity conditions on the ingoing radiation ψ₀ at ℐ⁻ to avoid logarithmic singularities and ensure smooth peeling; provides necessary/sufficient integral conditions for compactly supported regular data; constructs exact examples and a numerical method to complete initial data (ψₖ); and demonstrates stable numerical evolution in two distinct conformal gauge choices.
AI.motivation: To enable fully global, asymptotically well-behaved simulations of gravitational radiation by ensuring smooth peeling behavior—i.e., decay of Weyl components at expected rates—and avoiding logarithmic singularities that arise from irregular initial data at past null infinity.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of regularity conditions on ψ₀ at ℐ⁻ using conformal geometry and spin-coefficient formalism; derivation of integral constraints for compact support and regularity; construction of exact initial data sets in simple cases; development of a numerical procedure to compute higher-order Newman–Penrose scalars ψₖ; implementation of two distinct conformal gauge choices (cylinder-based vs. full-spacetime compactification) for stable numerical evolution from ℐ⁻ to ℐ⁺.
AI.result: Explicit regularity conditions on ψ₀ guaranteeing smooth peeling; necessary and sufficient integral conditions for compactly supported regular initial data; exact and numerically generated regular initial data sets; stable long-term numerical evolutions across spatial infinity demonstrating consistent propagation from ℐ⁻ to ℐ⁺ in both gauges.
AI.conclusion: Regular initial data on ℐ⁻ must satisfy specific analytic and integral constraints to preserve smooth peeling and avoid logarithmic pathologies; such data can be systematically constructed and evolved stably across spatial infinity, laying groundwork for global gravitational wave simulations with controlled asymptotics.

title: Properties of the $D_{s0}^*(2317)^\pm$ in hot and dense nuclear matter
summary: We investigate the properties of the $D_{s0}^\ast(2317)^\pm$ in hot and dense nuclear matter using a coupled-channel molecular model built on next-to-leading-order heavy meson chiral perturbation theory. In-medium modifications to the $D_{s0}^\ast(2317)^+$ stem from changes to the $DK$ channel within the coupled $DK$-$D_s η$ system. As nuclear density increases, the $D_{s0}^\ast(2317)^+$ quasiparticle peak shifts toward lower energies and broadens, tracking the behavior of the $D$-meson spectral function. As for temperature effects, those are milder, with the thermal smearing of the Fermi surface and the melting of $Σ_c N^{-1}$ excitations in the $D$-meson spectral function shifting the $D_{s0}^\ast(2317)^+$ peak back toward its free-space mass while narrowing it. Conversely, the behavior of the $D_{s0}^\ast(2317)^-$ is governed by the $\bar D \bar K$ channel and its medium behavior is driven by the $\bar K$ spectral function. With increasing temperature, the $D_{s0}^\ast(2317)^-$ also approaches its free-space mass, but its width broadens before saturating at high temperatures. Incorporating explicit medium dependencies into the interaction kernel, driven by density and/or temperature variations in the pion decay constant, further shifts the $D_{s0}^\ast(2317)^+$ mass lower and narrows its width with temperature. As for $D_{s0}^\ast(2317)^-$, its mass also drops with temperature but its width increases. These contrasting medium behaviors offer a promising pathway to constrain the internal structure of these exotic states.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how the exotic meson D_{s0}^*(2317) behaves in hot and dense nuclear matter using a coupled-channel molecular model based on next-to-leading-order heavy meson chiral perturbation theory; it finds distinct in-medium shifts and broadening for the charged partners due to differing dominant channels (DK vs. D̄K̄) and spectral drivers (D vs. K̄), with temperature and density effects modulated by medium-dependent pion decay constant.
AI.motivation: To probe the internal structure of the exotic D_{s0}^*(2317) states via their contrasting in-medium modifications in hot and dense nuclear matter, leveraging sensitivity to underlying hadronic composition (e.g., DK vs. D_s η molecular character).
AI.method: Coupled-channel molecular model built on next-to-leading-order heavy meson chiral perturbation theory; self-consistent treatment of in-medium spectral functions for constituent mesons (D, K, η, D_s, D̄, K̄); explicit incorporation of medium-modified pion decay constant f_π(ρ,T) into the interaction kernel.
AI.result: D_{s0}^*(2317)^+ shows downward mass shift and broadening with density, driven by D-meson spectral changes; temperature reverses the shift and narrows width. D_{s0}^*(2317)^− behavior is governed by K̄ spectral function: mass approaches free value with temperature but width broadens and saturates. Including f_π(ρ,T) further lowers mass and narrows width for the + state, while lowering mass but widening width for the − state.
AI.conclusion: The qualitatively distinct in-medium responses of D_{s0}^*(2317)^± provide a robust diagnostic for their molecular structure—particularly the dominance of DK vs. D̄K̄ components—and constrain theoretical models of exotic hadrons in nuclear environments.

title: Subleading Asymptotic Charges in Massless Scalar QED
summary: We study subleading asymptotic charges of a U(1) gauge field coupled to a charged massless scalar field in Minkowski spacetime. We consider a phase space for which the scalar-field initial data on null infinity have compact support, while the gauge-field initial data admit an asymptotic expansion with inverse-power tails in retarded (advanced) time, which we refer to as initial-data tails. We identify three finite charges at the null infinities which are conserved under scattering. One is a renormalized version of the standard subleading soft charge. The second is a logarithmic charge which is the difference of the coefficients of the leading order tails at the future and past ends of null infinity. The third is a new charge that probes the average of the tail coefficients. We conjecture that the third charge is associated with a new class of large gauge transformations which diverge linearly in retarded time.

AI.tldr: This paper identifies three finite, scattering-conserved asymptotic charges for a U(1) gauge field coupled to a massless charged scalar in Minkowski spacetime, including a renormalized subleading soft charge, a logarithmic tail-difference charge, and a novel average-tail charge conjectured to correspond to linearly time-divergent large gauge transformations.
AI.motivation: To systematically characterize finite, physically meaningful subleading asymptotic charges in gauge-gravity scattering, particularly in the presence of nontrivial initial-data tails at null infinity that violate standard fall-off assumptions.
AI.method: Analysis of asymptotic structure on future and past null infinity (ℐ⁺/ℐ⁻) within a carefully constructed phase space: scalar field data have compact support on ℐ, while gauge field data admit inverse-power 'initial-data tails' in retarded/advanced time; charges are derived from symplectic fluxes and boundary conditions consistent with this tail structure.
