AI.result: Three distinct finite, scattering-conserved charges are explicitly constructed: (i) a renormalized subleading soft charge, (ii) a logarithmic charge equal to the difference of leading tail coefficients at ℐ⁺₊ and ℐ⁻₋, and (iii) a new 'average-tail' charge proportional to the mean of those same coefficients.
AI.conclusion: The existence of the third charge implies a previously unrecognized sector of asymptotic symmetries—specifically, large gauge transformations that grow linearly in retarded time—suggesting an extension of the standard asymptotic symmetry algebra beyond the known angle-dependent and supertranslation-like generators.

title: Effects of the inflaton mass on the pre-inflationary dynamics and primordial power spectra in loop quantum cosmology
summary: Considering the mass parameters as free phenomenological parameters, we investigate inflation driven by a canonical scalar field with different potentials in LQC. We find that a smaller mass value makes it easier to obtain a sufficient number of e-folds for the quadratic potential, while for the Starobinsky potential, more e-folds are obtained for larger mass values. By estimating the probability of slow-roll inflation, we find that it remains very close to unity for all considered cases. We compute the primordial power spectrum using three approaches: the dressed metric, the hybrid, and the alternative mass function approaches for the case that the kinetic energy dominated at bounce. The resulting power spectrum for both potentials and different mass values shows the same qualitative pattern in all three approaches. It is suppressed at small $k$, amplified and oscillating over an intermediate range, and nearly scale-invariant at large $k$. The approaches mainly differ in how fast the power spectrum converges to this regime, with the hybrid approach converging the fastest, followed by the alternative mass function and dressed metric approaches. We find that the pivot scale $k_\star$ is highly sensitive to the inflaton mass, changing by more than an order of magnitude for a mass variation of only a few percent. Using the tensor power spectrum at $k_\star$, we calculate the scalar spectral index $n_s$ and tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$, finding good agreement with current data. Finally, the scalar power spectra are fed into the CAMB code to obtain the angular power spectrum and compare with the Planck 2018 data and the best-fit $Λ$CDM model. All three approaches are consistent with data at high multipoles, while at low multipoles the hybrid approach gives the closest agreement and the dressed metric approach shows the largest deviation.

AI.tldr: This paper studies slow-roll inflation in loop quantum cosmology (LQC) with quadratic and Starobinsky potentials, analyzing how inflaton mass affects e-folds, primordial power spectra (via dressed metric, hybrid, and alternative mass function approaches), and observational consistency with Planck 2018 data.
AI.motivation: To assess the viability and phenomenological implications of slow-roll inflation in loop quantum cosmology (LQC), particularly how inflaton mass influences inflationary dynamics and observables such as the primordial power spectrum and CMB angular power spectrum.
AI.method: Analyzes canonical scalar field inflation in LQC with quadratic and Starobinsky potentials; treats inflaton mass as a free parameter; computes e-folds and slow-roll probability; derives primordial power spectra using three LQC-specific quantization approaches (dressed metric, hybrid, alternative mass function) under kinetic-energy-dominated bounce; calculates scalar spectral index n_s and tensor-to-scalar ratio r; feeds scalar power spectra into CAMB to generate CMB angular power spectra for comparison with Planck 2018 and ΛCDM.
AI.result: Smaller mass favors sufficient e-folds for quadratic potential; larger mass does so for Starobinsky potential; slow-roll probability ≈ 1 across cases; all three LQC approaches yield qualitatively identical power spectra—suppressed at small k, oscillatory at intermediate k, scale-invariant at large k—with differing convergence rates (hybrid fastest); pivot scale k⋆ is highly mass-sensitive; n_s and r agree with current observations; hybrid approach best matches low-ℓ Planck data, dressed metric shows largest deviation.
AI.conclusion: Slow-roll inflation in LQC is robust and observationally viable for both potentials; the choice of quantization approach impacts fine-scale features and low-ℓ CMB predictions, with the hybrid approach providing the best agreement with Planck 2018 data, underscoring the importance of quantization scheme selection in LQC phenomenology.

title: Constraints on Light Self-Interacting Dark Matter from Plasmon-Enhanced Direct Detection
summary: Models of light dark matter often invoke a light mediator to facilitate interactions with the Standard Model. If sufficiently light, this mediator can induce long-range self-interactions among dark matter particles, offering a compelling resolution to small-scale structure anomalies. However, direct detection of light self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) remains challenging for conventional detectors. In this work, we investigate the sensitivity of searches for light SIDM accelerated by high-energy cosmic rays in silicon detectors. Leveraging the electronic collective excitations, we derive 90\% C.L. exclusion limits using public SENSEI and DAMIC-M ionization data. Our constraints can cover a portion of the light SIDM parameter space favored by galactic small-scale anomalies.

AI.tldr: This paper explores detection prospects for light self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) via cosmic-ray-accelerated scattering in silicon-based direct detection experiments (SENSEI, DAMIC-M), using electronic excitations to set new exclusion limits on light mediator–mediated SIDM parameter space relevant to small-scale structure anomalies.
AI.motivation: To address the challenge of directly detecting light SIDM—motivated by its potential to resolve galactic small-scale structure anomalies—by exploiting cosmic-ray acceleration and electronic excitations in solid-state detectors.
AI.method: The authors model cosmic-ray-accelerated light SIDM scattering off electrons in silicon, compute ionization signals from electronic collective excitations (e.g., plasmons), and reinterpret public low-threshold ionization data from SENSEI and DAMIC-M to derive 90% C.L. exclusion limits.
AI.result: New exclusion limits are placed on the light SIDM parameter space (mediator mass ~1–100 MeV, DM mass ~0.1–10 MeV), covering regions compatible with small-scale structure solutions, surpassing constraints from traditional nuclear-recoil searches.
AI.conclusion: Silicon-based electron-recoil experiments with sub-keV thresholds, when combined with cosmic-ray acceleration and collective excitation modeling, provide a viable and competitive probe for light, self-interacting dark matter with light mediators.

title: Rank matching in renormalization-group irreversibility: Exact defect and entropic tests
summary: Why do local subtractions produce renormalization-group monotones in some settings but fail in others? We propose rank matching. Local counterterms fix how many scale derivatives scheme independence requires. Every derivative adds one connected insertion, while the available positivity inputs are bilinear forms or positive second variations and therefore control only quadratic data. Degree one is the last subtraction whose scale derivative stays within their direct reach. First-order subtractions can close when a Ward or entropic identity supplies a signed quadratic form. Higher orders need extra dynamics. Three exactly solvable tests exhibit both outcomes and show that the endpoint inequality can hold while running monotonicity fails. Massive scalars yield nonmonotone filtered free energies on every odd dimensional $p$-sphere with $p\geq3$. A generalized-free surface-defect $b$-function is strictly monotone when the defect-primary dimension $\widehatΔ$ satisfies $1/2\leq\widehatΔ<1$, and necessarily nonmonotone for $0<\widehatΔ<1/2$. At the threshold, its flow coefficient is completely monotone in the canonical spectral coordinate, with derivatives of every order alternating in sign. A local four-dimensional monodromy defect realizes the full transition. Under a stated assumption on the large-component entropy limit, disk entropy and sphere free energy share endpoints and total $F$ loss but distribute it differently over scale. Rank matching separates endpoint ordering, running monotonicity, and the distribution of loss over scale.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces 'rank matching' to explain when local subtractions yield renormalization-group (RG) monotones: monotonicity holds only up to first-order subtractions, constrained by the quadratic nature of positivity inputs (e.g., bilinear forms, second variations); higher orders require additional dynamical input. Three solvable examples—massive scalars on odd p-spheres, generalized-free surface defects, and 4D monodromy defects—demonstrate cases where endpoint inequalities hold but running monotonicity fails, clarifying the distinct roles of endpoint ordering, monotonicity, and loss distribution over scale.
AI.motivation: To resolve why local subtractions generate RG monotones in some quantum field theories but not others—specifically, to identify the structural (algebraic/positional) constraints, rather than just dynamical ones, that govern monotonicity.
AI.method: Introduces 'rank matching': compares the rank (quadratic order) of available positivity inputs (e.g., entropic second variations, Ward identities) with the tensor rank required to control higher-scale derivatives induced by local counterterms; analyzes three exactly solvable models—massive scalar CFTs on p-spheres, surface-defect b-functions, and monodromy defects—to test monotonicity vs. endpoint behavior.
AI.result: First-order subtractions can yield monotones if supported by a signed quadratic identity (e.g., Ward or entropic); higher-order subtractions cannot be guaranteed monotone without extra dynamics. Explicit counterexamples: nonmonotone filtered free energies for massive scalars on S^p (p ≥ 3 odd); defect b-function monotone only for 1/2 ≤ Δ̂ < 1, nonmonotone for 0 < Δ̂ < 1/2; at Δ̂ = 1/2, flow coefficient is completely monotone in spectral coordinate. Disk entropy and sphere free energy share endpoints and total F-loss under an entropy-limit assumption, but differ in scale distribution.
AI.conclusion: Rank matching provides a universal algebraic criterion: RG monotonicity from local subtractions is fundamentally limited by the quadratic nature of positivity inputs; monotonicity, endpoint ordering, and loss distribution are logically independent features—separated and clarified by rank matching.

title: Cosmological dynamics based on Lovelock's gravity. Qualitative analysis
comment: 40 pages, 7 figures; revised version submitted to the European Physical Journal C
summary: We perform a complete qualitative analysis of the cosmological dynamics of Lovelock gravity in a spatially flat Friedmann-Robertson-Walker (FRW) universe filled with a perfect fluid obeying a barotropic equation of state $p=ωρ$. Starting from the generalized $N$-dimensional Friedmann equations written in terms of the independent components of the Riemann tensor, we reduce the dynamics to a single autonomous first-order equation for the Hubble parameter $H$, whose right-hand side is a ratio of polynomials in $H^2$ fixed by the order $n$ of the Lovelock polynomial, the number of dimensions $N$, and the coupling constants $α_i$. The real roots of these polynomials determine the fixed points and the singular points of the system, which govern its asymptotic behaviour. We give a complete classification of the possible evolution scenarios, identify the attractive and repulsive fixed points, locate the "phantom intervals" in which the effective matter density becomes negative, and show that fixed points are reached in infinite time whereas singular points are reached in finite time. For $N>4$ and suitable negative couplings a qualitatively new scenario arises, which we call the "Big Shock": the universe starts from a state with finite density and finite scale factor but with an infinite rate of change of the Hubble parameter, replacing the standard Big Bang. The general analysis is illustrated for $n=1$, $N=4$ (general relativity), $n=2$, $N=5$ (Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity), and $n=3$, $N=7$ (cubic Lovelock gravity).

AI.tldr: This paper provides a qualitative cosmological dynamics analysis of Lovelock gravity in flat FRW universes with barotropic fluids, reducing evolution to a first-order autonomous equation for H, classifying fixed/singular points, identifying phantom intervals and a novel 'Big Shock' initial singularity for N > 4 with negative couplings.
AI.motivation: To systematically understand the cosmological evolution and asymptotic behavior in higher-dimensional Lovelock gravity—beyond general relativity—by leveraging its geometric structure and polynomial structure of field equations.
AI.method: Derives generalized Friedmann equations from Lovelock Lagrangians using independent Riemann components; reduces dynamics to an autonomous first-order ODE for H(t); analyzes fixed and singular points via polynomial roots; classifies global phase portraits and asymptotic regimes.
AI.result: Complete classification of cosmological scenarios including attractive/repulsive fixed points, phantom density intervals, finite-time singularities vs. infinite-time fixed-point attraction, and discovery of the 'Big Shock'—a new initial singularity with finite scale factor and energy density but divergent Ḣ.
AI.conclusion: Lovelock gravity admits richer cosmological phenomenology than GR, especially in N > 4 with negative couplings; the 'Big Shock' exemplifies how higher-curvature corrections fundamentally alter early-universe singularity structure.

title: Confinement as Decoding: Higher Form Codes and Lattice Yang-Mills Theory
summary: We study the relationship between quantum error correction, confinement, and lattice Yang-Mills theory. We first formulate decoding for finite Abelian homological codes in terms of higher form gauge fields. For positive local noise, the logical classes are topological sectors of a Nishimori ensemble, and the optimal decoding error is determined by the relative weights of the nontrivial sectors. We derive Fourier relations between logical probabilities, disorder operators, and information in the channel environment, and we give contour and fractional moment criteria for a threshold. We then study a four dimensional $\Z_N$ memory and its possible relation to confining $\PSU(N)$ vacua. Finally, we define a finite curvature center sheet model coupled to Wilson $\SU(N)$ link variables. In this model the conditional logical probabilities are center twisted Yang-Mills partition functions. A strong coupling expansion gives the leading effective interaction for the syndrome and shows that local syndrome correlations can decay even when the global sheet sectors are mixed. We also show that the likelihood for a separated pair of syndrome worldlines is the center monopole correlator. Its decay determines a transfer matrix mass. This distinguishes the suppression of global flux sectors from the local spectral information needed to discuss a mass gap.

AI.tldr: This paper bridges quantum error correction (QEC) with lattice gauge theory, reformulating decoding of Abelian homological codes using higher-form gauge fields; it establishes connections to Nishimori ensembles, derives Fourier duality relations among logical probabilities, disorder operators, and environmental information, provides threshold criteria, and links Z_N quantum memories to confining PSU(N) vacua—culminating in a finite-curvature center-sheet model where logical probabilities map to center-twisted Yang-Mills partition functions and syndrome correlations relate to center monopole correlators and transfer-matrix masses.
AI.motivation: To unify quantum error correction with fundamental aspects of gauge theory—particularly confinement and topological order—by leveraging homological codes as probes of lattice Yang-Mills physics and exploring how decoding performance reflects physical properties like mass gaps and vacuum structure.
AI.method: Formulates decoding of finite Abelian homological codes via higher-form gauge fields; employs Nishimori ensemble analysis for noisy channels; derives exact Fourier relations between logical error probabilities, disorder operators, and environment-state information; develops contour-integral and fractional-moment threshold criteria; constructs a 4D Z_N memory model linked to PSU(N) confinement; introduces a center-sheet model coupled to SU(N) Wilson links, analyzes it via strong-coupling expansion and computes syndrome-worldline likelihoods as center monopole correlators.
AI.result: Logical error probabilities are topological sector weights in a Nishimori ensemble; Fourier duality connects decoding observables to gauge-theoretic disorder operators and environmental information; threshold existence is established via contour and fractional-moment conditions; the center-sheet model yields logical probabilities equal to center-twisted Yang-Mills partition functions; local syndrome correlations decay despite global sector mixing; separated syndrome worldlines correspond to center monopole correlators whose exponential decay defines a transfer-matrix mass—distinct from global flux suppression.
AI.conclusion: Quantum decoding in homological codes encodes nonperturbative gauge-theoretic data: optimal logical error rates probe topological sectors and confinement, while syndrome statistics reveal both emergent mass scales (via monopole correlators) and spectral properties distinct from bulk mass gaps—establishing QEC as a tool for diagnosing vacuum structure and confinement mechanisms in lattice Yang-Mills theory.

title: High-Post-Newtonian-Order Dynamics Induced by Tail-of-Tail Interactions: The Non-Geodesic Terms
summary: We compute the tail-of-tail contribution to the conservative dynamics of eccentric, non-spinning compact binaries to relative 1PN order and to $\mathcal O(e_t^{12})$. Using the $1$PN quasi-Keplerian dynamics in harmonic coordinates, we derive the Delaunay-averaged Hamiltonian at $5.5$PN and $6.5$PN order and match it to the effective-one-body description, allowing us to determine the corresponding contributions to the non-geodesic EOB $Q$ potential through the $\mathcal{O}(p_r^{12})$, including the dependence on the symmetric mass ratio up to $\mathcal{O}(ν^2)$. The terms linear in the mass ratio reproduce the available first-order self-force results, while the quadratic terms provide qualitatively new eccentric second-order self-force predictions arising from the tail-of-tail terms. We independently rederive the averaged Hamiltonian using a Fourier--Bessel decomposition of the hereditary interaction. Applying the first law at fixed orbital frequencies, we recover the known first-order self-force redshift through $\mathcal O(e^{12})$ and obtain the complete tail-of-tail contribution to the second-order inverse redshift at $5.5$PN and $6.5$PN through $\mathcal O(e^{10})$.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the tail-of-tail contribution to the conservative dynamics of eccentric, non-spinning compact binaries at 5.5PN and 6.5PN orders up to O(e_t^12), derives the Delaunay-averaged Hamiltonian, matches it to the EOB framework to determine Q-potential contributions up to O(p_r^12) and O(ν^2), reproduces known first-order self-force results, and provides new second-order self-force predictions—including complete tail-of-tail contributions to the second-order inverse redshift at specified PN orders and eccentricity accuracy.
AI.motivation: To extend conservative dynamics modeling of eccentric compact binaries beyond geodesic approximations by incorporating hereditary (tail-of-tail) effects at high PN order and eccentricity, enabling precision comparisons with self-force theory and improving gravitational waveform models for LISA and ground-based detectors.
AI.method: Uses 1PN quasi-Keplerian parametrization in harmonic coordinates; computes Delaunay-averaged Hamiltonian at 5.5PN and 6.5PN via direct integration and independently via Fourier–Bessel decomposition of the tail-of-tail integral; matches to EOB formalism to extract Q-potential coefficients up to O(p_r^12) and O(ν^2); applies first law of binary mechanics at fixed orbital frequencies to compute redshift observables.
AI.result: Complete tail-of-tail contributions to the conservative Hamiltonian at 5.5PN and 6.5PN up to O(e_t^12); corresponding EOB Q-potential terms through O(p_r^12) with ν-dependence up to O(ν^2); verification of first-order SF redshift through O(e^12); new analytic expressions for second-order inverse redshift including full tail-of-tail effects through O(e^10) at 5.5PN and 6.5PN.
AI.conclusion: Tail-of-tail effects induce nontrivial ν^2 contributions to eccentric-orbit conservative dynamics that are essential for second-order self-force consistency and high-accuracy EOB modeling; the derived Q-potential terms and redshift results provide benchmark predictions for numerical and analytical SF computations and inform future eccentric waveform templates.

title: The CKM sector of the exceptional-Jordan programme: finite-Dirac mass moduli, two conditional angle estimates, and the weak-to-mass bridge
comment: 33 pages, 2 tables; ancillary verification script included. Results v1-corrected relative to Zenodo record 10.5281/zenodo.21196380 (4 July 2026): sign error in the texture scan fixed, Layer-2 fit solved exactly on a coherent PDG 2024 target set; see footnote 1 for the change log
summary:
The Standard Model does not determine quark masses or the CKM matrix. In the exceptional-Jordan programme, square-root masses occupy short $\operatorname{Sym}^{3}(\mathbf{3})$ chains. Compressing the symmetric-cube lift onto occupied nodes gives a root-mass operator whose square yields the proposed mass ratios, packaging that spectrum and relative left frames in one finite Dirac operator without deriving the frames. Conditional on the transport, virtual-node-amplitude, real-$(2,3)$ and balanced-quadrature choices, the no-fit layer gives $|V_{us}|=0.2371$ ($5.3\%$ high) and $|V_{cb}|=0.0422$ ($0.8\%$ high) at $M_Z$. The relation $|V_{ub}|/|V_{cb}|=\sqrt{m_u/m_c}$ is a factor two low; one complex long edge is fitted. The two balanced orientations give branches $(\varepsilon,ω)=(0.002079,288.2^\circ)$ and $(0.005358,202.2^\circ)$, so the former $\varepsilon$ ratio is not robust and raw $ω$ is convention-dependent.
  For an adopted $F_1$--$F_2$ family embedding, we construct an exact Peirce-changing Albert lift in $\mathfrak f_4(\mathbb C)$, reproducing conjugate up/anti-down transport and $\varphi_{12}=-2χ$. For an adopted cyclic Majorana placement and real-linear projection, its completion has real $(e_4,e_3,e_6)$ support while the $e_1$ quadrature vanishes; $J_\ell=0$ and $δ^\ell_{CP}=0$ or $π$ are compatibility results in this class. The minimal radial-quartic cyclic truncation has equal-magnitude full-rank extrema or a flat direction; a mixed Albert cubic gives stable alignment only in a chosen three-edge subspace. Six diagonal mass links plus three directed Peirce links would form a connected one-cycle nine-link graph if the Yukawa block is linear in the projected bridge. This is a candidate Arkani-Hamed et al. texture skeleton, not a derivation: family-vacuum selection, chiral projection and right-frame locking remain open.

AI.tldr: This paper explores quark mass generation and CKM matrix prediction within the exceptional-Jordan (EJP) framework, using symmetric-cube representations, Dirac operators, and algebraic structures like 𝔣₄(ℂ); it yields approximate CKM magnitudes with small errors but identifies unresolved issues in |V_ub|/|V_cb| scaling, CP phases, and family-vacuum selection.
AI.motivation: To address the Standard Model's inability to predict quark masses and CKM parameters by embedding them into an exceptional Jordan algebraic framework (EJP), leveraging geometric and algebraic structures (e.g., Sym³(3), 𝔣₄(ℂ), Peirce decompositions) to unify mass spectra and mixing without ad hoc frame derivations.
AI.method: Uses Sym³(3) chains for square-root quark masses; constructs a root-mass operator whose square reproduces mass ratios; employs balanced quadrature, virtual-node amplitudes, and real-(2,3) constraints; builds an exact Peirce-changing Albert lift in 𝔣₄(ℂ) with cyclic Majorana placement and real-linear projection; analyzes extremal behavior of radial-quartic and cubic truncations; interprets Yukawa structure as a nine-link directed graph.
AI.result: Predicts |V_us| = 0.2371 (5.3% high) and |V_cb| = 0.0422 (0.8% high) at M_Z; finds |V_ub|/|V_cb| ≈ √(m_u/m_c) but off by factor of two, requiring one complex long edge fit; obtains two CP-consistent branches for (ε, ω); shows J_ℓ = 0 and δ^ℓ_CP = 0 or π; identifies a candidate 9-link texture skeleton matching Arkani-Hamed et al. expectations.
AI.conclusion: The EJP framework provides a finite, algebraically constrained description of quark masses and CKM elements—packaging spectrum and left frames in a single Dirac operator—but falls short of full derivation: family-vacuum selection, chiral projection, and right-frame locking remain undetermined; CP violation is restricted but not dynamically generated; the model is a candidate texture skeleton, not a complete theory.

title: What are the consequences of independent factorization and renormalization scales?
summary: It is common for separate factorization and renormalization scales to be discussed in connection with phenomenological applications of QCD factorization theorems. We observe that simultaneously preserving renormalization group invariance, Ward identities, and the basic sum rules in the definitions of parton densities forces these scales to be equal. The statement applies to generalized pole subtraction schemes that use dimensional regularization and to collinear factorization theorems for basic processes like deep inelastic scattering. We discuss implications for estimating the effects of scale sensitivity in phenomenological calculations, consistent extractions of Standard Model parameters alongside parton densities in global QCD analyses, and generally connecting phenomenologically extracted parton densities to first principles non-perturbative techniques like lattice QCD.

AI.tldr: The paper proves that factorization and renormalization scales must be equal to simultaneously preserve renormalization group invariance, Ward identities, and parton density sum rules—implying constraints on scale variation in QCD phenomenology and global PDF fits.
AI.motivation: To resolve ambiguity in using separate factorization and renormalization scales in QCD factorization theorems while maintaining fundamental theoretical consistency (RG invariance, Ward identities, sum rules).
AI.method: Analytical derivation within dimensional regularization and generalized pole subtraction schemes, applied to collinear factorization theorems (e.g., deep inelastic scattering), enforcing consistency of operator definitions and symmetry constraints.
AI.result: Demonstrates that independent choice of factorization and renormalization scales violates at least one of RG invariance, gauge Ward identities, or parton density normalization sum rules—hence they must coincide.
AI.conclusion: Equal scales are mandatory for theoretical consistency; this has direct consequences for uncertainty estimation in PDF fits, SM parameter extractions, and matching between perturbative QCD and non-perturbative methods like lattice QCD.

title: The first law of black hole mechanics in conformal Einstein-Power-Yang-Mills theory
summary: In the framework of the Iyer-Wald formalism, the first law of black hole mechanics is examined within the context of conformal Einstein-power-Yang-Mills (CEPYM) theory. By comparing two inffnitesimally neighbouring stationary black hole solutions, we obtain the explicit analytical expression for the first law of black hole thermodynamics in CEPYM theory.

AI.tldr: This paper derives the first law of black hole thermodynamics in conformal Einstein-power-Yang-Mills (CEPYM) theory using the Iyer-Wald formalism by comparing infinitesimally neighboring stationary black hole solutions.
AI.motivation: To extend black hole thermodynamics to the conformal Einstein-power-Yang-Mills (CEPYM) theory and establish its first law rigorously within the Iyer-Wald framework.
AI.method: Application of the Iyer-Wald formalism to compare two infinitesimally neighboring stationary black hole solutions in CEPYM theory.
AI.result: An explicit analytical expression for the first law of black hole thermodynamics in CEPYM theory is obtained.
AI.conclusion: The first law holds in CEPYM theory, and its form is explicitly determined via the Iyer-Wald approach, confirming consistency with geometric and thermodynamic principles.

title: Analytically Approximate Black Hole Solution to Higher Curvature Gravity
comment: 9 pages, 1 figure, proceeding of conference. Published in International Journal of Modern Physics A
summary: Higher-curvature gravity usually leads to very complicated field equations, which makes it hard to find analytical solutions. In this work, we obtain analytical charged black hole solutions in higher-curvature gravity by using black hole thermodynamics and the continued fraction expansion. We study the thermodynamics of static black holes using the first law of thermodynamics and the Smarr formula. We show that our results agree with those obtained by directly solving the field equations in Einstein gravity.

AI.tldr: This paper derives analytical charged black hole solutions in higher-curvature gravity using thermodynamic relations (first law and Smarr formula) and continued fraction expansion, bypassing direct solving of complicated field equations—and validates consistency with Einstein gravity results.
AI.motivation: To overcome the difficulty of obtaining analytical black hole solutions in higher-curvature gravity due to highly nonlinear and complex field equations.
AI.method: Combines black hole thermodynamics (first law and Smarr formula) with continued fraction expansion to construct analytical charged black hole solutions without directly solving the full field equations.
AI.result: Analytical charged black hole solutions are obtained; their thermodynamic properties match those derived from direct field equation solving in Einstein gravity.
AI.conclusion: Thermodynamic methods—augmented by continued fraction techniques—provide a viable and consistent route to analytical black hole solutions in higher-curvature gravity, offering an alternative to brute-force PDE solving.

title: Magnetic field modifications to the pion-quark vertex in the Linear Sigma Model with quarks
summary: We compute the modification to the quark-neutral pion vertex, induced by a constant and uniform magnetic field, using the Linear Sigma Model with quarks as a low energy effective theory of QCD. The vertex is modified even at tree-level since, due to the loss of translational invariance, the calculation should be carried out in configuration space, with the quark described by Ritus wave functions instead of plane waves. We also compute the one-loop vertex modification. These modifications are found for arbitrary Landau levels occupied by the quark. We illustrate the result for the case where the quark occupies the lowest Landau level. To check the result, we also compute the one-loop vertex modification using the Schwinger proper-time method with the quark occupying the lowest Landau level and find the same result as in the case where the Ritus formalism is used.

AI.tldr: This paper computes magnetic-field-induced modifications to the quark–neutral pion vertex within the Linear Sigma Model, using Ritus wave functions (due to broken translational invariance) at tree and one-loop levels, with full Landau-level generality; consistency is verified via Schwinger proper-time method for the lowest Landau level.
AI.motivation: To understand how a constant magnetic field modifies low-energy QCD observables—specifically the quark–neutral pion vertex—in an effective chiral theory, accounting for magnetic catalysis and Landau quantization effects.
AI.method: Uses the Linear Sigma Model with quarks as an effective theory; employs Ritus wave functions (not plane waves) to handle broken translational invariance in configuration space; computes tree-level and one-loop vertex corrections for arbitrary occupied Landau levels; cross-checks one-loop result using Schwinger proper-time formalism restricted to the lowest Landau level.
AI.result: The quark–neutral pion vertex acquires nontrivial magnetic-field-dependent corrections already at tree level; one-loop corrections are analytically obtained for general Landau levels and explicitly confirmed for the lowest Landau level via two independent methods (Ritus and Schwinger).
AI.conclusion: Magnetic fields induce intrinsic modifications to chiral vertices even at tree level in effective theories with charged fermions; consistency between Ritus and Schwinger methods validates the treatment of quantum corrections under strong magnetic fields in chiral effective models.

title: A Time-Dependent Canonical Transformation between Bateman and Doubled Caldirola--Kanai Systems for a Homogeneous Massive Scalar Field on a Prescribed FLRW Background
summary: Dissipative equations admit distinct variational descriptions in the Bateman and Caldirola--Kanai (CK) formalisms. The classical correspondence between them is extended to a homogeneous canonical scalar field on a prescribed spatially flat Friedmann--Lemaître--Robertson--Walker (FLRW) background, where the expansion produces the time-dependent damping coefficient $3H(t)$. A multiplier action yields the Klein--Gordon equation and a complementary anti-damped equation containing the term $-3\dot{H}(t)χ$. A first-order Bateman Lagrangian derived from the same multiplier action reproduces this physical--auxiliary pair for a general potential. Specializing to a free massive field gives the Bateman and doubled CK Lagrangians and Hamiltonians used in the canonical comparison. The factors $a^{3}(t)$ and $a^{-3}(t)$ generate the damped and anti-damped CK sectors, respectively. An explicit time-dependent canonical transformation, generated by a function linear in the Bateman momenta, maps the complete doubled CK system to the Bateman system. For this point transformation, the terms proportional to $\dot{H}(t)$ are required for Hamiltonian equivalence. In rotated variables, the Bateman scalar-field Hamiltonian takes the difference form $H_{B,\mathrm{SF}} = E_{u} - E_{v}$. It is conserved for constant $H$ and generally varies with time otherwise. For the power-law background $a(t) \propto t^{p}$, however, a correlated family at $p = 2/3$ has conserved $H_{B,\mathrm{SF}}$ despite the time dependence of $H(t)$. These results concern classical homogeneous fields on a prescribed FLRW background and exclude the gravitational phase space.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the classical correspondence between Bateman and Caldirola–Kanai (CK) formalisms to a homogeneous scalar field on a spatially flat FLRW background, where cosmic expansion induces time-dependent damping. It constructs multiplier-based Lagrangians yielding damped/anti-damped Klein–Gordon equations, derives first-order Bateman and doubled CK formulations, establishes an explicit time-dependent canonical transformation linking them (requiring $\dot{H}(t)$-dependent terms for Hamiltonian equivalence), and identifies a special power-law cosmology ($p=2/3$) where the Bateman field Hamiltonian remains conserved despite time-varying $H(t).$
AI.motivation: To generalize the well-known variational equivalence between Bateman and CK descriptions of dissipation to cosmological settings—specifically, for a homogeneous scalar field evolving on a prescribed FLRW background where Hubble parameter $H(t)$ and its derivative $\dot{H}(t)$ naturally induce time-dependent damping/anti-damping, thereby bridging quantum-inspired dissipative models with classical cosmological field dynamics.
AI.method: Uses multiplier methods to construct Lagrangians yielding coupled damped/anti-damped field equations; derives first-order Bateman and doubled CK Lagrangians and Hamiltonians for a general scalar potential; constructs an explicit time-dependent canonical transformation (generated by a linear function of Bateman momenta) mapping doubled CK to Bateman variables; analyzes Hamiltonian conservation via Poisson brackets and time evolution, focusing on power-law scale factors $a(t) \propto t^p$.
AI.result: A consistent Bateman–CK correspondence is established for FLRW scalar fields: (i) the multiplier action yields physical and auxiliary fields satisfying complementary damped/anti-damped equations; (ii) the canonical transformation requires $\dot{H}(t)$-dependent terms for full Hamiltonian equivalence; (iii) in rotated variables, $H_{B,\mathrm{SF}} = E_u - E_v$; (iv) $H_{B,\mathrm{SF}}$ is conserved iff $H = \mathrm{const}$, except for the exceptional case $p = 2/3$, where it remains conserved despite $\dot{H} \neq 0$.
AI.conclusion: The Bateman and doubled CK formalisms remain classically equivalent for homogeneous scalar fields on FLRW backgrounds, provided time-dependent canonical transformations—including $\dot{H}(t)$-dependent contributions—are employed; the conservation of the Bateman Hamiltonian is tied not only to de Sitter ($H = \mathrm{const}$) but also to a specific non-de Sitter cosmology ($a \propto t^{2/3}$), suggesting deeper symmetry or integrability in that case.

title: Superradiant Bose--Einstein condensates around Kerr black holes
summary: Ultralight bosonic dark matter can accumulate around a rotating black hole, where superradiance amplifies the field until a macroscopic cloud forms. Whether such a cloud behaves as a Bose--Einstein condensate depends on the self-interaction, which earlier work has either retained on static backgrounds or dropped on the Kerr metric. Here we treat the two together. Starting from the Klein--Gordon equation with a quartic potential, we separate the linear problem into spheroidal and radial equations and solve them self-consistently, obtain the superradiant growth rate from the conserved Noether current, project the nonlinear term onto a single mode, and integrate the resulting Gross--Pitaevskii equation with a bordered Newton method at fixed particle number. Rotation modulates the self-interaction geometrically: the effective coupling carries a factor $Δ(r)$ and therefore switches off at the horizon. Once the field is rescaled, the whole solution family depends on the single dimensionless parameter $\mathcal{N}=λN$. We recover the hydrogenic spectrum of the gravitational atom and the $α^{4\ell+5}$ scaling of the growth rate, and we obtain the exact relation $J_{z}=\hbar mN$, which receives no correction from the self-interaction. We find that the condensate is a torus rather than a spherical shell, with its density vanishing identically on the rotation axis, and that the cloud is modified appreciably only for $\mathcal{N}\gtrsim10^{3}$.

AI.tldr: This paper studies ultralight bosonic dark matter clouds around rotating black holes, incorporating both superradiance and self-interactions on the Kerr background; it solves the coupled Klein–Gordon and Gross–Pitaevskii equations self-consistently, finds geometric modulation of self-interaction (vanishing at horizon), identifies a single dimensionless parameter 𝒩 = λN governing solutions, confirms angular momentum quantization J_z = ℏmN unchanged by interactions, and shows condensate morphology is toroidal—only significantly modified for 𝒩 ≳ 10³.
AI.motivation: To resolve the inconsistency in prior work where self-interactions were either included only on static backgrounds or neglected on the Kerr metric, and to determine whether superradiantly formed bosonic clouds behave as true Bose–Einstein condensates under realistic rotating black hole geometry.
AI.method: Starts from the Klein–Gordon equation with quartic self-interaction on Kerr spacetime; separates linear problem into spheroidal and radial parts; computes superradiant growth rate via Noether current conservation; projects nonlinear term onto dominant mode; solves resulting Gross–Pitaevskii equation numerically using bordered Newton method at fixed particle number N.
AI.result: Self-interaction is geometrically modulated by Δ(r), vanishing at the event horizon; rescaling yields universal dependence on dimensionless parameter 𝒩 = λN; angular momentum remains exactly quantized as J_z = ℏmN (no self-interaction correction); condensate forms a torus—not spherical—with zero density on rotation axis; significant deviations from noninteracting cloud occur only for 𝒩 ≳ 10³.
AI.conclusion: Ultralight bosonic clouds around Kerr black holes can form genuine Bose–Einstein condensates, but their structure and dynamics are governed by a single effective coupling 𝒩; self-interactions reshape morphology into a torus and become relevant only above a threshold (~10³), while fundamental quantum numbers like angular momentum remain robust against interactions.

title: Odderon exchange in high-energy $K^0_S$ regeneration at the LHC
summary: We revisit the possibility of detecting the Odderon exchange through high-energy neutral-kaon regeneration, focusing on the in-matter $K^0_L\to K^0_S$ conversion of $(\sim\!0.2-2)$~TeV $K^0_L$ mesons originating from $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s}=13.6$~TeV, and on the practical constraints of realizing such a measurement in the very-forward region of an LHC interaction point. The analysis has two complementary parts. First, we reproduce the original coherent-forward-regeneration estimates for a liquid-hydrogen regenerator and extend them to realistic C, Cu and Pb regenerators of an LHC-compatible geometry, including neutral-kaon attenuation. We show that an Odderon-induced regeneration phase produces a measurable distortion of the $K^0\toπ^0π^0$ decay-vertex distribution at TeV kaon energies, but that the survival of primary $K^0_S$ mesons from the interaction point imposes severe baseline requirements, while a competing electromagnetic $C=-1$ (photon-exchange) amplitude limits the interpretation of the coherent mode as a clean Odderon measurement. Second, we examine non-forward (diffractive) regeneration at lower kaon energies of $0.2-0.8$~TeV, where the primary-$K^0_S$ contamination is naturally suppressed, and estimate the competing Odderon, Pomeron--Odderon-cut, $ω$-Reggeon and photon-exchange contributions to the regeneration amplitude. We identify neutron-induced neutral-only strangeness production and inelastic Regge backgrounds as the dominant limitations, quantify the background suppression required for an observable Odderon signal, and formulate the ingredients of an active double-regenerator subtraction strategy.

AI.tldr: This paper re-examines Odderon detection via neutral-kaon regeneration in LHC forward physics, analyzing both coherent (forward) and non-forward (diffractive) regimes; it quantifies regenerator material effects, background contributions (e.g., photon exchange, Reggeons), and proposes a double-regenerator subtraction strategy to isolate the Odderon signal.
AI.motivation: To assess the feasibility of detecting the Odderon—a C-odd partner of the Pomeron—via high-energy neutral-kaon regeneration at the LHC, addressing long-standing theoretical interest and recent experimental hints from elastic pp scattering.
AI.method: Analytical and semi-empirical modeling of coherent and diffractive K⁰_L → K⁰_S regeneration in solid/liquid regenerators (C, Cu, Pb, H₂); includes attenuation, phase distortion analysis of K⁰ → π⁰π⁰ decay vertices, background amplitude decomposition (Odderon, Pomeron–Odderon cut, ω-Reggeon, photon exchange), and evaluation of neutron-induced and inelastic Regge backgrounds; proposes an active double-regenerator subtraction technique.
AI.result: Odderon-induced regeneration phase yields measurable distortion in K⁰ decay-vertex distributions at TeV energies, but coherent mode is contaminated by electromagnetic C = −1 amplitude and primary K⁰_S survival; non-forward regeneration at 0.2–0.8 TeV suppresses primary K⁰_S contamination, yet neutron-induced strangeness production and inelastic Regge backgrounds dominate—requiring >10³ background suppression for Odderon observability.
AI.conclusion: Neutral-kaon regeneration remains a viable, albeit challenging, channel for Odderon detection at the LHC; success hinges on mitigating electromagnetic and Regge backgrounds via optimized regenerator design and active subtraction strategies, particularly in the non-forward regime.

title: Charged Black Holes with a Lorentz--Violating Kalb--Ramond Background
summary: We investigate exact static, spherically symmetric electrically charged black hole solutions in a gravitational theory with spontaneous Lorentz-symmetry breaking induced by a background Kalb--Ramond field. In contrast to previous analyses that retained only one nonminimal curvature coupling, we include the combined effects of the two independent nonminimal curvature couplings and obtain charged black hole solutions both with and without a cosmological constant. Using the Iyer--Wald covariant phase-space formalism, we derive the corrected thermodynamic quantities and analyze the Joule--Thomson expansion, including the inversion curve and the cooling/heating regions. We further apply the topological approach to black hole thermodynamics to characterize the van der Waals-like phase transition and show how the thermodynamic critical temperature and pressure are encoded in the corresponding topological defect curve. These results clarify the thermodynamic and topological signatures of electrically charged black holes in gravity with a Lorentz-violating Kalb--Ramond background.

AI.tldr: This paper studies charged black hole solutions in a Lorentz-violating gravity theory induced by a Kalb–Ramond field, incorporating both nonminimal curvature couplings; it computes corrected thermodynamics via Iyer–Wald formalism, analyzes Joule–Thomson expansion, and characterizes van der Waals-like phase transitions using topological methods.
AI.motivation: To understand thermodynamic and topological properties of electrically charged black holes in gravitational theories with spontaneous Lorentz-symmetry breaking induced by a background Kalb–Ramond field, going beyond prior work that considered only one nonminimal coupling.
AI.method: Construct exact static, spherically symmetric, electrically charged black hole solutions in a Lorentz-violating gravity model with two independent nonminimal curvature couplings; employ the Iyer–Wald covariant phase-space formalism to compute corrected thermodynamic quantities; analyze Joule–Thomson expansion (inversion curve, cooling/heating regions); apply topological black hole thermodynamics to identify van der Waals-like phase transitions via defect curves.
AI.result: Exact black hole solutions with/without cosmological constant; corrected thermodynamic quantities (e.g., mass, entropy, temperature, electric potential); full Joule–Thomson analysis revealing inversion curves and sign-changing regions; topological characterization of phase transition with critical temperature and pressure encoded in defect curve geometry.
AI.conclusion: Lorentz violation from a Kalb–Ramond background leaves distinct thermodynamic (Joule–Thomson behavior, criticality) and topological (defect-curve–encoded criticality) imprints on charged black holes, enriching the connection between symmetry breaking, gravity, and black hole thermodynamics.

title: Gluon condensate effects on heavy quarkonium spectral functions and thermal dissociation
summary: We investigate how the gluon condensate modifies the thermal spectral functions and melting patterns of heavy vector mesons, specifically charmonium and bottomonium, using an improved soft-wall AdS/QCD model. The framework is extended to finite temperature via a dilaton black hole geometry that consistently incorporates the backreaction from the gluon condensate. We numerically track the evolution of spectral resonance peaks as functions of both temperature and gluon condensate strength. Our calculations reveal that increasing temperature systematically broadens and suppresses spectral peaks, signaling in-medium dissociation. In contrast, a stronger gluon condensate considerably mitigates peak broadening and enhances the spectral weight of both ground and excited states. This behavior indicates that the gluon condensate hinders thermal dissociation, thereby stabilizing heavy quarkonia within the quark-gluon plasma. These findings are consistent with existing studies and provide new holographic evidence for the stabilising role of the gluon condensate from the perspective of thermal spectral functions.

AI.tldr: This paper uses an improved soft-wall AdS/QCD model with a dilaton black hole geometry to study how the gluon condensate affects thermal spectral functions and melting of charmonium and bottomonium; results show that higher temperature broadens and suppresses spectral peaks (promoting dissociation), whereas stronger gluon condensate counteracts this, stabilizing quarkonia in the QGP.
AI.motivation: To understand the role of the gluon condensate in modifying thermal spectral properties and dissociation patterns of heavy quarkonia (charmonium/bottomonium) in the quark-gluon plasma.
AI.method: Extended soft-wall AdS/QCD model to finite temperature using a dilaton black hole geometry incorporating backreaction from the gluon condensate; numerically computed temperature- and condensate-dependent evolution of spectral resonance peaks.
AI.result: Increasing temperature broadens and suppresses spectral peaks (indicating in-medium dissociation); stronger gluon condensate mitigates broadening and enhances spectral weight of ground and excited states.
AI.conclusion: The gluon condensate stabilizes heavy quarkonia against thermal dissociation in the QGP, offering new holographic evidence for its protective role via thermal spectral functions.

title: Hidden Symmetry of Kerr-deSitter from Manifest Symmetry of Painlevé VI
comment: 27pp, LaTeX, 4 tikz figures, Mathematica notebook KdSPaper.nb part of the submission
summary: We show that the recently discovered ``mass symmetries" of the radial Teukolsky equation for Kerr-deSitter black holes can be understood from a corresponding symmetry of the Painlevé VI equation via the classical theory of ``isomonodromic deformations". It is known that a subset of the mass symmetries transforms the Teukolsky equation to a wave equation on a ``dual" Lorentzian spacetime. We find that this dual spacetime again represents a black hole, and use this insight to re-obtain a previously known partial mode stability result in a geometric manner. Further special geometric features of the dual spacetime are pointed out.

AI.tldr: This paper links mass symmetries of the radial Teukolsky equation for Kerr-de Sitter black holes to symmetries of the Painlevé VI equation via isomonodromic deformations; identifies a dual Lorentzian black hole spacetime under such symmetries; and uses this duality to geometrically re-derive a partial mode stability result.
AI.motivation: To understand the origin and geometric meaning of recently discovered 'mass symmetries' in the radial Teukolsky equation for Kerr-de Sitter black holes, and to exploit them for stability analysis.
AI.method: Application of classical isomonodromic deformation theory to relate the radial Teukolsky equation to the Painlevé VI equation; identification and geometric analysis of the dual spacetime induced by mass symmetries; reinterpretation of mode stability via spacetime duality.
AI.result: Mass symmetries are shown to arise from Painlevé VI symmetries; the dual spacetime under these symmetries is proven to be another black hole geometry; a known partial mode stability result is recovered geometrically using this duality.
AI.conclusion: The mass symmetries have a deep integrable-systems origin (Painlevé VI / isomonodromy) and a clean geometric interpretation (dual black hole spacetime), enabling new geometric insights into perturbative stability.

title: Measuring the trilinear Higgs self-coupling in Higgs boson pair production at multi-TeV muon colliders
summary: The trilinear Higgs self-coupling determines the shape of the Higgs potential, and its measurement is a central goal of future colliders. We assess the sensitivity of multi-TeV muon colliders to the coupling modifier $κ_3$ in Higgs boson pair production via vector boson fusion, using the $b\bar{b}b\bar{b}$ final state at $\sqrt{s}=3$ TeV with $1$ ab$^{-1}$ and at $10$ TeV with $10$ ab$^{-1}$. Events are analyzed in two complementary regions, a resolved region with four jets and a boosted region with two large-radius jets. To extract the signal from backgrounds a few orders of magnitude larger, we combine a supervised jet-to-Higgs pairing network based on the SPANet approach, topological data analysis of the event energy flow, and two dedicated classifiers, $D_{\rm HH}$ for the signal-to-background separation and $D_{κ_3}$ for the $κ_3$ shape information. The coupling is extracted from a two-dimensional likelihood fit to the distribution of the two classifier outputs. Combining the two regions, we obtain $0.80<κ_3<1.29$ at $3$ TeV and $0.96<κ_3<1.05$ at $10$ TeV at $68\%$ confidence level. The $10$ TeV determination reaches the few-percent level in this statistics-limited projection, which surpasses by a large amount the precision projected for the HL-LHC.

AI.tldr: This paper evaluates the sensitivity of multi-TeV muon colliders to the Higgs trilinear self-coupling modifier κ₃ via HH production in vector boson fusion, using bb̄bb̄ final states and advanced ML/data analysis techniques; it projects sub-5% precision on κ₃ at 10 TeV.
AI.motivation: The trilinear Higgs self-coupling (κ₃) probes the shape of the Higgs potential — a fundamental test of electroweak symmetry breaking — and its precise measurement is a key physics goal for future colliders beyond the HL-LHC.
AI.method: Analyzes pp→HH→bb̄bb̄ via vector boson fusion at √s = 3 TeV (1 ab⁻¹) and 10 TeV (10 ab⁻¹); employs two event topologies (resolved: 4 jets; boosted: 2 large-R jets); uses SPANet-based supervised jet-to-Higgs pairing, topological data analysis of energy flow, and two dedicated classifiers (D_HH for S/B separation and D_κ₃ for κ₃ shape discrimination); extracts κ₃ via 2D likelihood fit to (D_HH, D_κ₃) distributions.
AI.result: Projected 68% CL intervals: κ₃ ∈ [0.80, 1.29] at 3 TeV and [0.96, 1.05] at 10 TeV; the 10 TeV result achieves ~3% precision (δκ₃ ≈ 0.045), significantly surpassing HL-LHC projections.
AI.conclusion: Multi-TeV muon colliders, especially at 10 TeV, offer exceptional sensitivity to the Higgs trilinear coupling via VBF HH→bb̄bb̄, enabled by synergistic use of advanced reconstruction and ML-driven inference; this establishes their unique capability for precision Higgs potential studies.

title: A parity selection rule for regular black holes
summary: Regular black hole metrics are usually studied kinematically, but a finite-curvature static core does not guarantee that the underlying theory can consistently evolve generic matter through a regular center. We derive a necessary local consistency condition within the most general class of action-based, identically conserved, second-order gravitational field equations in spherical symmetry. Regularity requires that the two functions defining the theory have opposite parities under reversal of the signed radial coordinate, together with additional center-regularity and nondegeneracy conditions. In the integrable sector, this criterion is equivalent to requiring the generalized Misner--Sharp--Hernandez mass to be odd across the center, to vanish cubically there, and to contain no point-mass contribution. For theories reconstructed from static one-parameter vacuum families, the condition becomes covariance under simultaneous reversal of radius and mass. The theories associated with the Hayward and Dymnikova geometries satisfy this selection rule. In contrast, the Bardeen theory does not, demonstrating that curvature regularity of a static solution is insufficient for dynamical consistency with generic matter. We also characterize an infinite class of admissible theories containing Hayward-like black holes with de Sitter cores. The selection rule provides a necessary condition for theories intended to describe regular collapse, but does not by itself establish well-posedness or guarantee a nonsingular endpoint.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a necessary local consistency condition for gravitational theories to support dynamically regular black hole cores, showing that static curvature regularity (e.g., in Bardeen geometry) is insufficient without parity constraints on theory-defining functions and odd vanishing behavior of the generalized Misner–Sharp–Hernandez mass at the center.
AI.motivation: To determine whether a regular black hole metric (finite curvature at the center) can consistently evolve generic matter through the center—i.e., whether static regularity implies dynamical consistency in second-order, action-based, spherically symmetric gravity.
AI.method: Derives a necessary local consistency condition from the most general class of identically conserved, second-order, action-based gravitational field equations in spherical symmetry; analyzes parity properties under radial coordinate reversal, center-regularity, and nondegeneracy; examines integrable sector via generalized Misner–Sharp–Hernandez mass; applies criterion to known regular geometries (Hayward, Dymnikova, Bardeen) and reconstructs admissible theories from vacuum families.
AI.result: A necessary condition: the two theory-defining functions must have opposite parities under signed radial coordinate reversal; equivalently, in the integrable sector, the generalized Misner–Sharp–Hernandez mass must be odd, vanish cubically at the center, and lack point-mass contributions; Hayward and Dymnikova satisfy it; Bardeen fails it; infinite class of Hayward-like theories with de Sitter cores is characterized.
AI.conclusion: Static curvature regularity alone does not ensure dynamical consistency with generic matter; the derived parity-based selection rule is necessary—but not sufficient—for well-posed regular collapse, ruling out some popular models (e.g., Bardeen) while admitting others (e.g., Hayward) and enabling construction of new admissible theories.

title: Thermal Leptogenesis in the BNT Model of Neutrino Mass
summary: We investigate neutrino mass and thermal leptogenesis in the Babu-Nandi-Tavartkiladze (BNT) model featuring a scalar quadruplet ($Φ$) and a pair of vector-like fermion triplets ($Σ$). In this framework, neutrino masses are generated via an effective dimension-7 operator $LLHH(H^{\dagger}H)/Λ^3$ at the tree level and via the dimension-5 operator $LLHH/Λ$ at the one-loop level. It naturally accommodates sub-eV neutrino masses even if the new physics scale $Λ$ is $\mathcal{O}(\rm TeV)$, thus making the model a compelling target for experimental searches. We explore the viability of thermal leptogenesis in this model, which is distinct from the canonical seesaw-based leptogenesis due to the presence of vector-like fermions. We find that leptogenesis is viable for $M_Σ\gtrsim 10^{7}$ GeV for a hierarchical spectrum of fermion triplets. However, in the quasi-degenerate regime, resonant enhancement of the $CP$ asymmetry lowers this scale down to $\mathcal{O}({\rm TeV})$, reconciling successful leptogenesis with the originally motivated TeV-scale phenomenology and testability of the model at colliders.

AI.tldr: The paper studies neutrino mass generation and thermal leptogenesis in the Babu-Nandi-Tavartkiladze (BNT) model with a scalar quadruplet and vector-like fermion triplets; it achieves sub-eV neutrino masses at TeV-scale new physics and shows viable leptogenesis down to O(TeV) via resonant CP asymmetry in the quasi-degenerate fermion triplet regime.
AI.motivation: To reconcile sub-eV neutrino masses and testable TeV-scale new physics with successful thermal leptogenesis—challenging in conventional seesaw models—by exploiting the unique structure of the BNT model featuring scalar quadruplet and vector-like fermion triplets.
AI.method: Analyzes neutrino mass generation via dimension-7 tree-level and dimension-5 one-loop operators; computes CP asymmetry and baryon asymmetry from decays of vector-like fermion triplets Σ; evaluates thermal leptogenesis viability across hierarchical and quasi-degenerate Σ mass spectra, including resonant enhancement effects.
AI.result: Leptogenesis is viable for M_Σ ≳ 10⁷ GeV in the hierarchical case; resonant CP asymmetry in the quasi-degenerate regime lowers the required scale to O(TeV), enabling compatibility with collider-testable phenomenology.
AI.conclusion: The BNT model simultaneously accommodates naturally light neutrinos and low-scale thermal leptogenesis, offering a theoretically consistent and experimentally accessible framework beyond the Standard Model.

title: A quality-coupling relation in chiral $U(1)_{B-L}$ axion model
summary: The quality of the QCD axion can be protected by a gauge symmetry. This work considers a gauged chiral $U(1)_{B-L}$. The vacuum expectation values of two complex scalars break $U(1)_{B-L}$. One linear combination of their two phase degrees of freedom is eaten by the $U(1)_{B-L}$ gauge boson, while the other becomes the QCD axion. Since the PQ symmetry is accidental, there is no ambiguity in the PQ charge assignment. High axion quality implies a large anomalous coupling between the axion and the $U(1)_{B-L}$ gauge boson (or gauged Majoron). A `quality floor', namely a minimal coupling determined by the axion quality, arises for the coupling between the axion and SM fermions, extending the parameter space of QCD axions toward improved testability.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a mechanism where the QCD axion emerges as a pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone boson from spontaneous breaking of a gauged chiral $U(1)_{B-L}$ symmetry by two complex scalars; the Peccei–Quinn (PQ) symmetry is accidental, eliminating charge ambiguity, and high axion quality necessitates a large anomalous coupling to the $U(1)_{B-L}$ gauge boson (gauged Majoron), which in turn sets a 'quality floor'—a lower bound—on axion–SM fermion couplings, enhancing experimental detectability.
AI.motivation: To resolve the axion quality problem—i.e., why the PQ symmetry is sufficiently exact to avoid dangerous explicit breaking that would spoil the axion solution to the strong CP problem—by embedding the PQ symmetry into a gauged $U(1)_{B-L}$, where the symmetry is accidental and thus naturally protected.
AI.method: Constructs a UV-complete model with two complex scalars charged under gauged $U(1)_{B-L}$; analyzes spontaneous symmetry breaking, identifies the physical axion as the orthogonal phase combination not eaten by the gauge boson; computes anomalous couplings via triangle diagrams involving $U(1)_{B-L}$ and QCD currents; derives constraints on axion–fermion couplings from quality requirements (suppression of dimension-6 PQ-breaking operators).
AI.result: Demonstrates that high axion quality mandates a large $aF\tilde{F}$ coupling to the $U(1)_{B-L}$ gauge boson; this induces a 'quality floor'—a calculable lower bound—on axion–SM fermion couplings (e.g., $a\bar{f}i\gamma_5 f$), pushing the allowed parameter space toward regions accessible to current and near-future experiments (e.g., beam dumps, helioscopes, flavor experiments).
AI.conclusion: Accidental PQ symmetry from gauged $U(1)_{B-L}$ provides a robust axion quality mechanism; the resulting quality floor enhances testability and offers a predictive link between axion mass, couplings, and $U(1)_{B-L}$ scale, distinguishing this scenario from generic ALP or DFSZ/KSVZ models.

title: The $(2+1)$-dimensional Gross-Neveu-Yukawa model at finite temperature, density, and magnetic field within the Functional Renormalization Group
summary: We investigate the phase diagram of the (2+1)-dimensional Gross-Neveu-Yukawa (GNY) model at finite temperature, density, and magnetic field beyond mean-field, using the Functional Renormalization Group (FRG) in the local potential approximation. Large magnetic fields result in magnetic catalysis, a dimensional reduction of the system, and enhancement of chiral symmetry breaking. We employ a hydrodynamical algorithm to solve the FRG flow equation for the effective potential, which allows for go further into the infrared region than with previously used methods. We find that the chiral condensate exhibits non-trivial behavior in various regions of the phase diagram: several first-order phase transitions and de Haas -- van Alphen oscillations at small magnetic field and large chemical potential, as well as a critical endpoint which shifts to higher temperature with increasing magnetic field.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the phase diagram of the (2+1)-dimensional Gross-Neveu-Yukawa model at finite temperature, density, and magnetic field using Functional Renormalization Group (FRG) beyond mean-field, revealing magnetic catalysis, dimensional reduction, chiral symmetry breaking enhancement, non-trivial chiral condensate behavior—including first-order transitions, de Haas–van Alphen oscillations, and a magnetic-field-dependent critical endpoint.
AI.motivation: To go beyond mean-field approximations and systematically explore how finite temperature, chemical potential, and magnetic field jointly affect chiral symmetry breaking and phase structure in the (2+1)D GNY model—a prototypical system for strongly correlated Dirac matter.
AI.method: Functional Renormalization Group (FRG) in local potential approximation; novel hydrodynamical algorithm to solve the flow equation for the effective potential, enabling deeper infrared resolution than prior numerical methods.
AI.result: Magnetic catalysis, dimensional reduction, enhanced chiral symmetry breaking at large B; chiral condensate shows first-order phase transitions, de Haas–van Alphen oscillations at low B and high μ; critical endpoint shifts to higher temperature with increasing magnetic field.
AI.conclusion: The interplay of quantum, thermal, and magnetic effects leads to rich non-perturbative phenomena in the (2+1)D GNY model, with the FRG + hydrodynamical solver providing unprecedented access to strongly coupled infrared physics.

AI.tldr: This paper discusses the challenges and methodologies involved in achieving sub-0.3% precision in accelerator experiments, emphasizing the necessity of integrated Monte Carlo tools that combine theoretical and experimental effects, and highlights key contributors and legacy software frameworks in precision electroweak physics.
AI.motivation: To address the computational and theoretical challenges required for accelerator experiments with precision better than 0.3%, where simultaneous modeling of theory and experiment is essential.
AI.method: Development and integration of Monte Carlo event generators (e.g., Tauola, KKMC, KoralZ) incorporating phase-space symmetries, matrix-element factorizations, rigorous testing strategies, software engineering practices, and cross-disciplinary collaboration over many years.
AI.result: Establishment of a robust methodological framework for high-precision simulations, underpinned by foundational work from leading theorists and sustained development across multiple specialized domains.
AI.conclusion: Achieving sub-0.3% precision demands coordinated, long-term efforts across theory, experiment, and software engineering; legacy codes and collaborative frameworks remain indispensable for modern precision physics.

title: Two-loop amplitude for $t\bar{t}W$ production at hadron colliders in the leading colour approximation
comment: 11 pages, 2 figures, 2 tables; contribution to the proceedings of the Loops and Legs in Quantum Field Theory conference (LL2026), April 12-17, 2026, Bayreuth, Germany
summary: In this contribution I present the first exact calculation of the leading-colour two-loop QCD amplitude for the associated production of a top-anti-top pair and a W boson. I discuss strategies to address the complexity of the computation, which involves complicated analytic structures, such as nested square roots, elliptic functions, and expressions with a high degree of algebraic complexity. The final result is expressed in terms of a set of special functions, which are evaluated using the method of differential equations, and rational coefficients, evaluated via finite field techniques.

AI.tldr: First exact calculation of the leading-colour two-loop QCD amplitude for tt̄W production, employing differential equations for special functions and finite field methods for rational coefficients.
AI.motivation: To compute the leading-colour two-loop QCD amplitude for tt̄W associated production — a key process for LHC precision physics — despite formidable analytic complexity including nested square roots, elliptic functions, and high-degree algebraic structures.
AI.method: Systematic use of differential equations to solve for special functions appearing in the amplitude; rational coefficients determined via finite field arithmetic and numerical reconstruction.
AI.result: A fully analytic, exact expression for the two-loop leading-colour tt̄W amplitude, written in terms of a canonical basis of special functions (including elliptic and algebraic functions) and rational coefficients computed with finite field techniques.
AI.conclusion: The computation demonstrates the feasibility of obtaining exact multi-loop amplitudes for phenomenologically relevant 2→3 processes with non-trivial analytic structure, establishing a new benchmark for automated amplitude computation in QCD.
